news.Title: 微軟、Alphabet、亞馬遜本週財報登場！AI資本支出、雲端訂單成股價關鍵
news.Content: 美股財報季持續升溫，本週市場焦點轉向「科技七巨頭」，其中微軟( MSFT-US ) 、Google母公司Alphabet( GOOGL-US ) 及亞馬遜( AMZN-US ) 將陸續公布季度財報。隨著市場關注大型科技企業的人工智慧（AI）資本支出、雲端業務成長及資料中心建置進度，三大巨頭的財報與展望，預料將牽動主要股價指數及相關ETF表現。 根據《Benzinga》報導，Benzinga Pro彙整的分析師預估，微軟與Alphabet本季營收及每股盈餘（EPS）均可望較去年同期成長，亞馬遜營收也預期維持雙位數成長。 不過，在AI投資規模持續擴大的背景下，市場除了檢視財報是否優於預期，也將評估雲端訂單能否隨著運算產能擴張，順利轉化為實際營收。 微軟、Alphabet、亞馬遜財報預估一次看 三家公司均將於美股收盤後公布財報。微軟將於週三（28日）公布第一季財報，Alphabet同日公布第三季財報，亞馬遜則於週四（29日）公布第三季財報。 分析師預估，微軟每股盈餘將達4.72美元，高於去年同期的4.13美元；營收預估為906.8億美元，也高於去年同期的776.7億美元。微軟已連續超過10季繳出優於分析師預期的成績。 Alphabet方面，每股盈餘預估為3.02美元，高於去年同期的2.87美元；營收預估達1,281.8億美元，較去年同期的1,023.5億美元成長。Alphabet同樣已連續超過10季營收及每股盈餘優於市場預期。 亞馬遜每股盈餘預估為1.96美元，略高於去年同期的1.95美元；營收預估達2,022.4億美元，高於去年同期的1,801.7億美元。亞馬遜營收已連續8季超越分析師預期，過去10季有9季表現優於預期；每股盈餘則連續2季優於預期，過去10季同樣有9季超標。 AI資本支出與雲端訂單成關鍵 分析師Dan Ives指出，市場對新興雲端服務商（neocloud）的融資能力，以及大型科技企業資本支出規模的疑慮，正為科技七巨頭股價帶來壓力。 不過，他預估，美國未來幾年還將興建800至1,000座資料中心，並看好微軟、亞馬遜與Alphabet等超大規模雲端服務商在這波產業變革中的發展機會。

news.Title: Bull of the Day: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM)
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM is one of, if not the most important companies in the world, making it a nearly surefire long-term investment in artificial intelligence and technology in general.

Taiwan Semi, or TSMC, physically manufactures the most cutting-edge semiconductors fueling the artificial intelligence boom and the wider tech-driven economy.

The chip builder reported a strong beat-and-raise Q3 on October 15, confirming that the AI capex spending spree remains full-steam ahead even as bubble concerns ramp up. The chart below showcases Taiwan Semi's impressive earnings expansion, including ~400% growth between 2019 and 2025.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

TSMC's Q4 earnings estimate surged ~12% since its mid-month release, while its FY27 estimate jumped significantly as well to help it earn a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Its robust guidance is supported by "continued strong demand" for its "leading-edge process technologies, including the steep ramp-up of our 2-nanometer technology."

The stock, which nearly quadrupled the Tech sector over the last 15 years and tripled it over the past five, is down ~12% from its recent peaks.

TSMC is on the verge of a possible technical breakout, and it is trading at a 43% discount to its highs and in line with its 10-year median at 19.5X forward earnings.

TSMC: Is This the Best Tech Stock to Buy Now and Hold Forever?

AI and the global economy rely, directly or indirectly, on semiconductors. More importantly, TSMC likely manufactured a large share of the chips fueling the AI boom and beyond, since the chip builder reportedly captures 60% of the foundry market and 90% of advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

The company on a tiny island doesn't design or sell its own semiconductors. Instead, TSMC was founded in the late 1980s on a simple, yet revolutionary "pure-play foundry" model, dedicated exclusively to manufacturing advanced semiconductors for other tech companies.

Taiwan Semi has built an almost unbreachable fortress around its leading-edge chip-building business by earning the trust of customers such as Nvidia (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), AMD, Qualcomm, and other tech titans.

Nvidia, Apple, and others rely on TSMC because of its unmatched scale and expertise. Plus, their CEOs know that Taiwan Semi is their partner, not a competitor. The company is also critically rushing to expand its global manufacturing operation outside of Taiwan into the U.S., Japan, and beyond to address one of its only potential shortfalls: geopolitics.

Story Continues

What AI Bubble? Buy Taiwan Semi Stock for AI-Boosted Growth

Wall Street is still waiting for Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia, and many other tech firms to report third-quarter earnings. But TSMC already confirmed that the AI capital spending boom is ramping up.

TSM grew its Q3 earnings by 58% on 41% higher revenue. The chip builder said that 3- nanometer shipments accounted for 33% of its total wafer revenue, up from 23% in the year-ago period. Plus, its most advanced 2-nm chips accounted for 8%, up from 3% in the second quarter (first time 2-nm shipments were broken out in its earnings release).

TSMC's Q4 earnings estimate surged 12% since its Q3 release on October 15, with its fiscal 2027 estimate 6% higher. The recent positivity extends its impressive run of upward earnings revisions, and its most accurate estimates for FY26 and FY27 came in above consensus. The tech giant's overall upbeat earnings revisions land it a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) right now.

The leading chip builder said at the start of 2026 that it expects to grow its revenue by a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of ~25% between 2024 and 2029.

TSMC is projected to grow its revenue by 41% in 2026 and another 33% next year to reach $229 billion, adding more than $100 billion vs. 2025's $122 billion total and more than tripling its 2023 figure.

On the bottom line, it's projected to grow its earnings by 60% in 2026 and 32% next year, more than doubling its 2025 total ($10.65) in the process ($22.44 a share in 2027). TSMC's robust guidance is supported by "continued strong demand" for its "leading-edge process technologies, including the steep ramp-up of our 2-nanometer technology."

On top of that, Taiwan Semi has topped our quarterly earnings estimates for five years running.

Buy This Top-Ranked Tech Stock Now for Value and Breakout Potential?

Taiwan Semi stock soared ~3,300% in the last 15 years to blow away Tech's ~870%. More recently, TSM stock outclimbed the entire Mag 7 over the last year, up ~44%.

The chip builder is nearly neck-and-neck with Nvidia over the last three years, skyrocketing ~400%, while leaving the rest of the Mag 7 in the dust.

TSM is down roughly 12% from its October 5 records, and its average Zacks price target implies 27% upside from Monday's levels.

Some of its drop can be attributed to the laws of market gravity. The stock reached heavily overbought RSI levels to start October. TSM stock is attempting to retake its 50-day and its long-term 21-week moving averages.

The pullback, coupled with its strong earnings growth outlook, has TSMC trading at a 43% discount to its highs at 19.5X forward 12-month earnings.

The chip builder is also trading almost directly in line with the Tech sector, the S&P 500, and TSMC's 10-year median, even though it has climbed ~1,300% in the past decade vs. the Zacks Tech sector's ~470%.

On top of all that, TSMC's balance sheet is robust and supports its various expansion efforts. And 16 of the 19 brokerage recommendations that Zacks has are "Strong Buys."

Disclosure: Ben Rains owns TSM stock in his personal portfolio.

news.Title: Nvidia to commit $3 bln to Meta share offering as part of bigger AI partnership
news.Content:
Investing.com-- Nvidia said on Tuesday it will invest $3 billion in a recent equity offering by Meta Platforms, as part of an expanded partnership focusing on the Instagram owner's Muse line of artificial intelligence models. The move follows Meta's announcement that it plans to raise $95 billion to fund its AI infrastructure buildout.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The two companies said in a joint statement they will collaborate on improving inference and training performance in Meta's Muse models.

Meta said it plans to expand the deployment of Nvidia infrastructure in its data centers, including using Vera Rubin and Vera CPUs to power its AI agents. The company will also deploy Nvidia's network technology.

"We see the Meta equity financing helping remove part of the equity overhang," Mizuho analyst Lloyd Walmsley said in a note. "Investors feared they would have to wait until the Class C shares were established in Jan '27. The pull-forward helps."

The collaboration comes after Meta's Muse AI models, specifically its Muse agents, were positively received by users, with the Muse agent application becoming one of the most downloaded apps within a week of its launch.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

"NVIDIA and Meta are expanding our partnership to optimize the computing infrastructure end to end for capable, efficient and secure AI agents," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement.

Separately, Meta said it had upsized an offering of common stock to $25 billion from $22.5 billion. The offering, coupled with a depository share offering, will now raise up to $37.5 billion.

Meta said it had also priced the offerings at $625 a share for the common stock issuance and $50 per share for the depository share offering.

The capital raise is aimed chiefly at funding the instagram owner's AI infrastructure buildout. The company had on Monday said it was also planning a separate $60 billion non-voting share offering in 2027.

Wells Fargo analysts said Meta's equity raise "likely fulfills our expectation of a financing gap of $60-$80B for FY27." They see the size and structure of the common, preferred and at-the-market offerings of Class C shares as "sufficient to fulfill funding needs in '27."

The analysts expect the AI investment cycle to persist well beyond 2027, so future equity or debt offerings remain possible, but likely only with "greater visibility on Muse adoption/monetization and AI demand." In their view, the raise "removes the financing dependence upon an increasingly volatile credit market."

Vahid Karaahmetovic contributed to this report.

news.Title: Peter Thiel's Apple verdict raises a $5 trillion question
news.Content: Having recently bought my wife a new iPhone 16+, I can't help but think about its lofty price tag and what it's really all about. Sure, the camera might have gotten sharper (switching from 14+), the battery might have lasted longer, and the screen might have looked better. But if I put the two phones side by side, I don't really think either felt like a tech revolution or even a major upgrade over something my wife already owned. That's the question PayPal co-founder Peter Thiel just raised about Apple ( AAPL ). In a recent interview with Walter Isaacson, Thiel said that the company has done little genuinely new since Steve Jobs died in 2011. Though the business is brilliantly run, Thiel said the breakthroughs have become tougher to spot. The criticism comes at a point when Apple is spending billions on research and development, while its market value has surged into the trillions. For anyone holding Apple stock, the question isn't whether the iPhone remains popular. It's whether Apple's next big idea can justify the premium Wall Street is willing to pay. Peter Thiel says Apple became better at profits than invention In a recent interview with Walter Isaacson, as cited by the Times of India , the PayPal co-founder and serial entrepreneur Peter Thiel argued that Apple had done " nothing new after Jobs. " More Tech: Meta and Microsoft just sent employees a memo about Anthropic Microsoft cutting off popular software with no extension Oct. 13 Apple's biggest AI advantage may face new privacy challenge The original iPhone was such a tremendous leap, he said, that management spent the following 15 years refining, marketing, and expanding the business instead of delivering a comparable breakthrough. He contrasted the leadership styles of Apple's prolific former CEOs Steve Jobs, who took unpredictable product bets, and Tim Cook, who perfected the machinery that turned those bets into profits. Thiel called Apple a "pure, well-run value stock," suggesting commercial success and technological progress aren't exactly the same thing. Apple's accounts back that argument with substance. During the first nine months of fiscal 2026, the company spent $62.1 billion on share repurchases, versus $34 billion on research and development, as per an SEC Filing . That's $1.82 in buybacks for every $1 in R&D spending. But buybacks don't prove Apple neglected innovation. Research spending actually rose 33% from a year earlier, and the company has introduced the Apple Watch, AirPods, and its own Mac chips since Jobs died. Story Continues At the same time, Thiel's skepticism hurt shareholders. He declared Apple's era over in 2017. Yet the stock closed October 23 at $347.73, up nearly 28% in 2026, giving Apple a market capitalization of roughly $5.1 trillion as reported by Reuters . There's another irony: its shares trade at around 40 times trailing earnings, hardly a bargain-basement valuation for what Thiel calls a value stock. Apple has proved it can monetize its ecosystem brilliantly. Whether it can invent another revolutionary product remains to be seen. Marques Brownlee echoes Thiel as Apple's AI troubles divide customers Thiel isn't alone in questioning if Apple's financial success comes at the expense of powerful new products. On an episode of the Flagrant podcast , tech reviewer Marques Brownlee, better known as MKBHD, contrasted Steve Jobs' relentless product demands with Tim Cook's mastery of operations. "Tim Cook might be an example of the ruthless supply chain guy. More like, he's the business guy. Stock price has never been higher, but now you're not necessarily as inspired by the new products or visions from the company." That criticism has become especially pointed over Apple's AI endeavors. In March 2025, longtime Apple commentator John Gruber criticized the company for promoting personalized Siri features before it could demonstrate them working. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman and Drake Bennett later talked about the internal problems that delayed Apple's AI ambitions. For iPhone buyers, the disappointment was more personal than a missed technology milestone. In a 2025 post on r/iphone , Reddit user u/Jamballam asked: "How are you going to sell me a phone that doesn't have the features advertised until after the warranty runs out?" That exchange predates Thiel's remarks, but clearly trust matters when phones promise features that arrive late. Still, declaring Apple's innovation finished overlooks the Apple Watch, AirPods, and M1 chips. Its redesigned Siri entered beta in September 2026, and the foldable iPhone Duo reached stores on October 23 . What Peter Thiel's Apple criticism means for Apple stock investors For shareholders, Thiel's criticism runs into a powerful counterargument, which is that Apple's underlying business is still booming. In fiscal Q3 , sales jumped 16% to $109.4 billion. iPhone sales climbed 22%, while Apple's services business generated $30.7 billion at an impressive 75.6% gross margin. That profitable ecosystem helps explain Apple's $5.1 trillion market valuation, which it achieved this year. Nevertheless, Apple stock is trading at a steep valuation and is priced for continued growth. That said, Apple's November 2 earnings report offers the next test. New CEO John Ternus needs to demonstrate whether iPhone upgrades, services growth, and improved AI capabilities can justify that premium while building confidence in Apple's next chapter. Apple doesn't need to reinvent the iPhone every year to reward shareholders. But investors paying today's premium need evidence that its products and future innovations can keep earnings growing. news.Title: Apple vs. Taiwan Semiconductor: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) represent two pillars of the modern technology landscape. Choosing between these giants involves weighing brand power against manufacturing dominance for your 2026 portfolio.

Apple creates the consumer hardware and software ecosystem that millions of people use daily. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing provides the essential manufacturing capacity that makes those devices possible. While they operate at different stages of the supply chain, both companies are massive players in the global electronics market.

The case for Apple

Apple sells a diverse range of consumer electronics, including the iPhone, Mac, and Apple Watch. Its services segment includes the App Store and subscription platforms that provide high-margin recurring revenue and foster customer loyalty. Because indirect distribution channels account for nearly 60% of total net sales, the company depends heavily on third-party retailers and cellular carriers to move its products.

Through the June quarter, trailing-12-month (TTM) revenue reached nearly $467 billion, representing roughly 14% growth compared to the previous year. The company reported a net income of nearly $129 billion for the same period. This resulted in a net margin of nearly 28%, indicating the company remains highly profitable as its revenue base expands.

As of its June 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 0.8x. This ratio measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, indicating how much the company uses debt to finance its operations. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts with short-term assets, was close to 1.0x.

Free cash flow, or the cash left after paying for capital investments, reached nearly $137 billion.

The case for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing operates as a pure-play foundry, meaning it manufactures chips for other companies without designing its own products. It is a critical part of the semiconductor industry , providing specialized engineering support to the world's leading chip designers. By focusing entirely on manufacturing, the company maintains its position as the primary supplier for the global high-performance computing and smartphone markets.

Through the September 2026 quarter, TTM revenue reached nearly $155 billion, a significant increase of approximately 30% over the prior year. Net income for the period was close to $80 billion. The company achieved a net margin of roughly 51%, showing exceptionally strong profitability relative to its total annual sales. This performance highlights the company's ability to maintain high margins while scaling production.

Story Continues

As of its September 2026 balance sheet, the company maintained a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.1x. This low figure suggests that the business relies very little on borrowed money to fund its massive manufacturing facilities. Its current ratio stood at nearly 2.6x, indicating a robust ability to cover its immediate financial obligations with liquid assets.

Free cash flow for the fiscal year was nearly $46 billion.

Risk profile comparison

Apple faces significant regulatory and legal risks, including ongoing antitrust investigations and litigation in the United States and Europe. The company recently addressed a $250 million settlement related to Siri marketing claims. It also relies on a search distribution agreement with Alphabet that could be adversely affected by future regulatory rulings or changes in commercial terms.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing must navigate intense geopolitical tensions given its central role in the global semiconductor supply chain. The company faces competition from rivals like Samsung Electronics and Intel as they attempt to catch up in advanced manufacturing processes. Additionally, the business requires massive recurring capital investments to stay at the cutting edge of chip technology.

Valuation comparison

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing trades at a lower valuation relative to future earnings estimates, while Apple trades at a lower multiple of past 12-month sales.

Investors often look at the Forward P/E , which compares the stock price to future earnings estimates. Another common metric is the P/S ratio, which compares market cap to sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

Taiwan Semiconductor is the faster-growing business and also trades at a lower forward P/E, and therefore offers the highest upside potential. The main risk is a slowdown in chip demand that could cause the stock to underperform. But looking out five years and beyond, TSMC is the stock I would want to hold.

Apple arguably has the widest competitive moat due to its brand power and large base of customers locked into the Apple ecosystem of hardware and services.

But TSMC also enjoys a wide moat by being the world's largest chipmaker. It has even made chips for Apple. It controls over 70% of the foundry market, according to Counterpoint. This means TSMC is one of the most important suppliers not just for AI data centers but for the global economy as a whole.

Over the long term, more devices from Apple and other smartphone brands, data centers, and industrial markets will need many more chips for an increasingly digital economy. This is a big tailwind for TSMC. While Apple posted a 16% year-over-year revenue increase in the recent quarter, TSMC posted a 30% year-over-year revenue increase.

Wall Street analysts expect Apple to grow earnings at an 11% annualized rate in the coming years, but TSMC is expected to grow earnings at 44%. Apple's forward P/E of 36 looks more expensive than TSMC, which tilts the risk-reward balance more in the chipmaker's favor.

news.Title: Elon Musk Says Merging SpaceX and Tesla Would Be a Good Idea. Here's What Investors Should Know.
news.Content:
What do electric cars, rockets, humanoid robots, and artificial intelligence (AI) have in common? Elon Musk believes they could all benefit from being part of the same company.

Musk has publicly backed a potential merger between Space Exploration Technologies Corp (NASDAQ: SPCX) and Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA). Both Musk-led companies have formed special committees to explore the idea, although they have yet to agree on terms of a transaction, which would have to be approved by shareholders.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The logic of merging is understandable. Tesla is expanding into AI, robotics, and energy, while SpaceX is growing beyond rockets and satellite internet into AI computing infrastructure.

But combining two ambitious businesses would not automatically create a better investment. To be good for investors, the merger needs to deliver benefits that outweigh its costs and create additional value for shareholders.

Why does Musk want to combine the companies?

Musk's vision extends beyond selling cars or launching rockets. He wants to build an ecosystem spanning AI , robotics , energy, communications, and computing infrastructure.

Today, pursuing that vision involves coordinating resources across separate companies. A merger could make it easier to share technology, engineering talent, and capital.

Consider chip development. Both companies need advanced computing capabilities for their AI ambitions. Their proposed Terafab semiconductor project could help supply the chips required for future AI systems and robotics.

Besides robotics, satellite connectivity and the infrastructure that requires the support of AI computing would likely benefit from closer cooperation. A combined company might also reduce the friction involved in coordinating investments across separate corporate structures.

But investors should ask an important question: Do these businesses need to merge to cooperate? They could pursue many of the same opportunities through partnerships and joint ventures. Thus, the real justification for a merger must go beyond making collaboration easier.

The real benefits could go beyond cars and rockets

The strongest argument for a merger is that the companies' technologies could reinforce one another.

AI and robotics: Tesla's autonomous driving and Optimus robot projects require computing power, advanced chips, and software. Closer cooperation with SpaceX's AI operations could help accelerate that development.

Story Continues

Energy and computing: AI infrastructure consumes enormous amounts of electricity. Tesla's energy-storage products could help support computing facilities, potentially creating opportunities to coordinate power and infrastructure investments.

Connectivity and space: Starlink provides satellite internet, while SpaceX's rockets deploy satellites. These capabilities could support connected devices and future technologies operating beyond the reach of conventional networks.

If these connections produce better products, lower costs, or faster development, shareholders could benefit in the long run. However, these are potential synergies, not guaranteed profits. The companies must still execute their plans, compete effectively, and earn attractive returns on their investments.

In other words, the key question is whether common ownership would create more value than cooperation between two independent companies.

The risks and complications are substantial

The first challenge could be agreeing on a fair deal. A merger would determine how much of the combined business each group's shareholders own. If Tesla shareholders receive too little for their stake, they could lose out even if the combined company performs well. The same goes for SpaceX shareholders.

The second challenge is governance. Musk has significant interests in both companies and supports the transaction. He has said he will not participate in the special committees' discussions because of this conflict -- an example of how these things can get quite messy if not managed well. Investors will want to watch who ends up controlling any combined entity.

Finally, combining the companies could complicate capital allocation. SpaceX is investing heavily in AI computing infrastructure, while Tesla is pursuing autonomous driving and robotics. A merger might make it easier to move resources between projects, but it could also make it harder for investors to assess which investments are generating attractive returns.

What are investors watching?

A SpaceX-Tesla merger has a plausible strategic rationale. Combining AI, robotics, energy, and space capabilities could accelerate development and open new commercial opportunities.

But strategic logic alone is not enough to justify a deal. Investors need to know whether the merger would create benefits that the companies could not achieve independently, whether the terms are fair to both groups of shareholders, and whether the combined business could generate better returns on its investments.

My view: The strategic case is credible, but the investment case remains unproven. Until the companies disclose meaningful terms and explain the expected financial benefits, investors should not treat the merger proposal as an automatic reason to buy either stock.

news.Title: Prediction: 3 Stocks That Will Be Worth More Than Apple 5 Years From Now
news.Content:
Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) recently reclaimed the mantle as the world's largest company by market cap, at least for a short while. However, when looking five years out, I think three stocks will be worth more: Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX), Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), and Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG).

Apple is a great company, with one of the best compounding businesses on the planet. However, the stock currently trades at a very high valuation given its growth prospects, which likely limits its upside over the next five years.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

As such, let's see why I think these three growth stocks will surpass it by the end of 2031.

1. SpaceX

With a market cap of about $2 trillion, SpaceX is the smallest company on this list, and its stock will need to deliver some pretty strong returns to overtake Apple, which has a $5 trillion valuation. However, I think a likely merger with Tesla (market cap of $1.5 billion) in the next few years will quickly close the gap.

Barring a merger with Tesla, though, I think SpaceX has the opportunity to grow into a company larger than Apple by 2031, even as a stand-alone company. CEO Elon Musk recently projected that the company will reach $500 billion to $1 trillion in annual recurring revenue (ARR) in 2027, led by its artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure business. With the company achieving a one-year payback on its chip and networking investments and planning to add a massive 10 to 20 gigawatts of computing power next year, the path to reaching that number is actually quite clear.

Throw in Starship, Starlink, and its Cursor AI coding business, and SpaceX looks poised to see massive revenue growth over the next five years. It looks as if SpaceX could actually crush Musk's $1 trillion 2030 revenue prediction, but even placing a 10-times price-to-sales (P/S) multiple on that would take SpaceX to being a $10 trillion company.

2. Nvidia

With a $5 trillion market cap, Nvidia would only have to outperform Apple over the next five years to be the larger company. Meanwhile, the chipmaker is growing much faster and is trading at less than half the valuation of Apple on a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) basis, at only 13 times fiscal 2028 (ending January 2028) analyst estimates.

Story Continues

Nvidia looks poised to remain one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI build-out. Its graphics processing units (GPUs) are still the main chips used to train AI models, while it continues to take a larger slice of spending through its networking, central processing units (CPUs), language processing units (LPUs) for inference, and open-weight Nemotron models.

Meanwhile, Nvidia is also set to ride SpaceX's huge AI spending, as the space company ramps up its computing capacity. With SpaceX consolidating on Nvidia's Vera Rubin architecture and Nvidia getting roughly $40 billion per gigawatt of power, the company still has huge growth ahead.

3. Alphabet

With a market cap near $4 trillion, Alphabet has some catching up to do to overtake Apple in the next five years, but I'd be very surprised if it doesn't. The company is the most complete AI player and has built-in advantages in distribution and monetization.

Alphabet's biggest edge is that it has taken a wide lead in custom AI chips with its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). This gives it several advantages, starting with its cloud computing unit, where, with its own chips, it gets a payback in about a year, half the time it takes when using Nvidia GPUs. Meanwhile, Anthropic is set to become a major TPU customer, adding another revenue stream for the company.

On top of that, its TPUs allow it to train its AI models and run inference more cheaply than competitors. With Google Search as the gateway to the internet and given Alphabet's ownership of Chrome and Android, as well as a search revenue-sharing deal with Apple, the company also has a major distribution advantage that helps drive usage and growth. Its global ad network also allows it to better monetize the consumer market than upstarts.

As the most profitable company in the world entering this year, just ahead of Nvidia, and with strong growth ahead, Alphabet looks poised to be a bigger company than Apple by 2031.

news.Title: Target has a problem that sends shoppers to Amazon
news.Content:
Target has always been my retail destination of choice, but I don't even have its app on my phone. That's because if I need something quickly, I go to Amazon.

If I need something only available from Target and I need it fast, I'll place my order on Uber Eats, even though it will often cost more than buying it in-store.

It's a weakness for the retail giant, as it's losing sales to Amazon and Walmart because those retailers offer next-day, and in some cases, same-day delivery.

That's an area where Target has been quietly investing in an effort to bridge the gap with its rivals.

Target improves its delivery

While Target has never been top-of-mind for me when it comes to delivery, the chain has been expanding its reach.

"Over 60% of the U.S. population has access to quicker, easier shopping as Target expands next-day delivery of online orders to more markets. Guests in more than 50 top U.S. metro areas will be able to get their purchases delivered next day — in many cases for free. It's yet another option among Target's fulfillment offerings, which also includes guest-favorite same-day services and two-day shipping," the chain shared in a press release .

Target owns Shipt , which offers free same-day delivery on orders over $35. It also offers a $99 annual membership that waives those limits.

More Target:

Target tackles a frustrating problem for shoppers

Target jumps on food trend Kroger and Publix embraced

Target rolls out another generous deal to win back customers

The chain has also expanded its selection of items available for delivery.

"Most items eligible for shipping at Target are eligible for next-day delivery. That includes hundreds of thousands of items — 85% of what we sell in Target stores," the chain shared.

Next-day delivery is free for orders over $35 or with no minimum order amount if you're a Target Circle 360 member or use your Target Circle Card for purchases.

"This is just one of the ways Target offers a convenient digital shopping experience. We already reach 80% of the U.S. population with same-day delivery — often within two or three hours — and 99% with two-day shipping. And our Order Pickup and Drive Up services are always free and available for guests on their timeline," Target shared.

Target needs to fix delivery

Target has a big bridge to cross in order to catch up to its rivals.

Walmart already serves nearly the entire country with same-day service.

"We expanded our U.S. store-fulfilled delivery areas in Q4 FY25. We can now reach 93% of U.S. households with same-day delivery," the company shared in its fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release .

Story Continues

That number climbed to 95%, according to an April press release .

eMarketer analyst Rachel Wolff warned in April that Target faces a difficult path to catching up with Amazon and Walmart on delivery speed.

"Target's delivery speed disadvantage underscores how difficult it is to catch up as Amazon and Walmart are zooming ahead. At this point, it's unclear whether Target has the means — or even the vision — to close the gaps with its competitors.

"Much of the company's turnaround strategy is rooted in returning to its pre-pandemic model, rather than reinventing the business for an age in which customer loyalty is more fragile and more spending is shifting online," she wrote.

Target tries to catch up to Amazon and Walmart

RTM Nexus CEO Dominick Miserandino had a simple response when I asked him about Target investing in delivery.

"They need to! They're the go to for that quick purchase and that feeling of getting it asap is the consumer standard," he told TheStreet.

Target COO Lisa Roath talked about delivery during the chain's second-quarter earnings call .

"We also saw meaningful gains in delivery speed. This past quarter, we fulfilled nearly 30% more same-day and next-day units than last year, and we will continue investing to get even faster," she said.

Delivery, she noted, is part of a broader effort to improve customer service.

"When we combine the impact of our in-store transitions, assortment changes, tech enhancements and improvements in inventory reliability, it all adds up to an elevated experience that is being noticed by our guests," she added.

Those efforts, Roath shared, have started to pay off.

"Overall satisfaction scores continue to improve across multiple measures of the guest experience, extending the momentum we shared with you last quarter and reinforcing that our continued investments in our teams, training and our team's tireless execution are making a difference," the COO said.

The chain has been addressing concerns that GlobalData Managing Director Neil Saunders raised in September ahead of Michael Fiddelke taking over as CEO.

"Visiting Target stores is less pleasurable and less fun than it used to be," Saunders said in an email. "There is far too much friction, and the experience is sometimes unpleasant. That's an issue as it lowers the probability of people making visits, reduces visit frequency, and weakens conversion and basket size when people are in stores," he told Retail Dive .

news.Title: Will Alphabet Stock Surge After Oct. 28?
news.Content:
Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG)(NASDAQ: GOOGL) reports Q3 2026 earnings after the market closes on Oct. 28. Wall Street analysts have an average revenue estimate of $127.8 billion, which would be a 25% year-over-year increase, and earnings per share (EPS) of $3.

Last quarter, Alphabet easily surpassed revenue expectations -- and its share price still ended up falling 7% the next day. Based on the tech giant's recent track record, investors probably shouldn't feel too confident about which direction Alphabet stock will move immediately post-earnings.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

What history says about Alphabet's post-earnings performance

The way Alphabet stock moves after an earnings report is about as predictable as a coin flip. Over the last four quarters, it has had an even split, closing higher the day after earnings twice and closing lower twice, despite beating headline EPS expectations each time. Its moves this year have been significant, closing up 10% after its April 29 report, and down 7.1% after its July 22 report.

Stretching it to the last 16 quarters, Alphabet has closed up seven times and closed down nine times. The average move is 5.2% in either direction.

Why July's beat turned into a sharp drop

Alphabet's earnings report in Q2 2026 looked great on the surface. Revenue was up 24% to $119.8 billion, Google Cloud revenue grew 82% to $24.8 billion, and EPS skyrocketed 294% to $9.11. The company's post-earnings slump makes more sense when you dig a little deeper.

Net income included about $99 billion in unrealized gains, mostly from Alphabet's investments in Space Exploration Technologies and Anthropic, and that caused the huge jump in EPS. These holdings are certainly valuable, but an increase in unrealized gains is much different from an increase in sales. Alphabet's adjusted EPS (without the unrealized gains) was $2.85, which actually missed consensus estimates by $0.04.

Alphabet also raised its 2026 capex guidance to between $195 billion and $205 billion, and management said that 2027 capex will increase significantly. The company ended the quarter with negative free cash flow for the first time in its history since going public in 2004. The heavy spending worried investors and resulted in a sell-off.

What to watch on Oct. 28

Story Continues

There are a few potential swing factors, outside of revenue and EPS, to watch for in Alphabet's Q3 earnings. Any updates to its 2026 capex, as well as early guidance for 2027, could cause a big move, especially as rates have gone up and investors have become increasingly concerned with AI spending.

Free cash flow will give an idea of how manageable Alphabet's spending is. CFO Anat Ashkenazi said it will "remain under pressure" in the Q2 earnings call. How deep in the red it ends up will likely play a role in how the market reacts to earnings. Finally, Google Cloud revenue is a key metric, as it indicates that all the AI spending is turning into measurable sales growth. Ideally, Google Cloud growth will hold around 80%.

All that said, it's best to keep your expectations open. Earnings reports and post-earnings performance are inherently unpredictable. Considering how investors have rotated out of AI stocks recently, I think a decline in Alphabet stock is more likely than a surge post-earnings. However, when you're a long-term investor, what matters is what a company does over a period of years, not right after earnings.

news.Title: Lumentum stock surges 10% as AI components ‘completely sold out’
news.Content: Lumentum Holdings (LITE) shares jumped about 8% to $818 on Monday, Oct. 26, after StoneX initiated coverage of the optical networking company with a Buy rating and a $1,200 price target. The rally spread to other optical networking stocks. Coherent (COHR) and Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) gained about 6% and 7%, respectively, while the Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (LYTE) rose 4%. StoneX said Lumentum occupies "critical scarcity points" in high-speed indium phosphide lasers, cloud transceivers and optical circuit switches, The Fly reported . The analyst also highlighted management's comments that AI-related optoelectronic components were "completely sold out" through 2029, as Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston told Bloomberg earlier this month. The new price target implies roughly 47% upside from Lumentum's afternoon trading price. Why Wall Street is bullish on Lumentum Lumentum, based in San Jose, California, makes lasers and optical components used in telecommunications networks and data centers. The company has benefited largely from the AI infrastructure boom as tech hyperscalers spend billions of dollars building data centers that require faster connections between servers. Related: Analysts revamp Super Micro stock price targets after 10% surge on revenue boost One of its biggest backers is Nvidia (NVDA). In March, Nvidia announced a multi-year strategic partnership with Lumentum to develop advanced optical technologies for next-generation AI infrastructure. The agreement includes a multibillion-dollar purchase commitment from Nvidia and rights to access future manufacturing capacity for advanced laser components. Nvidia also committed to invest $2 billion in Lumentum to support research and development and expand U.S. manufacturing, including a new fabrication facility. "Together with Lumentum, NVIDIA is advancing the world's most sophisticated silicon photonics to build the next generation of gigawatt-scale AI factories," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in the announcement . StoneX isn't the only firm optimistic about Lumentum. On Oct. 20, Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis raised his price target on Lumentum to $1,250 from $1,200 and maintained a Buy rating. Curtis expects Lumentum to capture a larger share of Alphabet's (GOOGL) optical circuit switching demand and benefit from growing adoption of 1.6T transceivers. Jefferies also expects Lumentum to become Alphabet's largest optical circuit switch supplier next year, overtaking the tech giant's in-house production. Lumentum earnings reflect growing AI demand Story Continues Lumentum's latest quarterly results showed strong demand for its optical networking products. In its fiscal fourth quarter ended June 27, the company reported revenue of $1.01 billion, up 109.3% from $480.7 million a year earlier. Adjusted earnings rose to $3.23 per share from $0.88 a year earlier. For fiscal 2026, revenue reached $3.01 billion, compared with $1.6 billion in fiscal 2025. Also read: Meta stock falls despite Wall Street analysts raising price targets The company expects fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue of $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion, with adjusted earnings of $4.05 to $4.35 per share. Lumentum is scheduled to report its next quarterly results on Nov. 5. Investors will be watching closely whether the company can expand production quickly enough to meet demand, as well as its outlook for cloud networking revenue and profit margins. Lumentum shares have gained 122% so far in 2026, as of this writing, although the stock has pulled back sharply from its recent all-time high of $1,143, reached on October 8. news.Title: Mark Cuban puts Bitcoin and Apple in the same bucket
news.Content:
Artificial intelligence can change the world without every company being worth the price investors are paying. That gap is getting harder to ignore.

The expectations surrounding Anthropic's upcoming IPO offer another sign of investor enthusiasm for artificial intelligence. The company publicly filed for its initial public offering on Oct. 26, though its share price and offering size have not yet been determined.

Some current and prospective investors, however, value the AI firm at around $1.5 trillion, Reuters reported .

Billionaire investor Mark Cuban thinks markets have already crossed into the crypto and AI bubble territory.

Related: Arthur Hayes says AI bubble won't burst like 2008

In an interview released Monday , Cuban said the setup differs from the dot-com boom because "everything's a meme stock."

"Bitcoin is a meme stock, right? Pick Micron, you know, pick Google, Apple, they're meme stocks."

Cuban was not saying Bitcoin is literally a stock. His point spotlighted the broader trading behavior.

On Jan. 9, 2024, for instance, Bitcoin jumped to around $48,000 after a false post from the SEC's compromised X account claimed spot Bitcoin ETFs had been approved.

Within minutes, however, BTC fell back to $45,000 right after the agency disavowed the announcement. Apple offers a more recent example.

Shares of the iPhone-maker rose as much as 1% in early trading on Oct. 23 as the iPhone Duo reached stores following strong pre-orders and delivery estimates stretching into January. Apple shares were down about 1.3% in trading Monday , giving back part of those gains.

Cuban argued that investors now move rapidly in and out of major assets on relatively small pieces of news instead of focusing on long-term value.

"We're trading them like baseball cards," Cuban said, adding that he believes markets are in a bubble for that reason.

He was less certain about what could end it.

"What causes it to burst? I have no idea."

Popular on TheStreet Roundtable:

Goldman Sachs revises rating and target on beaten-down AI stock

Sam Altman has kind words for Elon Musk's flying car

Trump vows crypto scam crackdown then gets hit with lawsuit

Why Cuban's warning has a real-world backdrop

Meta spent $34.91 billion on capital projects in the third quarter of 2026, exceeding the $32.79 billion it generated in operating cash flow. This left the Mark Zuckerberg-led company with negative free cash flow for the period.

Last week, Meta beat Wall Street's third-quarter revenue expectations and forecast stronger fourth-quarter sales. But shares still fell about 7% on Oct. 22 as investors focused on its enormous AI spending plans and a new non-voting share class it said could help fund growth.

Story Continues

Earlier this month, the stock prices of Nvidia, Oracle and CoreWeave also dropped after investors received clarification around OpenAI's annualized revenue figures .

The difference reflected how revenue through partners was counted, not billions of dollars in suddenly lost sales. The clarification rippled through several AI-linked stocks.

Still, the AI boom is backed by real demand.

Nvidia reported $89 billion in data-center revenue for its fiscal second quarter , up 117% from a year earlier.

Cuban's point here is not that AI is fake, but that, in his view, investors are overpaying for the hype

His advice was simple: "Have some cash because at some point it's going to turn." He expects winners to emerge, but says he does not know which companies they will be.

news.Title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 26: AI Optimism Lifts Nasdaq as Tech Stocks Rebound
news.Content:
The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) gained 0.70% to 7,677, the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) rose 0.82% to 26,169 as AI optimism returned, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) edged up 0.28% to 52,362, diverging from Friday's energy-driven session as oil prices retreated.

Gold prices rose 0.46% to $4,026.30 as of U.S. market close and the 10-Year Treasury yield rose 0.04% to 5%, with investors favoring Real Estate and Technology stocks while Communication Services shares faced selling pressure.

Today's biggest moves

Surgery Partners (NASDAQ:SGRY) soared 48% on reports of a majority-stake takeover negotiation, while Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) jumped 8% following a bullish price target initiation. Conversely, Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) fell 2% after filing to raise capital for AI infrastructure, and Petrobras (NYSE:PBR) plunged 14% following election results in Brazil.

What this means for investors

The big driver for Wall Street's tech stock rally on Oct. 26, 2026 was the long-awaited initial public offering (IPO) filing by artificial intelligence giant Anthropic. The company filed its S-1 prospectus to go public on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT." Its massive revenue growth figures in the filing calmed investor fears that the artificial intelligence boom was losing steam.

Anthropic's IPO revived enthusiasm for technology stocks, helping the Nasdaq Composite lead the market today despite pressure on more mature communication services providers. Adding to today's market performance was Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) stock gaining over 5%. Barclays upgraded shares to an Overweight rating, and raised its price target from $370 to $450 due to potential ties with CEO Elon Musk's other company, SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX), growth in Tesla's robotaxi business, and a recovery in its core automotive operations.

Meanwhile, Meta Platforms shares slipped after the company disclosed plans to raise up to $95 billion for AI infrastructure, signaling that the immense capital requirements for industry dominance remain a primary concern for mega-cap investors. Next, investors are looking ahead to this week's earnings from Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) and the upcoming Federal Reserve interest rate decision, which will determine if the current momentum can survive tightening financial conditions.

news.Title: Don't Miss This Week's 5 Most Important Earnings Charts
news.Content:

The AI Revolution trade will also be in the spotlight with several key infrastructure companies reporting earnings.

But it's not just about technology this week. Big pharma, key restaurants like Wingstop, Chipotle and Starbucks, and big oil like ExxonMobil and Chevron will also report earnings.

True Earnings All-Stars

These are five of the top earnings charts this week. They are true earnings all-stars. These companies have excellent earnings surprise track records and some of the stocks are trading near all-time highs.

It's not easy to beat every quarter, or nearly every quarter, for several years in a row.

Can they beat again?

Is it too late to get into Eli Lilly?

news.Title: KLA Corporation (KLAC) vs. AMAT and LRCX: Can Rising Semiconductor Complexity Create Another Growth Cycle?
news.Content:
Is KLAC a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on KLA Corporation on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on KLAC. KLA Corporation's share was trading at $145.61 as of October 23rd 2026. KLAC's trailing and forward P/E were 39.78 and 26.95 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a semiconductor equipment company pitched as a great investment. KLAC shares gained 19.83% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Applied Materials and Lam Research gained 63.07% and 46.65%, respectively, during the same period. Why are semiconductor equipment stocks rising, and does KLAC's recent weakness make this a good time to buy?

Posonskyi Andrey/Shutterstock.com

In June, we published an article about the 10 Best Growth Stocks to Buy According to Billionaire Dan Loeb and KLAC ranked #8 in that article. KLAC has declined since then, leaving investors who backed the stock waiting for that confidence to translate into returns. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on KLAC. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

KLA Corporation (NASDAQ:KLAC) provides tools that help chip makers find defects, measure wafer quality, and run their factories more efficiently. Its fastest-growing opportunity right now is tied to artificial intelligence-driven semiconductor demand, and that is central to understanding the stock. As chips become smaller and more complex, manufacturers need more advanced inspection and measurement tools to keep production yields high, which is exactly where KLA Corporation operates.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

In fiscal 2026, the company's revenue reached $13.6 billion, up 11.7% from a year earlier, and it kept very healthy profit margins. These are strong results, but the stock is not cheap, as it trades at about 49 times trailing earnings and 33 times forward earnings. This suggests investors are paying not just for today's performance, but also for several more years of AI-related growth.

The positive case rests on KLA Corporation being a leader in process control, meaning the tools that catch problems during chip making. Every new generation of advanced chips needs more inspection and measurement, and even tiny defects can hurt production yields. As AI pushes chip makers to expand capacity and invest in newer manufacturing technology, demand for KLA Corporation systems should benefit. The company also enjoys long relationships with leading chip makers, who find it costly and difficult to switch suppliers. Growth in advanced packaging and AI-related chip investment could support the business for years.

Story Continues

The company's recent results support this view. KLA Corporation turned a large share of its sales into real cash, generating $4.14 billion in operating cash flow and $3.8 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2026. Its 35.6% net margin and 76.1% return on equity show how efficiently it makes money for shareholders. Fourth-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion also came in above the midpoint of management's guidance, showing steady execution even in a choppy industry. If AI-driven chip spending continues and manufacturers keep adding advanced capacity, bulls believe the company can keep growing earnings and justify its premium price.

Analysts are also fairly upbeat. Their average price target of about $233.77 implies nearly 29% upside from the current price of roughly $180.64, with individual targets ranging from $175 to $325. This bullish outlook depends on continued AI-related chip investment, strength in advanced packaging, and stable margins. However, because the stock already carries a high valuation, slower earnings growth or weaker chip spending could make that price harder to defend. You can check out why Jim Cramer recommends buying KLA stock in small doses here .

A slowdown in chip industry spending is the main risk. Even if AI demand stays strong, semiconductor equipment is a cyclical business that depends on customers' investment decisions. Wider U.S. export limits on selling chip equipment to China add another challenge, since China has historically been a meaningful source of revenue for KLA Corporation. With a premium valuation and little room for error, the stock could come under pressure if growth slows, margins shrink, or geopolitical restrictions tighten.

Another risk for the stock is that rising chip complexity makes KLA's own product development harder and more expensive. Each new manufacturing process requires inspection tools that can detect smaller defects accurately without slowing production. KLA warns that its success depends on anticipating customer needs and launching new technologies on time and at competitive costs. Existing customer relationships cannot guarantee it wins every new equipment purchase. A delayed launch or a better competing tool could cost it business even while AI investment remains strong. Higher development spending could also pressure margins before new products generate revenue. In our opinion, this execution risk could pressure KLA's valuation if growing inspection demand fails to translate into sustained earnings growth.

Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 81 hedge fund portfolios held KLA Corporation at the end of the second quarter, up from 71 in the previous quarter. That is a steady climb, suggesting institutional interest in the company is improving. Among its peers, Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) was held by 137 hedge funds, down from 138, while Onto Innovation (NASDAQ:ONTO) was held by 75 hedge funds, up from 67, and Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) was held by 139 hedge funds, up from 123. This shows institutional investors grew most confident in Lam Research Corporation during the quarter, with KLA Corporation and Onto Innovation also seeing solid gains, while Applied Materials held roughly steady with only a marginal dip in ownership.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture, with just 1.86% of KLA Corporation shares sold short. That compares with 1.71% for Applied Materials, Inc., 2.07% for Lam Research Corporation, and a much higher 7.68% for Onto Innovation Inc. Because fewer investors are betting against KLA Corporation than Onto Innovation Inc., there is little direct bearish pressure on the stock. Still, its premium valuation and reliance on continued chip spending remain the key things to watch.

Valuation Analysis

KLAC's forward P/E is 26.95x. Applied Materials, Inc., Lam Research Corporation, and Onto Innovation Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 21.14x, 24.88x, and 16.84x, respectively. KLAC's own forward P/E was 33.44x on December 31, 2025, meaning its current valuation is approximately 19% lower. We believe the current valuation reflects investor concerns about semiconductor spending cycles, export restrictions, and the durability of AI-driven equipment demand. However, its premium to all three peers suggests that the historical decline has reduced expectations without making the shares an obvious bargain. KLA's fiscal 2026 revenue increased 11.7% to $13.6 billion, while fourth-quarter adjusted earnings per share rose approximately 12% from $0.94 to $1.05, supported by annual free cash flow of $3.77 billion. We believe continued earnings growth could support the current valuation, but a narrowing premium would reduce shareholder returns even if profits keep rising. If KLA can convert increasing chip complexity and advanced packaging demand into sustained earnings and cash flow growth, the shares could offer attractive long-term returns, although we would prefer a lower entry price to provide more protection against a slower semiconductor spending cycle.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on KLA Corporation (KLAC) by Quality Equities in January 2025, which highlighted semiconductor tailwinds, TSMC's capex expansion, and AI-driven demand for KLA's process control tools. KLAC's stock price has appreciated by approximately 94.19% since our coverage. We believe KLAC could be a good long-term investment at a lower price, as its premium valuation could limit returns even if earnings continue growing, particularly if semiconductor spending slows.

KLA Corporation is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds . While KLAC could benefit from growing demand for advanced chip inspection and packaging tools, we believe certain AI infrastructure stocks offer far stronger long-term potential at a much more attractive entry point. If you are looking for an AI stock more promising than KLAC that operates as a critical AI tollbooth and stands as the most important company in the world, check out our report about this must-own AI stock .

news.Title: Lumentum Is Sold Out Until 2029. Is LITE Stock Still a Buy at $800+?
news.Content:
Lumentum (LITE) is sold out of optical components through early 2029, according to CEO Michael Hurlston. Hurlston said the company could not meet about 70% of demand for certain products through 2027. In my view, Lumentum does not need to prove that artificial intelligence (AI) networking demand exists. It needs to produce enough components to serve that demand.

Lumentum's main advantage is that it sits on a scarce input: The lasers that power AI data-center optics. Its electro-absorption modulated lasers (EMLs) are in a supply crunch, helping the company with pricing power and margin expansion. This supply shortage also spreads across the company's continuous wave and ultra-high-power lasers. The best part about Lumentum is that demand for its lasers will seemingly always be there, whether the industry moves toward pluggable modules, near-packaged optics, or co-packaged optics.

Released on Aug. 11, Lumentum's fiscal fourth-quarter results show how the company is already benefiting. Revenue surged 109% year-over-year (YOY) to $1.01 billion in Q4, while non-GAAP operating margin rose to 36.6% from 15% a year earlier. Management also guided Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue to $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion. This shows that the company is benefiting from both higher sales and improved efficiency. If Lumentum expands production without a similar increase in operating costs, the company could boost profits. Moreover, its 1.6T transceivers and optical circuit switching products offer additional growth opportunities.

About Lumentum Stock

Lumentum provides optical and photonic products, from components like lasers to systems spanning cloud transceivers and optical circuit switches. In recent years, the firm has become a crucial backbone of the global AI boom. Founded in 2015, the company is headquartered in San Jose, California.

LITE stock has soared in 2026, up 122% year-to-date (YTD) as investors have poured into companies benefiting from surging AI infrastructure spending. The bull rally has been led by demand for optical elements to link larger clusters of high-speed GPUs. But AI stocks also have become fairly volatile. After trading near $602 at the end of July, LITE stock rallied to a high of $1,143 on Oct. 9, then fell to the $800 mark within a week. LITE stock now trades at roughly $818 per share. In contrast, the iShares U.S. Telecommunications ETF (IYZ) has climbed only 14% YTD.

Story Continues

Is the Valuation Still Reasonable?

Lumentum stock trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 38 times, almost in line with its five-year average of roughly 37.5 times. However, its price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 22.6 times is well above its five-year average of about 5.4 times.

This premium reflects the growth investors expect from the company as AI infrastructure spending drives demand for optical components. Analysts expect EPS to grow 143% in fiscal 2027 and another 67% in fiscal 2028. If these forecasts materialize, strong earnings growth could make the current valuation more reasonable. However, Lumentum still needs to expand production and turn its unmet demand into actual sales. Any delays or weaker-than-expected growth could put pressure on LITE stock.

Lumentum's Earnings and Growth Drivers

The latest quarterly results give investors plenty to cheer. In Q4, the company reported revenue of $1.01 billion, up 109% YOY and ahead of Wall Street's $988 million estimate. The increase was widespread throughout the company. Components revenue grew 103% YOY to $649.4 million, while Systems revenue increased 123% YOY to $356.9 million.

Profitability also improved, as gross margin climbed to 50.4% and the operating margin increased to 36.6%. On the balance sheet, free cash flow amounted to $196.2 million, while the company accumulated about $2.7 billion in cash and short-term investments by the end of the period, providing further financial flexibility.

Management anticipates the trend to persist through fiscal 2027. Lumentum is projecting an increase of more than $150 million in sales for Q1, along with gains in profitability. Revenue for the period is expected to be $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion, while adjusted EPS is projected to range between $4.05 and $4.35. CEO Michael Hurlston said that about half of the expected revenue growth will come from its components business, while the rest will come from 1.6T transceivers and faster deliveries of optical circuit switches.

What Do Analysts Expect for LITE Stock?

Analysts remain bullish after the latest earnings report. Stifel recently raised its price target from $1,100 to $1,232 and kept a "Buy" rating on shares. Meanwhile, Bernstein analyst Daniel Zhu has a "Buy" rating and a price target of $1,220 for LITE stock.

Overall, LITE stock holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating from 25 Wall Street analysts with coverage. The mean price target of $1,169 reflects 43% potential upside from current levels, while the Street-high price target of $1,500 implies potential upside of 83% from here.

news.Title: Trading Day: AI light, Brazil flight
news.Content:
By Jamie McGeever

ORLANDO, Florida, Oct 26 (Reuters) - Stocks mostly rose on Monday, lifted by renewed optimism around AI as Anthropic filed for a US IPO and as investors awaited more 'Big Tech' earnings later this week. Weaker oil prices also support risk appetite.

The big exception, however, was Brazil, where financial assets plunged ‌following left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's shock win in Sunday's presidential election.

In my column today, I look at whether 'stagflation' pressures may be building in the US. ‌A deflating artificial intelligence bubble puts downward pressure on Wall Street and wider economic growth, but the revival of oil and energy prices is putting upward pressure on inflation. It's a tricky one for investors, and the ​Fed.

Today's Key Reads

• Brazil stocks, real tumble as Lula win ends bullish run

• Anthropic's IPO filing shows explosive growth, risks and staggering costs

• Meta eyes record $95 billion equity raise to fund AI expansion

• In China, the AI bubble has already burst

• Fed to hit pause on rate hikes, but maybe not for long

• Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Brazil -14%. Asia mixed, Europe and UK up around 0.8%. Wall Street higher: Nasdaq +0.8%, S&P 500 +0.7%, Dow +0.3%.SECTORS/SHARES: Seven sectors on the S&P 500 rise, four fall. Tech +1.5%, comms services -1.4%. Tesla +5%, DoorDash -6%.FX: Brazilian real -8.5%, biggest fall since devaluation in 1999. Philippine peso sinks ‌to record low near 64.00/$. US dollar index edges higher.BONDS: ⁠Brazil buys back bonds, cancels auctions. US 2-year auction is ok — foreign demand dips, domestic demand surges.COMMODITIES/METALS: Oil slips — Brent -0.8%, WTI -1.5%. Gold +0.5% back above $4,000/oz.

Today's Talking Points:

AI funding blitz

If investors were showing signs of AI fatigue in recent weeks, they're hiding it well as this week gets underway. On Monday, ⁠Anthropic filed for a US IPO, Meta announced plans for a $95 billion equity raise, and SpaceX said it has struck a $40 billion deal with Apollo Global Management for AI chip funding. The Anthropic IPO could value the company at a record-breaking $1.5 trillion or more, and Meta's capital raise would also be a record.

The eye-popping sums needed to fund the AI buildout have begun to suck some of the ​air ​out of the AI bubble, but that was shrugged off on Monday, at least temporarily — tech and AI ​stocks fueled a solid rebound on Wall Street. Competition for investor ‌capital is heating up.

Brazil

Politically, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's surprise election victory on Sunday was truly historic: never before had a candidate won the decisive second-round vote after losing the first. It also means a record-setting fourth term for Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday. Unsurprisingly, given the historic significance of Lula's comeback, there was a reaction across Brazilian markets.

Story Continues

Few doubt the scale of Brazil's fiscal and economic challenges, but Monday's collapse in Brazilian assets is likely to reverse, to some degree. Part of the selloff was because investors were caught so flat-footed. As late as Sunday, prediction markets were pointing to an 80% chance of a win for Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. But Lula's scope to push through an agenda that investors fear will ‌be limited, due to Bolsonaro's backing in Congress.

Central bank bonanza

This week is one of the busiest in years ​for policymaking in the world's developed economies, with half of the G10 central banks set to decide interest ​rates. Monetary authorities in New Zealand and Canada are widely expected to hike by ​25 basis points, while those in the US, euro zone and Japan are expected to keep them on hold but signal possible increases in ‌December.

The common enemy is inflation, which is already too sticky in many ​countries. Oil and global energy prices remain elevated ​as war continues to choke Middle East supply routes, and the worry for policymakers is this bleeds into core inflation and becomes embedded in inflation expectations. But if the AI bubble deflates, growth, consumer confidence and investor sentiment could deflate too, putting policymakers in an even tighter bind.

What could move markets tomorrow?

• Japan services producer price inflation (September)

• ​South Korea GDP (Q3, advance)

• US Treasury sells $70 billion of 5-year notes ‌at auction

• US durable goods (September)

• Corporate earnings, including Visa, Coca-Cola, Boeing, Seagate Technology, HSBC, Novartis

news.Title: Why Google might avoid an earnings 'reckoning' this week
news.Content:
Google's ( GOOG ) investors have a few things in their favor coming into earnings day this week that Meta ( META ) investors weren't afforded when the tech giant reported a few negative surprises .

"Google has already done some of its fundraising and indicated a 'significant' increase in capex next year when it reported Q2, so that particular reckoning may be behind it," D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria wrote in a note on Monday. "It is worth noting that Mr. Brin and Mr. Page moved out of California before the 1/1/26 cutoff and may be able to avoid having to sell their shares. Which means that investors will be able to focus on the Anthropic-driven growth in Google Cloud."

Meta surprised investors last week on several fronts.

The company posted negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012 amid aggressive AI spending. It signaled more aggressive spending in coming quarters.

To fund that spending, it further surprised investors by establishing a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock, which effectively serves as a 2-for-1 stock split.

Under the scheme — in part designed to keep founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg working in California as the 5% billionaire's tax looms — existing shareholders will receive one new nonvoting Class C share for every Class A or Class B share they hold. Trading is slated to begin in January 2027.

Issuing nonvoting stock allows Zuckerberg to raise external capital for Meta's AI build-out without diluting his personal voting control over the tech giant.

Meta shares have come under pressure on fears Zuckerberg may have to sell shares to pay for his Prop 40 tax bill.

But as Luria pointed out, Google investors need not worry on this front.

Co-founder Larry Page bought two Miami estates for a combined $173.4 million, the Wall Street Journal reported earlier this year. His co-founder, Sergey Brin, moved to the Nevada side of Lake Tahoe and also bought a home in Miami this year, Fortune reported.

"We expect the company to discuss its plans to regain primacy in AI, where it is now a 2nd or 3rd place in each of the markets — 2nd in chat to ChatGPT, 3rd in enterprise to Anthropic and OpenAI, and now even trailing Meta's Muse in the personal AI assistant market," Luria wrote about Google's upcoming earnings report.

news.Title: Tesla Isn’t a Hyperscaler. Why the AI Bears Are Misreading Its $5 Billion Capex Cut.
news.Content:
Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) is spending less money than originally planned this year. And for investors who track how much money is being poured into artificial intelligence, that might sound like bad news.

But Tesla's decision to reduce its 2026 capital expenditure (capex) forecast by more than $5 billion isn't necessarily a warning about AI demand. In fact, it could be a smart move for the electric vehicle maker.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The reason is simple. Tesla doesn't need to build massive amounts of computing capacity to compete with Amazon , Alphabet , and Microsoft .

That's not its business.

Image source: Tesla.

Tesla is still all-in on AI

On Tesla's third-quarter earnings call , Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Taneja announced the company reduced its 2026 capex forecast from more than $25 billion to approximately $20 billion.

The reduction doesn't mean Tesla is backing away from artificial intelligence. The company continues to develop its Full Self-Driving technology, expand its Cybercab robotaxi program , and work on its Optimus humanoid robots. All three projects require considerable investment. But they don't require Tesla to build the equivalent of Amazon Web Services or Microsoft's Azure.

Tesla needs computing power to train its AI models and improve its autonomous systems. It also needs manufacturing capacity to produce vehicles and robots, as well as the infrastructure to operate its planned robotaxi fleet.

Those investments serve a specific purpose: developing products and services Tesla can eventually sell to customers.

Tesla doesn't need to win the data center race

Cloud computing companies are spending hundreds of billions of dollars building data centers to support AI workloads. Alphabet raised its 2026 capex forecast to $200 billion, while Amazon increased its spending plans to $220 billion.

The aggressive spending makes a lot of sense. Those companies are building computing infrastructure that supports their existing cloud businesses, serves external customers, and provides the capacity needed to meet growing demand for AI services. Tesla has a different business model.

That doesn't mean Elon Musk's company can stop investing in AI infrastructure. Training autonomous driving models requires enormous computing resources, and those requirements could increase as the company expands its ambitions.

Story Continues

But there's little reason for Tesla to match the spending of companies whose business is selling computing capacity. In fact, building more infrastructure than it needs would tie up capital that could be used to expand vehicle production, develop Optimus, or support its robotaxi business.

And with those businesses still developing, Tesla has good reasons to be selective about where its money goes.

Tesla's capex cut is good news for investors

Tesla posted $28.05 billion in revenue for the third quarter, essentially unchanged from a year earlier. Automotive revenue declined 3%, while operating margins narrowed from 5.8% to 2.6%. Those numbers demonstrate that Tesla can't rely on its automotive business to generate unlimited amounts of cash for new projects.

But even so, Tesla generated $1.53 billion in free cash flow during the quarter and ended September with more than $45 billion in cash and investments. Cutting back on unneeded spending will give Tesla more flexibility to work on its autonomous driving and robotics businesses.

And importantly, management hasn't suggested that its AI development plans are being scaled back. Taneja said capital spending is expected to increase in the coming years as Tesla expands robotaxi operations, Optimus manufacturing, and AI computing infrastructure.

So the reduction in this year's budget appears to be more about when Tesla spends money than whether it intends to make those investments.

For investors in Nvidia and other AI infrastructure suppliers, Tesla's decision also shouldn't be confused with a slowdown in hyperscaler spending. The companies building cloud computing infrastructure have different customers, different revenue opportunities, and much larger capital budgets.

Tesla's challenge isn't to build the world's biggest collection of data centers. It's to turn AI technology into profitable products. And if the company can accomplish that while spending $5 billion less than originally planned, shareholders have every reason to welcome the decision.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

news.Title: Tesla stock leaves rest of the Magnificent 7 in the dust, surging to October's top spot
news.Content:
For most of 2026, Tesla has been the Magnificent Seven's minivan. In October, it's the only one leaving skid marks.

Tesla ( TSLA ) stock jumped about 5% Monday, its best day since early September and its highest close in about three months. The rest of Big Tech was a mixed bag, with Apple ( AAPL ), Alphabet ( GOOGL ), and Meta ( META ) all ending lower.

That leaves Tesla with two very different report cards. It's still down by double digits this year, the worst showing in the Magnificent Seven. But it's up by double digits in October, the best in the group, while Meta, Alphabet, and Nvidia ( NVDA ) are all lower for the month.

Tesla is breaking through a crowded spot on the chart

The stock opened above Friday's high — a gap — and pushed through the $386 area. That level is both Tesla's highest close of October and roughly its 200-day moving average , a long-term trend line many traders watch. Clearing both at once is what makes this a breakout.

Even so, Tesla remains about a fifth below its record close.

The SpaceX connection

The rally came alongside a Barclays upgrade betting that a Tesla merger with SpaceX ( SPCX ) would hand shareholders a takeout premium , as Pras Subramanian reported . Barclays raised its price target to $450 from $370. Musk confirmed last week that the two companies had formed independent committees to explore a combination, though no deal has been announced.

Tesla is already in on the joke. On Monday, its Robotaxi service switched on a bigger Houston service area shaped like a Starship rocket, announced with a "Houston, we have liftoff" post. "I swear it's just a coincidence 😂," Musk replied on X.

A combination wouldn't just bring rockets. On Sunday, Musk said SpaceX had closed $40 billion in debt financing to buy AI chips, and he also warned about neoclouds — rent-a-GPU cloud companies such as CoreWeave ( CRWV ) — as my colleague Ines Ferré reported . A merged company would share that chip bill.

Watch $386. Holding it keeps the liftoff on course, while a slide back below would turn Monday into a one-day pop. Above, the next stop is the low $450s, where Barclays' target and Tesla's 2026 closing high nearly overlap.
