news.Title: Barclays Just Upgraded Tesla Stock. Here's Why.
news.Content:
Barclays' senior analyst Dan Levy believes Tesla (TSLA) shares are worth buying after Elon Musk hinted at the electric vehicle (EV) maker's potential merger with SpaceX (SPCX) on the latter's recent earnings call. In a research note this morning, Levy upgraded TSLA to "Overweight" and raised his price objective to $450, indicating potential upside of about 13% from current levels.

Tesla stock has already been in a sharp uptrend in recent months, currently trading more than 30% above its price in late July.

Why Barclays Upgraded Tesla Stock

He's convinced that such a transaction will likely value the EV stock at a premium, which makes it rather attractive at its current price-to-sales (P/S) multiple of about 15x.

Even from a technical perspective, TSLA shares look positioned for continued gains ahead. At the time of writing, they are trading firmly above their major moving averages (MAs), with an RSI in the early 60s indicating significant room before the company hits overbought levels.

What Else Could Drive TSLA Shares Higher?

Crucially, Barclays expects Tesla's core business to help unlock its stock price as well.

"The auto business is on track to grow this year after two years of declines — and 2027 should see further upside, supported by demand spurred by FSD and rising exports from Giga Shanghai," the analyst told clients.

Thanks to robust data center demand, Tesla's energy business is already sold out for 2027, and the investment firm expects that to drive more than 50% growth in shipments over the longer term.

The final pillar of Levy's bullish view on Tesla shares is the company's robotaxi business that he's convinced is strongly positioned to go up against Waymo.

news.Title: Billionaire predicts 'unhinged' future for iPhone Duo
news.Content:
Last week, Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) released its first foldable smartphone, iPhone Duo. The smartphone's 7.6-inch inner display, when unfolded, is its most talked about feature.

In fact, it's the largest display in any iPhone so far and billionaire entrepreneur Changpeng Zhao thinks many iPhones will be "unhinged" by "crypto trenchers."

Zhao says Duo is 'pretty good for charting'

Zhao is the cofounder of Binance , the world's largest crypto trading exchange. In June, the company said the total number of registered Binance users worldwide has exceeded 300 million.

While trading of nearly all the assets, including equities, commodities, government bonds, etc., can take place on smartphones now, crypto trading was born in an age when these mobile devices were reaching the hands of common people.

But trading on a smartphone is not the smoothest experience and the most challenging part is looking at long-term price charts on a narrow screen.

It's not uncommon for serious crypto traders to keep two or three computer screens open at the same time.

There is the asset's price chart, the latest market news, a rival asset's performance to compare, and so much more to look at when placing an order. A smartphone is just not built to accommodate these demands.

But Zhao thinks the iPhone Duo will be widely used by crypto traders who will go "unhinged."

Most Popular on TheStreet Roundtable:

Warren Buffett once offered $25 for all Bitcoin. Here's its value now

Microsoft, Google parent and McDonald's protest new trading plan

The smartphone's 7.6-inch display can offer a convenient way to look at the long-term price chart of cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH), XRP , etc.

While the iPhone Duo can't replace a multi-display computer system that crypto traders are so fond of, the smartphone is certainly handy for traders on the move.

In fact, Zhao last month shared a screenshot of the device showing a BNB/USDT trading pair on the Binance exchange and said the "Duo is pretty good for charting."

The iPhone Duo (256GB) costs $1,999 in the U.S. With Bitcoin currently trading at $80,600, an American crypto trader will have to let go of 0.025 BTC to purchase a Duo.

news.Title: Tesla's Full Self-Driving Business Is Growing Fast. But There's a Catch for Investors
news.Content:
Tesla 's (NASDAQ:TSLA) difficult year continues. On Oct. 21, the company released its third-quarter earnings, and the market wasn't that impressed. Tesla's shares dropped by about 3% post-earnings, adding to the significant market losses it had already incurred this year.

However, Tesla's latest quarterly update wasn't all bad. There were positive signs for the business, including the company's commercial progress with its Full Self-Driving (FSD) software. Let's look deeper into it.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

The FSD software is growing in popularity

Tesla's third-quarter deliveries were very strong. Total deliveries came in at 486,532. Although that declined 2% year over year, it was well ahead of the consensus analyst estimates.

However, the deliveries beat was already baked into the share price before Tesla reported its third-quarter results, since the company announces quarterly deliveries weeks before its update.

Why, then, did Tesla's shares fall after its earnings update? Because the company's actual financial performance was mixed. Vehicle sales declined 3% year over year, and total revenue was roughly flat at $28 billion.

Also, Tesla's non-GAAP net earnings per share dropped by 4% year over year to $0.48. Despite the mixed performance, Tesla made progress in some categories. The company's increasingly popular FSD software was one of them. Active FSD subscriptions grew 67% year over year during the period, reaching 1.74 million.

Tesla charges $99 per month in the U.S. for these subscriptions. The 1.74 million total includes people who purchased the subscription upfront (an option Tesla no longer offers). According to management, the FSD subscription now boasts an annual run rate approaching $1 billion.

That's a tiny percentage of the company's total revenue, but there are several reasons this business is particularly important to Tesla. First, FSD subscription sales likely carry higher margins than electric vehicle (EV) sales.

So, as FSD subscription revenue continues to grow, it could help lift the company's profits, even if it doesn't match EV sales. Second, as Tesla notes, the FSD software is actually helping the company deliver more vehicles.

It seems many customers are increasingly buying Tesla vehicles partly because of the benefits of the FSD software.

Story Continues

In the third quarter, Tesla's FSD attach rate -- the percentage of new buyers who also sign up for the FSD subscription -- reached over 75% in North America, growing nearly 20 percentage points sequentially.

Third, an increasing number of FSD subscriptions should help the company improve its software over the medium term. The more Teslas on the road that run the FSD software, the more data the company has from real-world situations to train and improve the software.

This data flywheel will have important implications for Tesla's entire business. Not only could it help the company sell more EVs, but it may also enable it to improve its robotaxi service.

Is there significant upside ahead?

Even with unimpressive EV sales over the next five years, Tesla's business may improve, provided the company makes substantial progress with its robotaxi business. Tesla launched the Cybercab, a two-seater with no mirrors, steering wheel, or pedals, in September.

The company will be looking to scale its Cybercab fleet over the next few years, and its FSD software will be a key part of its strategy. Assuming a large robotaxi fleet and significant utilization, this business may start contributing meaningfully to the company's revenue growth.

However, there are several risks to consider. First, despite a strong FSD attach rate, the retention rate will be just as important. Tesla does not disclose this metric, but even if the majority of new Tesla buyers opt for the FSD software, it won't be quite as lucrative a revenue stream if a significant number cancel it later. Second, Tesla still has plenty of work to do to scale its robotaxi fleet, and it will need to overcome various regulatory headwinds.

The company was the subject of a federal safety investigation after launching the Cybercab, underscoring that this poses a meaningful risk to the company. Third, and perhaps most importantly, Tesla's valuation seems to already assume significant success across its various projects.

The company is trading at 149.3x forward earnings, which seems incredibly high. Tesla will have to exceed expectations to deliver competitive returns from current levels over the next five years. That's certainly possible, so the upside potential is there. But there is also enough uncertainty to make me a skeptic. That's why I'd avoid Tesla stock right now.

news.Title: Move Over, Tesla: This Robotics Stock Is the Better Buy
news.Content:
The U.S. has nearly 300 robots per 10,000 manufacturing workers, and the International Federation of Robotics projects that figure could rise as re-shoring pushes domestic factories to become more productive and globally competitive.

Headlines around robotics tend to focus on flashy humanoids like Tesla 's (NASDAQ: TSLA) Optimus. However, Optimus faces real manufacturing and technical hurdles, and the bigger transformation is already underway on factory floors.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Rockwell Automation (NYSE: ROK) supplies the critical hardware and software that power this shift, making it a compelling "pick-and-shovel" play on the robotics boom. Here's why Rockwell could be a better buy than Tesla right now.

Tesla's Optimus is in very early production stages

Tesla first rolled out its Optimus robots in a 2021 demonstration and has since unveiled several prototypes with mixed results. CEO Elon Musk believes Optimus will become the biggest product ever .

During its third-quarter earnings call, Musk said the company has converted part of its former EV manufacturing space at its Fremont facility to build the first batch of Optimus units. Tesla won't begin delivering its Optimus robots until at least the end of 2027, and many are skeptical the robot will be ready by then.

Rockwell Automation is a key player in factory automation

While Tesla develops Optimus, Rockwell Automation has been developing the electrical components, software, and equipment that form the backbone of modern industrial plants for decades.

The company's offerings include programmable logic controllers, which manage high-speed machinery and automation systems. It also provides motion control, drives, actuators, safety switches, and software to manage industrial processes. Its products ultimately help connect data across an organization, enabling industrial operators to achieve faster production times and greater efficiency.

In Rockwell's third quarter (ended June 30), the company reported sales of $2.3 billion, an 8% year-over-year increase. Adjusted earnings per share rose 22% to $3.49, and the operating margin rose to 22.3% due to higher sales volume and a more favorable sales mix.

The company is seeing very strong growth in certain customer subsets, including e-commerce, warehouse automation, and data centers, with particularly strong growth in North America. One major driver for Rockwell's growth is the reshoring of U.S. manufacturing.

Story Continues

CEO Blake Moret noted that reestablishing domestic production requires a trained workforce along with advanced automation technology, and that "America continues to be interested in bringing more manufacturing on board."

Rockwell Automation is a pick-and-shovel investment in robotics

Rockwell Automation isn't a high-flying growth stock with pie-in-the-sky projections. But it provides the backbone of factory automation and is well-positioned to support the reshoring of domestic manufacturing in the U.S.

If you're seeking exposure to the growing use of robotics and the U.S. reshoring theme, Rockwell Automation is a solid stock to buy today.

news.Title: Apple Reveals Biggest iPad Overhaul Yet
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) has unveiled its biggest iPad mini upgrade yet , introducing an OLED display, a powerful A20 Pro processor, and expanded artificial intelligence capabilities. However, the revamped tablet comes with a substantially higher starting price of $699, putting Apple's premium pricing strategy under the spotlight as investors assess demand for its latest devices.

Is AAPL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The redesigned iPad mini features an 8.5-inch OLED display, up from the previous generation's 8.3-inch screen, with more than twice the peak brightness.

Apple also equipped the tablet with its latest A20 Pro chip, built on 2-nanometer technology, which the company claims delivers up to 4.5 times faster AI performance and 60% faster multithreaded CPU performance compared with its predecessor.

Other improvements include IP67 water and dust resistance, a thinner 5.4-millimeter design, a 12-megapixel front camera, and faster wireless connectivity.

The tablet runs iPadOS 27, bringing upgraded Apple Intelligence features and a revamped Siri with greater contextual awareness.

However, the biggest surprise may be the price.

At $699, the new iPad mini costs $200 more than the previous generation's original $499 launch price , representing a 40% increase.

That premium suggests Apple is increasingly emphasizing higher-value hardware and AI capabilities rather than competing aggressively on price.

Preorders begin October 28, with availability starting November 6. The cellular model starts at $849.

What investors should watch next

For Apple shareholders, the launch presents another test of whether consumers are willing to pay more for meaningful hardware upgrades.

The immediate catalyst is Apple's November 2 fiscal fourth-quarter earnings report, where investors should watch iPad revenue, product gross margins, and management's outlook for the holiday quarter.

Importantly, the new tablet launches after the September quarter, meaning its initial sales will affect subsequent results.

Strong demand could support Apple's premium-device strategy and average selling prices, while resistance to the higher price could limit upgrades.

The bigger question is whether Apple Intelligence can become a compelling reason for consumers to replace otherwise functional devices.

news.Title: How to Play Amazon Stock Before Q3 Earnings as the AI Trade Flounders
news.Content:
The Q3 2026 earnings season for "Magnificent 7" stocks is looking a lot like the previous quarter. In a reminiscence of the Q2 earnings season, both Tesla (TSLA) and Meta Platforms (META) plunged following their respective Q3 earnings last week, taking down the entire artificial intelligence (AI) universe with them. The earnings season gains pace this week, with Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), and Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) releasing their September quarter reports.

Tech Stocks Have Weakened as AI Trade Flounders

In the last earnings season, Microsoft gained the most among its Mag 7 peers following its confessional. The stock continued to build on the gains and rose an impressive 38% in Q3, clocking its best quarter since 1998. It went on to hit its record closing high last Tuesday and reclaimed its $4 trillion market cap before earnings from fellow Mag 7 companies dampened sentiment.

More News from Barchart

Amazon's story has been a bit different from Microsoft's, and it failed to hold onto its post-Q2 earnings gains. In a previous article, I noted that investors shouldn't expect a big rally in MSFT stock following its fiscal Q1 2027 earnings. Let's dive into how to play Amazon stock as the AI trade flounders.

What to Expect From Q3 Earnings

Amazon guided for Q3 revenues to rise between 9% and 12% year-over-year (YoY). Analysts are modelling the company's Q3 earnings per share (EPS) to rise 30.8%. During the Q3 earnings call, enterprise-focused Amazon Web Services (AWS) and the AI business, including the chip segment, would garner most attention. However, I would also watch the commentary on consumer health, given the deteriorating macro environment. Consumers globally have been hurting from higher inflation, particularly elevated energy prices, which is taking a toll on discretionary spending. To make things worse, interest rates are on an upward trajectory, hurting the monthly budgets of many middle-and-lower income families.

How Do Analysts Rate AMZN Stock Before Q3 Earnings?

Sell-side analysts have mostly made cursory adjustments to Amazon's target price—both on the upside and downside—ahead of its Q3 earnings. There have been some notable changes, though. For instance, famed tech analyst Dan Ives initiated coverage on Amazon at his recently formed Yorkville Ives with an "Outperform" rating and a $300 target price, while Tigress Financial analyst Ivan Feinseth raised the stock's target price from $315 to $385.

Story Continues

Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Nowak named Amazon as a Top Pick and believes AI could drive AWS revenues to over $1 trillion. As a note of caution, Amazon has been a "top pick" for analysts for the last few years, but the stock hasn't been able to live up to expectations. AMZN stock is up around 47% over the last five years, which trails not only the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index ($IUXX) but also the more diversified S&P 500 Index ($SPX). In fact, among its Mag 7 peers, AMZN is the second-worst performer and has fared better than only Tesla, whose shares are almost flat over the period.

How to Play Amazon Stock?

I have been bullish on Amazon stock this year and maintain my stance as the Andy Jassy-led company heads into its Q3 confessional. There are legit concerns about agentic AI negatively impacting Amazon's lucrative digital advertising business, and the company's once-enviable free cash flows are falling prey to burgeoning AI capex. Furthermore, the growth in the company's e-commerce operations in developed markets has slowed.

I, however, believe the risks are overblown and markets are overlooking the AI opportunity, including from third-party chip sales. In the e-commerce business, competition from the likes of Walmart (WMT) is rising, but Amazon has built an enviable ecosystem that is challenging to emulate.

Amazon's business has several moving parts, like Prime and digital advertising, that complement each other. Despite concerns about some aspects of its business, Amazon has a reasonably strong outlook, with AI being an enabler of both topline and bottomline growth.

In terms of valuation, AMZN stock trades at 23.2x its expected 2027 EPS, which is quite attractive. I remain invested in Amazon and believe the recent weakness in the stock, coupled with tepid valuations, raises the possibility of a post-earnings rally unless the company comes up with dud numbers.

news.Title: Anthropic makes more per employee than every Magnificent Seven company but Nvidia
news.Content:
Anthropic's headcount nearly tripled in a year. Its revenue grew 13x.

That pushed the AI lab's revenue per employee over the past year to more than $6.6 million, up from $1.4 million a year earlier, according to the IPO prospectus it filed Monday . Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) had about 5,300 employees as of Sept. 30.

Only Nvidia does better

Nvidia ( NVDA ) brings in about $7.2 million per employee, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Meta ( META ) is at $3.6 million. Apple ( AAPL ), at $3.1 million, brings in less than half as much per worker as Anthropic. Amazon ( AMZN ), with more than 1.5 million workers, is at $0.5 million.

This measures sales, not profit. Warehouses and retail stores swell Amazon's and Apple's payrolls. And Anthropic rents most of its computing, so many of the people running its data centers work for Google and Amazon .

The prospectus credits Claude, its AI model, for some of the leanness. More than 90% of the code added to Anthropic's codebase in September was written by Claude, the company said. That helped revenue climb from $41 million in all of 2023 to $16.3 billion in just the first half of 2026.

Investors are paying up for it

At the $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion valuation reportedly under discussion for its IPO, Anthropic would be worth $283 million to $377 million per employee. That's two to three times Nvidia's $121 million, a figure that has drawn attention of its own . Palantir ( PLTR ) is at $107 million and SpaceX ( SPCX ) at $95 million.

The price range in an updated filing will set the real number. Near $2 trillion, investors would be paying close to three times Nvidia's rate per worker. Even at the low end, Anthropic would top every company on the chart.

Apple's Products segment generated $78.7 billion in revenue in the third quarter, up 18% year over year. Strong demand for the iPhone and Mac drove growth, with both recording double-digit revenue gains. iPhone revenue rose 22% year over year to $54.3 billion, supported by the iPhone 17 lineup. The company also reported growth across most major markets, while its active iPhone installed base hit a record high, led by a record June quarter for customers upgrading their devices.

Mac revenue increased 29% year over year to $10.4 billion, driven by solid demand for the MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro.

Despite this positive momentum, product-related growth is expected to decelerate in the fourth quarter. Management said during the Q3 earnings call that supply constraints would intensify significantly sequentially, affecting product availability. Consequently, Apple guided total company revenue growth of 9%-11% year over year in the September quarter, down from 16% in Q3.

The iPhone segment is expected to remain a primary revenue contributor, supported by sustained consumer demand. Nevertheless, supply limitations are likely to restrict the conversion of demand into reported sales. Management anticipated mid-teens year-over-year iPhone revenue growth for the September quarter, below the 22% increase recorded in the preceding quarter.

Story Continues

Apple's Services business generated $30.7 billion in Q3 revenue, an increase of 12% year over year. The segment is expected to maintain its growth momentum, supported by broad-based contributions from advertising, the App Store, AppleCare, Apple Music, and Apple TV+. Cloud-related offerings and payment services are also expected to drive revenue growth.

Apple's expanding installed base is a significant competitive advantage. The company reported about 2.5 billion active devices at the end of Q3, creating a substantial customer ecosystem it can monetize through subscriptions, digital content, advertising, payment solutions, and cloud storage. Further expansion of this installed base in Q4 could increase the number of potential service customers and deepen engagement with existing users.

Apple's fourth-quarter earnings will benefit from higher revenue and favorable pricing. However, elevated memory costs may constrain margin expansion. Conversely, lower costs for certain non-memory components could partially offset these pressures.

Analysts expect Apple to report Q4 earnings per share of $2, an 8.1% year-over-year increase. The iPhone maker has exceeded analysts' EPS expectations for four consecutive quarters, reflecting consistent earnings outperformance.

Valuation and Supply Risks Could Limit AAPL Stock's Upside

While Apple's strong iPhone demand, resilient Services business, and favorable pricing are expected to support Q4 earnings growth, intensifying supply constraints and rising memory costs could temper revenue momentum and profitability.

With the stock already up 27.9% year to date and trading near its all-time high, expectations appear elevated, leaving limited room for disappointment. Although Apple's track record of earnings beats is encouraging, investors should exercise caution ahead of the earnings release, as solid results may not drive further gains.

With AAPL stock trading at a forward earnings multiple of 36.3, which is high relative to its earnings growth potential, analysts have a "Moderate Buy" consensus rating.

news.Title: Not AMD. Not Marvell. Here's Which Company Nvidia Needs to Be Worried About.
news.Content:
Nvidia holds the title for the largest market share in the artificial intelligence (AI) computing unit market. Its GPUs have become synonymous with AI computing power, but it's not without competition.

One of the more obvious picks is Advanced Micro Devices , as it also makes GPUs. However, AMD's data center division is far smaller than Nvidia's and also grew at a slower rate during its most recent quarters.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

However, GPUs aren't the only way AI computing is done. While GPUs are incredibly flexible and can do a lot of tasks, they aren't optimized for any one workload. There are many tasks that need to be done on a repetitive basis in the AI world, and a specialized computing unit can thrive in these tasks.

This is where I see the biggest threat to Nvidia's business, and there are two key players in this industry.

Custom AI chips are expected to become more popular in the future

The two primary custom AI chip firms are Marvell and Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO). Marvell's primary clients are Microsoft and Amazon , while Broadcom has partnered with Alphabet , Meta Platforms , Anthropic, and OpenAI. Marvell and Broadcom are very similar to AMD and Nvidia. While Marvell has the business and is competing, it doesn't have the size. Marvell's AI data center revenue totaled $2.1 billion in Q2.

Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue reached $16.7 billion. Broadcom is the company to beat in this industry, and I think it's one that Nvidia actually needs to worry about.

The crown jewel of Broadcom's custom AI chip empire is Google's Tensor Processing Unit (TPU), a device that Broadcom and Alphabet have collaborated on for a long time. These units have gone through several generations and are even starting to be sold on the market by Alphabet because there's such high demand for them. Broadcom's other clients will look to recreate these units optimized for their own workloads, and Broadcom will benefit significantly from growth in this area.

This year, they estimate their AI segment revenue will be around $58 billion. However, that figure is expected to reach $115 billion in 2027 and $230 billion in 2028. For reference, Nvidia expects its 2027 revenue growth to be about 70% so that Broadcom will be growing at a slower pace. This points to Broadcom taking market share from Nvidia as the build-out grows. Still, it will never fully replace Nvidia, as GPUs are useful in many situations that custom AI chips aren't.

Story Continues

This leaves a major market open for both stocks, although Broadcom may be in a better position to capture more business. However, its stock isn't really pricing in any growth for 2027.

Broadcom's stock isn't expensive

Broadcom currently trades at 43 times trailing earnings, which isn't super cheap. However, it doesn't price in the massive growth it's expected to undergo next year.

AVGO PE Ratio data by YCharts

With the shares trading at 17 times next year's earnings estimates, it shows the market expects huge growth. If Broadcom rose to 35 times earnings by the end of next fiscal year, it would indicate that the stock has the potential to double.

That's a solid return in a short time frame, but remember, Broadcom also said it would double its revenue base again in 2028. That means there are multiple years of strong returns ahead for Broadcom. With it gaining new clients in the AI sector, there's a lot of opportunity for Broadcom to firmly establish itself alongside Nvidia as a major leader in the AI computing space . As a result, I think it's a smart buy now.

news.Title: Intel and TSMC Are Vying for Chip Fabrication Supremacy. 1 Offers Superior Value.
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) (NYSE: TSM) and Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) are two major names in the chip fabrication world. However, Taiwan Semiconductor has a monster lead that cannot be overstated. Intel used to be a major player, but because it let its technology slip, clients gradually moved their business to other foundries, namely TSMC.

However, with recent investments from Nvidia and the U.S. government, Intel's chip foundry business looks to be back in action. There is a major market shift that could happen over the next few years, but which stock is best positioned to capitalize on it? Let's take a look.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Intel is seeing strong growth

Intel splits its business into two parts: Intel Foundry and Intel Products. Intel products include the devices that it makes, like CPUs, and it is split into two divisions: Client Computing and the Physical AI Group, and Data Center and AI. This is not what's coming against TSMC, but it is doing pretty good growth figures, with revenue rising 28% year over year to $15.1 billion. Still, it's good to know in the context of Intel as a whole, as an investment in Intel also acquires these segments, not just its foundry business.

Intel's foundry business has steadily improved and generated revenue of $5.8 billion, up 31% year over year. So, it's a lot smaller of a business unit than its products. However, if Intel's foundry business can continue acquiring clients, this could be the start of a major growth trend.

However, it's much smaller in size than TSMC. TSMC is only a foundry company, so it should only be compared to that division from Intel. In Q3, its revenue totaled $46.7 billion, up 41% year over year. We're still waiting on Intel's Q3 results, so if we rewind the clock to Q2, TSMC grew at a 34% year over year pace to $40.2 billion.

So, if Q2 results are used, TSMC and Intel are about on the same level in terms of growth, although TSMC has a notable size advantage.

But there is one glaring difference that investors cannot miss: profitability. Right now, Intel is fighting to get its foundry business back to profitability. In Q2, its operating margin was a pretty sad 36% loss. On the flip side, TSMC's operating profit margin was 59%.

So, Intel's Foundry business is currently a major loss leader for the company, while TSMC has achieved an incredible level. I think this is something notable to keep in mind, as it helps put the valuation of the two in context.

Story Continues

Intel looks incredibly expensive right now

The most commonly used metric investors use to value stock is the price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio. While it works in some situations, it's terrible for Intel because its foundry business is deeply unprofitable right now. However, if we shift the focus from now to next year, Intel's profitability is expected to improve, which brings its P/E ratio into a more comparable range.

TSM PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts

If 2027's earnings estimates are used, Intel trades at 44 times future earnings while TSMC is only at 18. That's a huge price mismatch, and points to TSMC providing superior value versus Intel. The reality is that Intel's stock has done very well in 2026. However, its turnaround is far from complete, even if the market has already declared it a winner.

While I'm rooting for an Intel turnaround, I don't need to invest in its stock . Instead, picking Taiwan Semiconductor makes far more sense, as it is reasonably priced and is already where Intel is trying to go.

Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

news.Title: Verizon Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates on Strong Margins, Revenues Miss
news.Content:
Verizon Communications Inc. VZ reported adjusted earnings of $1.31 per share in the third quarter of 2026, up 8.3% year over year and ahead of the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.27 by 3.15%.

Total operating revenues increased 1.5% year over year to $34.31 billion but missed the consensus mark of $34.81 billion by 1.43%. Strong service revenue growth, improved operating efficiency and robust subscriber additions supported profitability. Verizon delivered 406,000 postpaid phone net additions, its strongest third-quarter performance in five years.

Verizon Communications Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Verizon Communications Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Verizon Communications Inc. Quote

Service Revenues Grow Despite Equipment Weakness

Service revenues and other increased 3.5% year over year to $29.20 billion, supported by improving mobility and broadband trends. Wireless equipment revenues declined 9% to $5.12 billion, reflecting reduced upgrade activity and disciplined promotional spending.

Mobility and broadband service revenues reached $23.5 billion, increasing 2.9% year over year compared with 2.8% growth in the preceding quarter. Management attributed lower equipment sales to customers retaining devices longer and its strategy of reducing handset subsidies.

Consumer Segment Benefits From Service Growth

Consumer operating revenues increased 1.3% year over year to $26.43 billion. Mobility and broadband service revenues rose 3.6% to $19.78 billion, while wireless equipment revenues declined 10.3% to $4.28 billion. Other revenues grew 6% to $2.38 billion.

Consumer operating income improved 5.6% to $8.09 billion, with the operating margin expanding to 30.6% from 29.4%. Segment EBITDA increased 6.5% to $11.97 billion, while the corresponding margin improved 230 basis points to 45.3%.

Business Segment Records Higher Profitability

Business operating revenues rose 2.6% year over year to $7.02 billion. Mobility and broadband service revenues declined 0.8% to $3.71 billion, while wireless equipment revenues fell 1.6% to $839 million. Other revenues increased 10% to $2.47 billion.

Business operating income climbed 19.4% to $855 million, supported by lower selling, general and administrative expenses. Segment EBITDA advanced 13% to $1.94 billion, with the corresponding margin expanding to 27.6% from 25.1%.

Margins Expand Through Cost Discipline

Total operating expenses declined 0.2% year over year to $25.66 billion. Selling, general and administrative expenses decreased 3.5% to $7.48 billion, while wireless equipment costs fell 10.2%. However, depreciation and amortization expenses increased 10.3% to $5.10 billion.

Operating income rose 6.7% to $8.65 billion. Consolidated net income increased 5.2% to $5.32 billion, while net income attributable to Verizon improved 5% to $5.20 billion. Adjusted EBITDA increased 8% to a record $13.80 billion, with the adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 240 basis points to 40.2%. Interest expenses increased 17.2% to $1.95 billion.

Story Continues

Wireless Gains Offset Slower Broadband Additions

Verizon added 137,000 postpaid accounts, its best quarterly performance in more than a decade. Retail postpaid phone churn improved four basis points year over year to 0.94%, while Consumer postpaid phone churn declined to 0.87%.

Broadband net additions totaled 314,000, down from 322,000 a year earlier. Fiber broadband additions reached 155,000, while fixed wireless access contributed 159,000. Total broadband connections reached 17.4 million. The company also announced an agreement valued at more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services to support AI infrastructure.

Cash Flow Strengthens Shareholder Returns

Third-quarter operating cash flow increased 2.2% year over year to $11.52 billion, while free cash flow improved 12.1% to $7.80 billion. Capital expenditures totaled $3.72 billion, compared with $4.31 billion a year earlier.

For the first nine months, free cash flow increased 14.3% to $18.01 billion. Verizon returned $12.8 billion to shareholders through dividends and repurchases. Net unsecured debt stood at $123.72 billion, down from $128.68 billion in the preceding quarter. Net unsecured debt to adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially to 2.3 times.

VZ Raises 2026 Earnings and Subscriber Outlook

Verizon raised its 2026 adjusted earnings guidance to $5.04-$5.06 per share, implying 7%-7.5% year-over-year growth, compared with its previous projection of 6%-7%.

The company increased its postpaid phone net additions forecast to 1.1 million-1.2 million. Mobility and broadband service revenue growth is expected in the upper half of the 2.5%-3% range, while free cash flow growth is projected to approach 12%. Capital expenditure guidance remains unchanged at $16-$16.5 billion.

news.Title: 1 Unstoppable Stock-Split Stock to Buy Before It Joins Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Apple in the $3 Trillion Club
news.Content:
A high-quality company will typically create tremendous long-term value, sending its stock price soaring into the hundreds or even thousands of dollars. As a result, investors with small portfolios could find themselves priced out of owning one full share, which is why the company might decide to execute a stock split.

Stock splits work by increasing the number of shares in circulation, which reduces the price per share by a proportionate amount. The adjustment is entirely cosmetic, so it doesn't change the value of the underlying company. Facebook parent Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) just announced it will execute the equivalent of a 2-for-1 split by introducing a new class of shares.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Investors who currently own a single Meta Class A share worth $650 will end up with two shares after the record date: one Class A share with voting rights, and one Class C share with no voting rights, presumably worth $325 each. The prices I've described are merely hypothetical, because we don't know where Meta will be trading when the split eventually happens in January 2027.

In any case, Meta is likely to continue creating substantial value for investors over the long term. The company has a market capitalization of $1.65 trillion as I write this (Oct. 23), but here's why I think it could cross the $3 trillion milestone within the next few years, joining an exclusive club that currently only includes Nvidia , Alphabet , Microsoft , and Apple .

Artificial intelligence is transforming Meta's social media apps

Meta's portfolio of social media apps includes Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp, and Threads. During the third quarter of 2026 (ended Sept. 30), a record 3.64 billion people used at least one of them every single day. That number represents almost half of the world's population, so it's getting harder for the company to find new users, especially sincee its apps are banned in populous countries like China.

As a result, Meta is focusing on engagement instead. If each existing user spends more time online, they will see more ads and generate more revenue for the company. Artificial intelligence (AI) plays a central role in this strategy by powering Meta's recommendation algorithms. It learns what type of content users like to see and shows them more of it to keep them locked in. It's working, because chief executive Mark Zuckerberg said engagement hit new record highs on Facebook and Instagram during the third quarter.

Story Continues

But Meta's AI strategy is evolving beyond social media entirely. The company launched a personal AI agent called Muse in September, and it has already attracted more than 10 million users. Zuckerberg says more than one-quarter of them are using it as a personal shopper, with an average purchase size of $200. Managing emails and calendars are other common use cases so far.

Zuckerberg wants Muse to eventually serve billions of people, who he hopes will use it to improve every facet of their lives -- whether they want relationship advice or want help building a business. This will significantly expand Meta's addressable market by creating an opportunity to divert internet traffic from entrenched platforms like Google Search.

Meta is growing rapidly, but AI spending is becoming a headwind

Meta generated $64.6 billion in total revenue during the third quarter, a 26% increase from the year-ago period. It was a strong result, but the company's bottom line is drawing more attention right now.

Meta spent $72 billion on building AI data centers in 2025, and it's on track to spend up to $145 billion this year. Capital expenditures can't be deducted up front because data centers have a useful life of several years, so the company has to depreciate the infrastructure over time. That means the money it spends today will affect its earnings in 2027, 2028, 2029, and beyond.

The impacts are already showing up, because Meta's third-quarter expenses soared by 68% year over year to $51.6 billion. That included a $9.9 billion charge from a legal settlement, but most of the growth was driven by AI infrastructure costs, including depreciation, cloud spending, and data center operations.

Meta still delivered a generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) profit of $9.8 billion during the quarter, more than tripling from the year-ago period -- but only because the company took a one-time tax hit of $15.9 billion in the third quarter of 2025. Without that, Meta's recent Q3 result would have represented a year-over-year decline of 47%.

Meta's mathematical path to the $3 trillion club

Based on Meta's trailing 12-month GAAP earnings of $29.33 per share, its stock is trading at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of just 22.1. The Nasdaq-100 index has a P/E ratio of 30.2, so Meta looks heavily undervalued compared to a basket of its big-tech peers.

Moreover, Wall Street's average forecast (provided by Yahoo Finance) suggests Meta's earnings could grow modestly to $33.82 per share in 2027, placing its stock at a forward P/E ratio of 18.7.

META PE Ratio data by YCharts

That suggests Meta stock would have to soar by 61% over the next 12 months or so just to match the P/E of the Nasdaq-100, which is possible given its P/E was over 30 for a significant part of the last decade. That alone would see Meta's market cap rise to $2.66 trillion, so even modest revenue growth of 13.5% in 2028 would be enough to justify a $3 trillion valuation.

There is no guarantee Meta's P/E will rise to 30.2, but I think it could get there if it shows a phenomenal return on investment on its AI infrastructure spending through the continued success of products like Muse. Alternatively, pulling back on capital expenditures would significantly prop up its earnings, and this is a strategy Zuckerberg used in 2022 when the company's virtual reality spending was getting out of hand.

Nevertheless, even if Meta doesn't join the $3 trillion club by 2028, I think it's likely to get there in the long run.

news.Title: Is TSMC (TSM) a Buy as Wall Street Analysts Look Optimistic?
news.Content:
The recommendations of Wall Street analysts are often relied on by investors when deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock. Media reports about these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts changing their ratings often affect a stock's price. Do they really matter, though?

Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about TSMC (TSM) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage.

TSMC currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.21, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 19 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.21 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 19 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 16 are Strong Buy and two are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 84.2% and 10.5% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for TSM

Check price target & stock forecast for TSMC here>>>

While the ABR calls for buying TSMC, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential.

Do you wonder why? As a result of the vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover, their analysts tend to rate it with a strong positive bias. According to our research, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations for every "Strong Sell" recommendation.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures.

The ABR is calculated solely based on brokerage recommendations and is typically displayed with decimals (example: 1.28). In contrast, the Zacks Rank is a quantitative model allowing investors to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Story Continues

Analysts employed by brokerage firms have been and continue to be overly optimistic with their recommendations. Since the ratings issued by these analysts are more favorable than their research would support because of the vested interest of their employers, they mislead investors far more often than they guide.

In contrast, the Zacks Rank is driven by earnings estimate revisions. And near-term stock price movements are strongly correlated with trends in earnings estimate revisions, according to empirical research.

Furthermore, the different grades of the Zacks Rank are applied proportionately across all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide earnings estimates for the current year. In other words, at all times, this tool maintains a balance among the five ranks it assigns.

There is also a key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank when it comes to freshness. When you look at the ABR, it may not be up-to-date. Nonetheless, since brokerage analysts constantly revise their earnings estimates to reflect changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in predicting future stock prices.

Is TSM Worth Investing In?

Looking at the earnings estimate revisions for TSMC, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 3.1% over the past month to $17.07.

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term.

The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) for TSMC. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>>

Therefore, the Buy-equivalent ABR for TSMC may serve as a useful guide for investors.

news.Title: The 10 biggest stocks are faltering, and it's dragging the S&P 500 down
news.Content: Apple ( AAPL ) and Nvidia ( NVDA ) may be renewing their battle for the world's most valuable company, but a challenging few months for the S&P 500's ( ^GSPC ) 10 largest companies are holding back the broader index. The 10 biggest stocks in the S&P 500 have started to falter again relative to the rest of the market, RBC strategist Lori Calvasina rightly pointed out in a new note. These 10 stocks include Apple, Nvidia, Amazon ( AMZN ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), the two classes of Alphabet ( GOOGL ) ( GOOG ) stock, Micron ( MU ), Meta ( META ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Tesla ( TSLA ). Their stutter step weighs on the overall stock market given their weight in the benchmark index. Calvasina said she remains on the sidelines with tech, which she downgraded to a Market Weight rating earlier this month. Mounting investor skepticism about the timeline for AI return on investment has triggered severe rotation and pullbacks in megacap tech, preventing the broader market from breaking out. Consider this: Former market leader Nvidia is down about 13% from its all-time highs, while Tesla is off by 26%. Double-digit declines relative to their highs are also in play for Amazon, Alphabet, Google and SpaceX. The latest earnings from Meta and SpaceX only fanned investors' fears, with each reporting negative free cash flow and outlining aggressive AI spending plans. Amid rising oil prices and portfolio de-risking ahead of November's midterm elections, institutional investors have remained in a "wait-and-see" mode rather than chasing stocks near all-time highs. "We've been max Overweight stocks and max Underweight sovereign bonds since mid-March. Given the constant narrative bingo we just can't have the same level of conviction any longer. Heading into the mid-terms there may well be worries about AI regulation in the event of a 'Blue Wave' as well as renewed geopolitical concerns around the Middle East," HSBC strategist Max Kettner wrote in a new note on Monday. news.Title: Apple Inc. (AAPL) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
news.Content:
Apple (AAPL) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Shares of this maker of iPhones, iPads and other products have returned +2% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -1.2% change. The Zacks Computer - Micro Computers industry, to which Apple belongs, has gained 1.2% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Apple is expected to post earnings of $2.00 per share, indicating a change of +8.1% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -1% over the last 30 days.

The consensus earnings estimate of $8.86 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +18.8%. This estimate has changed +0.7% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $9.6 indicates a change of +8.4% from what Apple is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +0.3%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, Apple is rated Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Projected Revenue Growth

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.

In the case of Apple, the consensus sales estimate of $112.95 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +10.2%. The $477.34 billion and $521.76 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +14.7% and +9.3%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Apple reported revenues of $109.42 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +16.4%. EPS of $1.91 for the same period compares with $1.57 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $108.75 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +0.62%. The EPS surprise was +1.6%.

The company beat consensus EPS estimates in each of the trailing four quarters. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

Without considering a stock's valuation, no investment decision can be efficient. In predicting a stock's future price performance, it's crucial to determine whether its current price correctly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

As part of the Zacks Style Scores system, the Zacks Value Style Score (which evaluates both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics) organizes stocks into five groups ranging from A to F (A is better than B; B is better than C; and so on), making it helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Apple is graded F on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Bottom Line

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Apple. However, its Zacks Rank #3 does suggest that it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: Chip Stocks to Buy After Their Worst Day Since June
news.Content:
Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX), which sells chipmaking equipment, reported record revenue on Oct. 21. It also said limited clean-room space and shortages of some parts would stop chipmakers and equipment companies from fully meeting demand into 2027.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index dropped 6.7% on Oct. 22, its worst day since June 23. Lam lost 12%, Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) 6%, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) 8%, and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) 9%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But Lam was describing more demand than the industry can meet, not less. And all three chipmakers' own outlooks still point up. I think the sell-off makes all three worth buying.

Image source: Getty Images.

Lam's issue is supply, not demand

Lam's revenue rose 22% from the June quarter to $8.22 billion, up 54% year over year. And management still forecast around $8.6 billion in the December quarter.

"[T]his revenue guide would have been a bit higher if not for some near-term supply chain constraints," CFO Doug Bettinger said on the earnings call.

Lam also expects industry spending on chipmaking equipment to pass $200 billion in 2027, up from the mid-$150 billion range this year. Asked what that number would be without the constraints, Bettinger said it "would be higher."

Micron: short on clean rooms, not customers

On Sept. 30, memory maker Micron said industry supply of DRAM and NAND (the two main kinds of memory chips) should stay constrained in 2027 and 2028.

"We expect memory and storage supply-demand conditions to be much tighter in calendar 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026," CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said in prepared remarks for that day's call.

Showing what tight supply has done for Micron, its revenue rose 31% sequentially to $54.2 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter of 2026 (which ended Sept. 3), as DRAM prices climbed by a high-teens percentage and NAND prices by about 30%. Management expects another record in the fiscal first quarter of 2027, at roughly $61.5 billion, and to grow in every quarter of fiscal 2027. But the stock is off 29% from its June 25 record close, at about $856 as I write, or about 5 times earnings for fiscal 2027 on analysts' consensus. That price suggests investors expect memory profits to fall soon. Micron is predicting the opposite.

Story Continues

AMD: the upside hinges on supply

AMD is supply-limited, too. In Taipei on Oct. 6, CEO Lisa Su said it plans to substantially increase supply in 2027 and needs more advanced wafer capacity.

On AMD's August earnings call, Su said she saw nothing that gave her pause about meeting its targets. That suggests the limits Lam flagged could matter more for how far AMD beats its plan than for the plan itself. Management guided for around $13 billion in third-quarter revenue, up about 41% year over year, and expects data center sales, led by its artificial intelligence (AI) chips, to more than double next year.

AMD stock, at about $508, is 22% under its Oct. 6 record close. Shares cost around 32 times earnings, based on analysts' consensus for 2027, so the price already counts on that data center doubling.

Marvell: a higher profit target

At its Oct. 6 investor day, Marvell targeted $70 billion to $90 billion of revenue for fiscal 2031 (ending early 2031) and a non-GAAP (adjusted) operating margin of 44% to 46%. Management said the midpoint of those targets implies adjusted earnings of more than $30 a share. Marvell brought in $8.2 billion in fiscal 2026.

Its revenue growth is already picking up, from 28% year over year in the fiscal first quarter of 2027 to 37% in the fiscal second quarter (which ended Aug. 1), and management expects about $3.15 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue, roughly 52% above the year-ago quarter.

But at about $223, shares are 22% under their Oct. 6 close. They cost about 31 times earnings, based on analysts' consensus for fiscal 2028, but only about 7 times the earnings Marvell is targeting for fiscal 2031. Of course, that target's over four years off, and Marvell depends on outside manufacturers for its chips -- the sort of chipmakers Lam says can't fully meet demand.

Is the sell-off a buying opportunity?

None of these companies has cut its outlook, and all three stocks just got cheaper.

Micron's the one I'd buy first. Tight supply is already boosting its prices, and the stock's arguably priced for a downturn its own outlook doesn't show.

AMD and Marvell are pricier growth stocks that need their plans to hold up to justify over 30 times expected earnings. I think both are worth considering here, ideally a bit at a time. After all, a slowdown in AI spending might still hit all three stocks hard.

news.Title: Prediction: 2 Stocks That Will Be Worth More Than AMD 5 Years From Now
news.Content:
AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) has become a major winner in the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. But Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ: CBRS) and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) are taking different approaches to AI that could make them far more valuable than AMD over the next five years.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Cerebras is the more unconventional of the two, and the best place to start.

Cerebras is the AI chip challenger built for speed

For years, the AI chip race has been about building more powerful processors and connecting them to more complex systems. Cerebras is taking a different route: building an enormous chip designed specifically to make AI compute faster and less complicated.

That edge is becoming increasingly important as AI moves beyond chatbots toward autonomous agents and coding assistants. These applications don't just need compute power; they need answers quickly. In fact, Cerebras has built its whole platform around that need.

Its second-quarter 2026 results showed core revenue more than doubling year over year, while cloud revenue nearly quadrupled. On top of that, Cerebras reported $25.4 billion in remaining performance obligations (RPO), strengthening visibility into future revenue.

Management also expects core revenue to more than triple in 2027, after guiding for between $880 million and $890 million this year.

While the company hasn't offered any projections through 2031, if history repeats and Cerebras keeps roughly doubling its revenue each year, it could reach about $28 billion by 2031, compared with Marvell's target of $70 billion to $90 billion.

Plus, the company's partnerships could be just as important as its chips. Cerebras has worked with OpenAI on fast inference and partnered with AMD to combine speed with higher throughput.

It also expanded its relationship with Amazon 's AWS, potentially opening the door to wider enterprise adoption through Amazon Bedrock. If these collaborations continue, Cerebras could see stronger demand for its technology without needing to build an entire software and distribution system from scratch.

That said, the company still faces several risks. Customer concentration and competition from established chipmakers are both risks to the bull case, as is potential dilution as the company funds its expansion.

Story Continues

For Cerebras to catch up to AMD, it would need to establish a large, defensible AI compute business and convert its technological edge into durable profits.

But speed isn't the only way to approach the AI boom. Another company is building the infrastructure that keeps data centers running.

A pick-and-shovel supplier in the AI boom

Marvell is pursuing another strategy to win a larger share of AI compute: supplying custom chips and high-speed connections that power AI data centers.

As cloud companies build out their AI infrastructure, they aren't simply buying more off-the-shelf processors. Instead, they're designing more specialized chips to handle their own workloads, improve efficiency, and reduce dependence on any single chip supplier.

Marvell is positioned for this shift through its exposure to custom compute and networking hardware.

The company's relationships with major cloud providers matter to the investment case. For example, Alphabet , Microsoft , and Meta Platforms are among the hyperscalers investing heavily in AI infrastructure. That creates opportunities for Marvell to supply the chips and connectivity that tie these systems together.

Optical networking is also becoming an important growth driver at Marvell. As AI clusters expand, moving data between chips and servers becomes more challenging.

That means Marvell's expertise in optical technology and data center connectivity gives it exposure to this growing bottleneck in data center infrastructure.

The main risk now is that Marvell's growth targets depend on a small group of large customers. Meanwhile, custom chip programs can be delayed, customers can switch suppliers, and competition from other chipmakers could put pressure on margins.

But if Marvell scales to anywhere near management's long-term ambitions, it could become more valuable than AMD within five years. In fact, the company's goal is to 10x its revenue by fiscal 2031, from just $8.2 billion in fiscal 2026 to $70 billion-$90 billion.

Plus, by participating in several layers of the AI build-out, Marvell could very well achieve this ambitious target.

Of course, the market already has a view on how much growth to expect.

Can these two stocks outgrow AMD over the next five years?

AMD's market cap is roughly $829 billion, compared with $195 billion for Marvell and $26 billion for Cerebras. That means both have a lot of ground to make up.

Marvell looks like the best bet as it already has an established business and relationships with the biggest cloud companies worldwide.

Cerebras is the high-risk, high-reward pick, with faster growth but also customer concentration, dilution, and a high valuation.

Either could eventually surpass AMD based on their ambitions, but Cerebras could face a bumpier ride.

news.Title: Taiwan Semiconductor Is Set to Cash in on AI. Here's What a $5,000 Investment Could Be Worth by 2030.
news.Content:
Few stocks are as much of a guaranteed winner from the AI build-out as Taiwan Semiconductor (NYSE: TSM) is. Taiwan Semiconductor is the world's largest chip foundry by far, and it's the only one with the technology and expertise to produce the cutting-edge chips needed to power devices like GPUs from Nvidia or smartphones from Apple .

Taiwan Semiconductor is set to cash in, but what could a $5,000 investment now grow to by 2030? I think it could reach $15,000.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Taiwan Semiconductor has a great outlook

Few companies have the level of visibility into conditions in the tech sector that Taiwan Semiconductor enjoys. Because it makes chips for nearly every company designing AI computing units, it is privy to information regarding expected future demand. That allows Taiwan Semiconductor time to build out the production capacity necessary to meet demand. The company has heavily invested in new chip foundry facilities in Arizona, and has now committed $265 billion to increasing U.S. chip production capacity. That's not an insignificant investment, and it also helps diversify its chip production away from Taiwan, which is always at risk of military action from mainland China.

Previously, the company gave guidance that its AI chip sales would grow at a compound annual rate in the high 50% range from 2024 through 2029. An analyst asked for an updated figure during its most recent conference call, and while CEO C.C. Wei didn't offer a specific update, he noted that demand is "very extremely robust," and that the actual growth rate "doesn't matter, it probably will be higher."

That's a very bullish statement, and with other chip companies already starting to guide for high levels of demand for 2030 to 2031, it could last for much longer.

During Q3, nearly 70% of its business came from high-performance computing, which encompasses its AI products. About 20% of its business comes from smartphones, with the remaining 10% coming from various other industries. Taiwan Semiconductor's business is most heavily influenced by AI right now, and if that segment's growth rate stays rapid -- as management suggests it will -- then the company is in for quite the growth trajectory.

Here's how Taiwan Semiconductor will turn $5,000 into $15,000

Management's older long-term forecast for compound annualized growth of 50% now includes several years when its sales of higher-powered computing chips were growing much faster. From here, I think it's more reasonable to assume that Taiwan Semiconductor as a company can grow at a 35% rate until 2030. For reference, analysts expect 38% growth in 2027.

Story Continues

It has also achieved a 51% profit margin over the past few months. I could see that margin expanding as demand stays tight, but for the sake of these estimates, I'll keep it at 50% to bake in a bit of conservatism. If Taiwan Semiconductor can grow its revenue at a 35% pace from now until 2030, that would increase its revenue to $518 billion. At a 50% profit margin, that would be about $259 billion in profits.

Right now, the market values the stock at about 28 times earnings. If we assume that by 2030, its valuation will have slipped to just 25 times earnings (fairly cheap compared to its historical levels), that would give it a market cap of $6.5 trillion.

TSM PE Ratio data by YCharts.

Currently, Taiwan Semiconductor has a $2.2 trillion market cap. So, this estimate projects that TSMC's stock could nearly triple in the next four years, turning a $5,000 investment into about $15,000. That's a great return in just a few years, and if the AI build-out continues at the expected pace, Taiwan Semiconductor will be one of the best stocks to own during that time frame.

news.Title: Marvell’s Road to $90B: The 3 Moves Behind the Boldest Target in AI Chips
news.Content:
Investors don't have to bet on Nvidia (NVDA) alone to benefit from AI chip spending. Marvell Technology (MRVL) ranks among the top global chipmakers, thanks to its role in custom AI chips and data center connectivity. As companies develop more of their own processors due to the AI boom, Marvell could benefit from designing those chips and connecting the systems around them. This opportunity has led management to raise its fiscal 2028 revenue target to $20 billion. But can earnings grow fast enough to justify the stock's valuation?

Custom AI Chips Are Just One Part of Marvell's Growth Story

In my view, Marvell's biggest advantage is that its revenue streams are not just dependent on processors. The company raised its fiscal 2031 revenue target to $70 billion to $90 billion at its Oct. 6 investor day. It also expects custom chip revenue to exceed $12 billion in fiscal 2029. But I believe the broader opportunity is just as important. Marvell also sees opportunities in XPU-attached products, which add networking, memory, and other functions to AI processors. These products could give Marvell another source of growth beyond designing complete custom chips. CEO Matt Murphy's comments on the company's broader connectivity portfolio further support this thesis.

About Marvell Stock

Marvell Technology is a semiconductor company that provides data infrastructure solutions used in data centers, networking systems, and communication equipment worldwide. The company designs advanced chips that move, process, and store data efficiently. It offers a portfolio of Ethernet solutions, networking controllers, processors, storage controllers, optical and interconnect solutions, and custom chips. Marvell focuses on technologies that improve high-speed data transfer, connectivity, and AI infrastructure performance. Founded in 1995, the company is headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware.

Over the last 12 months, Marvell has significantly outperformed the semiconductor sector, with the stock climbing roughly 202%. This was well above the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX), which gained about 79% during the same period. The rally was driven by growing demand for AI data-center infrastructure, including custom AI chips and high-speed networking solutions. Moreover, Marvell's fiscal 2026 revenue rose 42% to a record $8.2 billion, while data-center revenue jumped 46% to $6.1 billion.

Story Continues

Marvell's forward P/E of 53.98x is steep, sitting about 42% above its five-year average of 38.05x. Its forward price-to-sales ratio of 16.55x is also 61% above its historical average of 10.25x. So the stock is more expensive than usual, even as investors bet on its AI opportunity. The earnings outlook helps explain the premium. Analysts expect EPS to grow 48.6% in fiscal 2027 and 72.89% in fiscal 2028. If Marvell delivers that growth, its earnings could begin to justify the valuation.

Expensive, but Earnings Could Catch Up

Marvell Technology reported its second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on August 27. For Q2 fiscal 2027, data-centre revenue increased 46% YOY to $2.17 billion, representing 79% of total revenue. The data-center segment is expected to remain the key growth driver, with Marvell having expanded commercial agreements with Tier 1 hyperscalers for multiple custom products. The non-GAAP earnings per share came in at $0.94, beating the Wall Street estimates of $0.93. At the same time, Marvell reported an operating cash flow of $605.5 million. This implies an annualized OCF potential of $2.42 billion.

Since the valuation might be a potential deterrent for investors, it's important to also talk about the growth trajectory. Marvell guided for 45% revenue growth in fiscal 2027 to $12 billion. Further, the company expects 50% revenue growth in fiscal 2028 to $18 billion. Even beyond fiscal 2028, the outlook remains positive. For example, Marvell is positioned for $10 billion to $11 billion in custom-silicon business for fiscal 2029. The company has a custom-silicon partnership with Alphabet's (GOOG) Google, which should have a meaningful impact on revenue.

What Do Analysts Expect for MRVL Stock?

The analyst outlook for Marvell Technology is significantly positive. Based on 39 analysts with coverage, MRVL stock has a consensus "Strong Buy" rating on Wall Street. While 30 analysts have a "Strong Buy" rating for the stock, three have a "Moderate Buy," and six have a "Hold" rating.

The mean price target of $337.05 represents potential upside of 38% from current levels. Meanwhile, the most bullish price target of $450 suggests that MRVL stock could climb as much as 84% from here.

news.Title: 聯發科TPU進度遭質疑！ 花旗法說前送暖：目標上看6800元
news.Content:
面對市場對聯發科TPU發展的疑慮，花旗證券於法說前夕出面力挺，看好受惠於AI ASIC貢獻與消費性產品漲價，第四季營收將迎來約30%的強勁季增，重申買進評等並維持目標價6,800元。

法說前夕送暖力挺

IC設計龍頭廠聯發科（2454）預計於10月30日召開線上法人說明會，公佈第三季財務報告與第四季業績展望。儘管近期市場對於聯發科的張量處理器（TPU）開發與新專案進展存有疑慮，但花旗證券在最新研究報告中發布正面看法，認為營運長線成長趨勢依舊明確，並給予正面評價。

AI ASIC與消費產品雙引擎

花旗分析指出，聯發科的v8專案正按計畫順利推進，今年超過20億美元的營收貢獻，將成為帶動第四季營收季增長的核心催化劑。結合消費性產品的價格調漲與產品組合改善，預期第四季營收可獲得約30%的季增表現，且在營運槓桿效益帶動下，營業利益率亦具備上行空間。

先進封裝與技術佈局延伸

針對市場對EMIB-T技術面臨良率挑戰與週期較長所引發的v9生產風險疑慮，花旗表示此狀況已在預料之中。然而，受惠於v8專案的長期成長動能，加上SerDes升級與N2製程開發帶動平均售價提升，花旗維持2028年AI ASIC營收貢獻達400億美元的預測。技術進展方面，聯發科除已量產的224G SerDes外，336G與448G SerDes也在積極開發中。此外，針對瞄準2029年量產的TPU v10，聯發科有很大機會採用CoWOS或CoPoS封裝技術，相關訂單能見度已延伸至2029年之後。

生態系合作與財務預估上調

花旗強調，聯發科憑藉先進製程設計能力、SerDes開發技術、供應鏈管理能力及靈活的商業模式，有極大機會進一步滲透至新的雲端服務供應商專案中。同時，聯發科亦為NVLink Fusion生態系中，少數具備前端設計與全流程AI ASIC服務能力的重要玩家，將為2028年之後帶來長遠發展契機。基於營運槓桿與AI ASIC的爆發性成長，花旗將聯發科2026年、2027年及2028年的獲利預估分別調升9%、25%與9%，並重申「買進」評等目標價6,800元。
