Loop Capital downgrades Apple after supply chain checks reveal no iPhone recovery plan

Brokerage firm Loop Capital this week downgraded Apple to Hold from Buy and cut its price target to $330 from $370, after supply chain checks revealed Apple has no plans to recover the 13 million iPhone shipments cut in the second half of 2026.

Analyst Ananda Baruah said Apple previously reduced September- and December-quarter iPhone shipments by 10%, with Loop having initially believed those units could be made up through 2027 as the reductions were supply-related rather than demand-driven.

"This no longer appears to be the case," Baruah wrote.

Loop lowered its December-quarter iPhone unit forecast to 79 million from the Street's 85 million, cutting its average selling price (ASP) estimate to $1,123 from $1,239. For calendar 2027, it raised its unit forecast to 260 million but cut ASP to $1,096 from $1,235, lowering iPhone revenue to $285 billion from $315 billion and trimming EPS to $9.76 from $10.11.

The broker also flagged potential gross margin risk as memory costs keep rising, lowering its normalized EPS estimate to $11 from $12 and applying Apple's median P/E of 30 times to arrive at the new target.

"We continue to like AAPL's longer-term share gain and Services story… but believe the stock also requires a fundamental catalyst reset after its recent stock appreciation," Baruah said.

JPMorgan upgrades Intel as pullback from peak makes risk-reward more balanced

JPMorgan has upgraded Intel to Neutral from Underweight, saying the risk/reward is now much more balanced as the stock approaches the bank's $85 price target after pulling back roughly 40% from its June peak, compared with a 20-25% decline for the broader chip group.

Analyst Harlan Sur noted that since JPMorgan downgraded the stock in November 2022, Intel's server x86 CPU revenue share has fallen from 77% to 53% and its PC CPU share from 81% to 68%, with a few more quarters of share losses expected, particularly in server CPUs.

In foundry, Intel appears to be making strong inroads on yields and new customer engagements, though it generated barely $1 billion in annualized external foundry revenue in the first half of 2026, compared with $150 billion for TSMC.

Sur said that since Lip Bu Tan became CEO, execution has improved in Intel's core client and data center compute markets and in next-generation manufacturing. "Despite near-term concerns on AI infrastructure spending sustainability, we believe increasing agentic AI workloads (CPU intensive) and a very tight supply chain for leading edge silicon should drive continued positive EPS revisions in the upcoming earnings season and through CY27," he wrote.

"Risk/reward is more balanced at current levels and we move to a Neutral rating," Sur said.

CEO Elon Musk also offered some of his most detailed comments yet on a potential merger with Tesla, saying the move would be "a good idea" and confirming for the first time that special committees had been formed to discuss a potential union.

Musk said he expects annual recurring revenue (ARR) to reach between $500 billion and $1 trillion by end-2027, driven by surging demand for data-center space amid the AI boom.

Citi, which rates the stock Buy, pointed to six factors behind its positive catalyst watch: SpaceX's "track record of beats/raises" expected to continue into the fourth quarter; Flight 15 as "a monumental space-industry catalyst that sets the stage for rapid reusability on a scale never before demonstrated in launch"; dollar-per-watt economics "trending significantly above consensus expectations"; an accelerated Grok model release cadence; the possibility of more detail on SpaceX's power-generation solutions before year-end; and further clarity on its "evolving mobile strategy."

"We've described Buy-rated SPCX as being in the midst of a catalyst-rich 2-3 year arc, and we see the next 2-3 months in particular as uniquely catalyst rich even within that timeline that supports our positive investment thesis," Citi analysts said.

Buy Lam Research on pullback, Mizuho says

Mizuho has reiterated its Outperform rating on Lam Research and recommended buying the stock after a significant pullback following quarterly results, trimming its price target to $360 from $365.

Analyst Vijay Rakesh highlighted that Lam expects wafer fab equipment (WFE) spending to grow more than 29% in 2027 to over $200 billion, after rising about 42% to roughly $155 billion this year. "We are buyers on the pullback, as new greenfield fabs, NAND/HBM/Terafab position for upside," he wrote, also flagging Tesla's comments pointing to "10s of $B WFE" from Terafab in early 2028 and $100 billion long-term.

Mizuho highlighted the emergence of SLC NAND as a major tailwind, with each 1 percentage point mix shift requiring 2% more NAND wafer capacity — a market where Lam holds about 90% share. NAND revenue rose 38% in the September quarter and foundry grew 28%. The broker estimates Lam's revenue will grow 37% next year, ahead of 30% consensus, and believes Lam sees 10 new tier 1 fabs coming online in 2027.

"We see LRCX well positioned with: 1) wide competitive moats, 2) secular technology trends with HPC/AI/ML, HBM/CoWoS/TSV, GAA/BPD, and 3) rising capital intensity at the leading edge," Rakesh said.

Lam reported September-quarter revenue of $8.22 billion and EPS of $2.20, broadly in line with consensus, with gross margin rising 40 basis points sequentially to 52.4%. December-quarter guidance of $8.6 billion in revenue and EPS of $2.33 came in slightly above expectations.

AI bubble exists but will not burst yet: Yardeni

This week, Financial research firm Yardeni Research introduced an AI Bubble Meter, built using Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1, which it says confirms a bubble exists in AI-related stocks but shows it is not yet close to bursting.

The tool has two dials. The Conditions dial measures whether a bubble exists by drawing on the setups that preceded the 1999-2000 tech bust and the 2006-2007 housing bust, and currently reads 83 out of 100. The Triggers dial tracks whether the forces that ended past booms — a credit boom and a sustained rise in the cost of capital — are underway, and reads just 34.

"The meter says there's a bubble, but it's not about to burst," Yardeni wrote.

One trigger has kicked in, with the two-year Treasury yield up 115 basis points from its December low, but credit is not stretched outside AI-related areas of the economy. "The preconditions of a bubble are in place and have been for a while, but the forces that ended past booms are only partially present," the firm said.

Yardeni noted that since 1965, quarters with high Conditions and low Triggers readings were followed by an S&P 500 bear market within two years only 9% of the time, with a median inflation-adjusted gain of 18.3% over that period. When both dials read high, the odds of a bear market rose to 42% with a median loss of 12.5%.

"But the Triggers dial is the one to watch: If it starts rising toward High, so do the risks," Yardeni said, flagging the two-year yield and signs of idle capacity in hyperscalers' third-quarter results as key things to monitor.

news.Title: Sandisk's New Business Model Is Transforming the Business. Now Is the Time to Buy the Stock.
news.Content:
Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) makes NAND memory chips, which are primarily used for long-term data storage in devices like solid-state drives. That may sound like a pretty boring business with not a lot of innovation going on in it -- and you'd be right.

That's why Sandisk and its peers are normally pretty boring stocks, but all of that changed in 2026. Demand for storage skyrocketed alongside data center build-outs, consuming all available production capacity. All of a sudden, Sandisk's products were hot commodities, and prices skyrocketed, which translated into incredible stock growth for Sandisk.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

It's up nearly 500% this year -- second-best in the S&P 500 . This also allowed Sandisk to form a new, sustainable business model. I think the transition to this model will help Sandisk tremendously over the long term and eliminate some of the cyclicality typically associated with companies in the memory chip industry.

That completely flips the narrative behind investing in Sandisk's stock, making this an ideal time to buy it.

Sandisk isn't as dependent on market conditions

In normal times with ample supply, there isn't a lot that separates Sandisk's storage devices from its competition, so only one thing matters: price. The lowest price wins here, which isn't the greatest for Sandisk as a business.

However, with sky-high demand and no supply, Sandisk is taking this opportunity to reformulate its business model. The aptly named "New Business Model (NBM)" is basically a contractual agreement with some clients that sets a floor and ceiling for memory prices but has committed volumes. This is a key development, because it makes Sandisk's future more predictable.

Consistent cash flows allow the management team to allocate capital where they see fit, rather than worrying about what the business will look like a few years down the road. That's why subscription business models are king, as they are predictable. With Sandisk moving toward contract-based work, this will help smooth out the demand curve and reduce cyclical drawdowns that have plagued investors in this industry.

However, the stock is still priced like it's due for a cyclical drawdown.

SNDK PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

Remember: 6.3 times forward earnings is a dirt cheap price tag to pay for any stock. Sandisk's business model shifting more toward consistent contract work, so this should result in an increased stock premium, as it won't be as dependent on price swings in the market.

Story Continues

I think the opportunity is compelling enough to warrant buying shares now , and investors should act before the market catches up to this transformation.

news.Title: Micron vs. Sandisk: Which Is the Better AI Memory Stock to Own for the Next 3 Years
news.Content:
Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) and Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) have delivered stellar returns so far this year, driven by the incredible demand for memory chips deployed in artificial intelligence (AI) data centers.

While Micron stock has jumped by more than 3x in 2026, clocking a 220% jump as of this writing, Sandisk's gains are even more impressive at 480%. Of course, both stocks have experienced volatility lately, but the strong fundamentals of the memory market suggest that they can step on the gas once again.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

We will take a closer look at the prospects of Micron and Sandisk in this article to find out which memory stock could deliver bigger gains to investors over the next three years.

Micron enjoys an edge over Sandisk

Though Sandisk stock has outperformed Micron this year, investors will do well to note that the latter is in a better position to capitalize on the memory boom. That's because Micron sells both dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and NAND flash storage products. Sandisk, meanwhile, is a pure-play NAND flash manufacturer.

Micron, therefore, is benefiting from the massive surge in demand for both DRAM and NAND flash. Specifically, the DRAM business produced 73% of Micron's top line in the previous quarter, reaching almost $40 billion in revenue. Micron's exposure to the DRAM business allows the company to capitalize on the fast-growing high-bandwidth memory (HBM) space, where both volumes and shipments are rising rapidly.

Micron management noted on the latest earnings call that HBM sales are growing faster than conventional DRAM sales. That isn't surprising, as HBM plays a central role in quickly transporting huge data sets in AI chip clusters, ensuring that accelerator chips don't sit idle waiting for data. Even better, strong HBM demand is fueling Micron's bottom-line growth. The company notes that it has raised HBM pricing "significantly" for 2027, suggesting that its strong earnings growth rate is sustainable.

Additionally, semiconductor equipment giant ASML recently noted that supply shortages in the memory industry are widening in both size and time horizon. Similarly, SK Hynix estimates that DRAM undersupply will widen in 2027, and new capacity will only come online in June 2029. As such, Micron's DRAM business is poised for healthy growth over the next three years.

Story Continues

On the other hand, the NAND flash market is also expected to remain undersupplied for the next three years. This is great news for both Micron and Sandisk. Chinese NAND flash company YMTC recently noted that the NAND flash shortage is likely to persist until the end of 2029.

It is easy to see why demand for NAND flash is poised to substantially exceed supply. AI data centers require a lot of storage to store enormous data sets needed to train AI models and continuously feed data for inference and agentic AI applications. Given that traditional hard-disk drives (HDDs) are reportedly in short supply until 2028, AI data centers are turning to enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs).

However, the phenomenal demand for enterprise SSDs has led to a massive price spike. Tom's Hardware reported in August that the price of a 30TB enterprise SSD has surged by 6.5x in just a year. The strong pricing environment is likely to continue for the next three years amid the ongoing supply shortage.

Also, smartphone and personal computer (PC) shipments are declining due to high memory costs. This will create strong pent-up demand in the coming years, indicating that the improvement in Sandisk and Micron's margins will continue. Micron, however, has an additional catalyst in the form of the DRAM market, which explains why it is anticipated to deliver stronger bottom-line growth than Sandisk.

The verdict

Though Sandisk is a pure-play NAND flash company, its market share of 11% is lower than Micron's 15%, according to Counterpoint Research. Additionally, Micron's share of the NAND flash market improved by two percentage points year over year in the second quarter of 2026, while Sandisk maintained its share.

Meanwhile, Micron has 24% DRAM market share, and its share increased by two percentage points year over year in Q2. All this explains why analysts are expecting Micron's earnings per share to grow at a faster pace in the long run compared to Sandisk.

YCharts

What's more, Micron is the cheaper semiconductor stock to buy right now.

So, Micron clearly seems like a much better growth stock to buy and hold over the next three years to benefit from the memory boom. It is more attractively valued, is present in both the DRAM and NAND flash markets, and is likely to grow at a significantly faster pace than Sandisk. These factors could help Micron outperform Sandisk over the next three years.

news.Title: 台股下周又崩盤？「16檔錯殺股」底氣爆表 內行曝KD超賣別亂砍
news.Content:
美股費城半導體指數22日重挫近7%後，周五（23日）小幅反彈0.44%，台積電ADR也上漲1.49%。不過，台股在外資大舉提款下，加權指數在連假前收在46021點、已失守季線46207點，下周二（27日）恢復交易後，仍面臨補跌與修正壓力。法人指出，隨著技術指標KD進入超賣區，若外資賣壓逐步減輕，聯電、台積電、南亞科等16檔基本面具支撐的錯殺股，有望成為反彈行情的觀察重點。

工商時報報導，據統計，這16檔個股10月以來均遭外資賣超逾3000張，第三季營收卻繳出年增、季增雙成長成績，本益比也回落至接近或低於7月30日前波低點的水準，且KD指標均低於20，顯示短線進入超賣區。個股名單包括聯電、台積電、南亞科、旺宏、聯發科、合晶、台達電、南茂、光寶科、威剛、亞翔、全友、映泰、聯鈞、華城及智伸科。

外資10月以來大舉賣超台股逾8,200億元，加權指數22日失守季線。法人分析，近期市場資金快速移動，籌碼整理仍需要時間，但部分企業營運表現持續成長，股價修正後，評價面也逐漸浮現吸引力。若後續外資調節力道收斂，市場重新聚焦企業獲利，這16檔個股有機會成為台股反彈時的觀察標的。

凱基投顧台股分析師張明祥表示，台積電法說會上修全年營收展望，顯示AI需求仍優於市場原先預期，半導體與AI產業鏈也有機會迎來獲利上修。隨著財報陸續公布，市場焦點可望從短期利空轉向企業獲利成長，近期震盪可能提供中長期布局機會。

野村台灣新科技50 ETF經理人林怡君指出，近期台股受到利率維持高檔、AI融資成本上升及部分AI伺服器訂單遞延等因素影響，外資因而大舉撤出。不過，隨著賣壓逐步消化，市場仍有機會回歸企業獲利與產業基本面，具備關鍵技術、穩定接單能力及良好獲利品質的企業，較有機會維持競爭優勢。

news.Title: Micron and Sandisk Hit Record Memory Margins. There's One Clear Winner.
news.Content:
Being a memory chip stock investor during 2026 has been incredibly rewarding. Two of the best performers are Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) and Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU), and each has delivered impressive returns over the past year. The reason is simple: Memory chip demand is at an all-time high, and supply has run out. Therefore, prices on memory chips have skyrocketed. This has been massively beneficial to Sandisk's and Micron's profit pictures, and each has achieved record margins.

While both stocks are doing quite well, I think there's one clear winner here, and it has far more upside moving forward.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Micron and Sandisk are thriving in today's environment

Micron and Sandisk both make memory chips, but the areas they focus on are different. Both Sandisk and Micron make NAND memory, which is used for long-term data storage, often in devices like solid-state drives. Micron also makes DRAM memory, which is used for quick information access in computing devices. Both of these are important, but one segment of Micron's business stands out.

A subsegment of DRAM memory is HBM -- high bandwidth memory. HBM is what is used inside computing units like graphics processing units (GPUs), and Micron points out that industry HBM shipments will grow at a faster pace than conventional DRAM. For 2027 and 2028, Micron expects industry NAND and DRAM shipments to grow in the low to mid-20% range both years. So, there isn't going to be a lot of growth in these two industries, but with HBM growing faster than DRAM, it will give Micron an edge over Sandisk.

Micron also announced an industry-first partnership: a custom HBM chip for Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA). This is a big deal, as Nvidia and its peers were just using off-the-shelf memory chips. But with Micron entering into a partnership with Nvidia, this could lead to a more contractual situation, stabilizing Micron's revenue.

This is an issue for both Sandisk and Micron, as unstable revenue and cash flows are common in the industry. Memory chips are cyclical, and prices can rise and fall with demand. You can see this come to life in Micron's and Sandisk's profit margins, as they are highest when demand is great -- like it is right now.

YCharts.

Both companies are taking steps to mitigate the effects of a downturn by entering into long-term supply agreements with their clients. Basically, Micron and Sandisk are trading the upside of higher memory chip prices for guaranteed revenue. This reduces the ceiling, but also raises the floor of business performance. Since this industry has been plagued by prolonged underperformance due to low demand, this is a smart move. Micron estimates it has now secured about 35% of its revenue through 2030. Sandisk has signed about 50% of its clients to these kinds of contracts.

Story Continues

This is a major evolution for both companies, and it could lead the market to value their stocks higher.

Micron and Sandisk are both cheap

Because the market is expecting a cyclical downturn from both companies at any moment, their stocks don't trade at very high premiums.

YCharts. PE = price-to-earnings.

However, with both companies taking steps to close their cyclical potential, I think they should trade at a nearly average premium for big tech stocks. If they can rally to something like 20 times earnings by the end of their respective fiscal years, that could lead to the stocks tripling or quadrupling in value by this time next year.

That's a huge performance, but that will only occur if the market understands that these two have fundamentally shifted their business to be less exposed to cyclical downturns.

So, which is the winner? I think it's clearly Micron . Micron has exposure to HBM, which will be the highest growth area within the memory chip industry. It's also trading at a far cheaper price tag than Sandisk, giving it more upside. While Sandisk is still a solid pick, Micron offers greater return potential.

news.Title: TSMC or Nvidia: If I Could Only Own 1 for the Next 5 Years, It Would Be This 1.
news.Content:
The ongoing artificial intelligence (AI) boom has birthed many new inspiring companies, but it has also added a fresh spark to companies that have been around for decades.

Many stocks have soared in recent years as investors pour money into AI stocks , but two of the main beneficiaries have been Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) (TSMC). In the past five years, Nvidia and TSMC are up 874% and 266%, respectively, far outperforming any major index.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Both stocks are great options, but if you had to choose one, which should it be? Let's take a look.

What Nvidia has working in its favor

Nvidia is the poster child of the current AI boom, with its hardware (especially its GPUs ) powering the most advanced AI models around. Nvidia's GPUs were initially used for video games, but they're also great at the processing required to train and run AI models.

In its fiscal second quarter (ended July 26), Nvidia reported $96.2 billion in revenue (up 106% year over year), with $89 billion from its data center segment (up 117% year over year).

NVDA Revenue (Quarterly) data by YCharts

Nvidia is more than just its advanced chips. It's done a great job of building a hardware-software ecosystem that essentially traps customers in because it's the de facto coding language used in AI development (called CUDA), and switching to a different chipmaker would be too costly and time-consuming for companies.

This stronghold in enterprise AI is how Nvidia has become the world's most valuable public company, with a market cap of over $5.2 trillion (as of market open on Oct. 21).

What TSMC has working in its favor

TSMC is the world's premier semiconductor (chip) foundry and is also extremely important to the AI ecosystem, but for a different reason. While companies like Nvidia design the chips they sell, TSMC manufactures them and brings them to life.

None of TSMC's competitors can match its scale or capabilities, which is why it has long been the go-to for some of the world's top tech giants -- including Nvidia. When it comes to manufacturing advanced AI chips, TSMC has a monopoly, and that's putting it lightly.

Being the go-to option has given TSMC significant pricing power, which it has used to its advantage. Its revenue growth is solid, but its margins are where its pricing power really shows up. From last third quarter to this recent third quarter, its gross margins rose from 59.5% to 66.4%, operating margin from 50.6% to 58.7%, and net profit margin from 45.7% to 51.1%.

Story Continues

This should continue. During TSMC's latest earnings call, CEO C.C. Wei highlighted the demand, saying:

The AI market continues to be very strong. Recent developments are very positive to AI's long-term demand outlook. We observe increasing AI demand, fueled by the rising adoption of agentic AI as we transition from chatbot to AI assistance.

Which is the better investment for the next five years?

From a business standpoint, one reason I give TSMC the edge is because of how much Nvidia depends on it. Nvidia is a powerhouse, no doubt, but without TSMC's manufacturing ability, Nvidia's business becomes limited. It's at the mercy of TSMC's capacity and production timelines.

TSMC is a great partner, but that dependency can also be a single point of failure. I don't see it happening, but the risk is there nonetheless. Nvidia could go with a rival like Samsung , but that could mean sacrificing production and having to redesign systems.

The same concentration risk applies to many other tech companies. Regardless of who dominates the AI race between the AI hyperscalers ( Amazon , Microsoft , Alphabet , and Meta Platforms ), they'll all rely on TSMC for manufacturing. That puts TSMC in a very lucrative position for at least the next five years, but even after the AI frenzy, it'll remain a key piece in the supply chain for tons of other electronics.

From a stock standpoint, Nvidia and TSMC trade similarly, at 23.3 and 24.2 times their projected earnings next year, respectively. However, the difference in market caps ($5.2 trillion versus $2.2 trillion) leads me to believe that TSMC has more upside. It could double in value and still not be as valuable as Nvidia is now.

NVDA PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

We can't predict how any stock will perform, and you likely can't go wrong with investing in either stock. However, over the next five years, I like TSMC's upside.

Earnings flood, Fed meeting will test rickety AI market rally
news.Content:
By Lewis Krauskopf

NEW YORK, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US stock investors face a pivotal week, with corporate earnings reports led by major AI players and a Federal Reserve meeting posing critical tests for a suddenly shaky market rally.

Weakness in technology shares left investors on edge about the state of the AI trade that has ‌driven the US equity bull market that just marked its fourth anniversary.

The Nasdaq Composite posted a slim loss on Friday, a day after the tech-heavy index suffered ‌its biggest daily drop since June. Investors were disappointed by quarterly reports from Meta and Lam Research. Meta is one of the hyperscalers spending massively to build out data centers, while Lam is a high-flying semiconductor company, one of ​a group that has been among the biggest AI stock winners.

Three other hyperscalers -- Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon -- headline a packed week of quarterly results, including about one-third of S&P 500 companies. The Fed's interest rate policy meeting on Wednesday also could rattle markets.

"There are a lot of balls in the air," said Nick Giorgi, chief equity strategist at Alpine Macro.

"Next week, you have a lot more tech earnings, and right now the market is taking a discerning eye as it relates to all the spending that goes along with artificial intelligence," Giorgi said. "The market's just not giving the benefit of ‌the doubt to companies that are spending a ton of money ⁠on building this all out, which to us is actually very healthy, but still does augur for some short-term pain."

Investors also have their focus trained on the US midterm elections on November 3, with growing bets that the Democrats will wrest control of the US Congress away from President Donald ⁠Trump's Republican party. The series of market catalysts could ratchet up volatility over the next couple of weeks and challenge optimism that has helped lift the benchmark S&P 500 index up 11% in 2026.

HYPERSCALERS ON THE HOT SEAT

Robust US profit growth has underpinned the stock market's gains this year in the face of headwinds including spiking Treasury yields and rising energy costs stemming from the Middle East conflict.

With more than ​100 ​companies having posted results so far, third-quarter S&P 500 earnings are on pace to have climbed more than ​32% from a year ago, according to LSEG IBES data. Next week ‌is the busiest of the reporting season.

"I think earnings will determine whether this ... tech pullback is a buying opportunity, or is there a deeper correction ahead," said King Lip, chief strategist at BakerAvenue Wealth Management. "What we need is just another round of really strong earnings."

Story Continues

Alphabet and Microsoft report on Wednesday. Amazon's results are due Thursday. Focus will be on the guidance the companies give on capital spending plans and whether they are seeing returns on the massive outlays.

Capital spending from hyperscalers, expected to be around $800 billion this year, is boosting the bottom lines for a wide swath of companies involved in the AI buildout. But investors are wary of the sustainability of such spending amid mounting financing costs.

"Earnings are critical to the overall confidence level of the ‌AI trade and how much longer the spend will continue," said Kevin Mahn, president and chief investment officer ​at Hennion & Walsh Asset Management.

FED EXPECTED TO PAUSE ON RATES, FOR NOW

Quarterly reports next week from chip companies Intel ​and Sandisk also could influence the AI trade.

Elsewhere, other high-profile companies set to report ​next week include drugmaker Eli Lilly, oil majors Exxon and Chevron and industrial equipment giant Caterpillar.

The prospect for more interest rate hikes also comes into ‌focus with the Fed meeting. The Fed raised rates in September for ​the first time since 2023, in an effort ​to control above-target inflation, but Fed funds futures late on Friday suggested a less-than 10% chance the Fed will hike again when it gives its policy statement on Wednesday, according to LSEG data.

One factor: Investors are dubious that the Fed will want to increase rates just a week before the midterm elections.

However, markets are leaning toward a hike ​at the next meeting in December, with futures suggesting a roughly ‌80% probability of such a move then.

Walter Todd, chief investment officer at Greenwood Capital, said he will be watching for any hints about the rate path at Fed ​Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference following the decision.

"Does he say something to give an idea about December, because right now the expectation is there is going ​to be a hike," Todd said.

(Reporting by Lewis Krauskopf, editing by Colin Barr and David Gregorio)

news.Title: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) Posted Record Profit and the Stock Still Fell. Here's What the Market Is Worried About.
news.Content:
TSMC (NYSE: TSM), the world's top contract chipmaker, posted its third-quarter earnings on Oct. 15. Its revenue and net profit surged 50% and 69%, respectively, and set new record highs.

That also marked TSMC's sixth consecutive quarter of record profits. However, TSMC's stock slipped after that impressive report -- and it's still down 7% over the past month. Let's see why TSMC's stock didn't soar higher, and if it's worth buying in this choppy market.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

How fast is TSMC growing?

TSMC manufactures the world's most advanced chips for the largest fabless chipmakers , including Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), AMD , and Broadcom . Most of its recent growth has been driven by the AI market's breakneck expansion.

In the third quarter, TSMC generated 68% of its revenue from producing high-performance computing (HPC) chips for AI-driven customers such as Nvidia. Its HPC revenue also rose 22% sequentially, marking a significant acceleration from its previous quarters.

TSMC also generated a third of its revenue from its 3nm node, which produces Nvidia's newest Vera Rubin computing platform. That expansion of that high-end node indicates that TSMC is maintaining its lead in the production of the world's smallest and densest chips. It also generated 8% of its revenue from its newest 2nm node.

Percentage of Revenue by Node

Data source: TSMC.

For the full year, TSMC expects its revenue to rise 44% in USD terms. That's up slightly from its prior outlook for at least 40% growth, and marks its third top-line guidance boost in 2026.

It expects that acceleration to be driven by the increased production of AI chips and the expansion of its 2nm node. It didn't raise its full-year capex target of $60 billion to $64 billion.

Why did TSMC's stock pull back?

TSMC's headline numbers were impressive, but a few issues weighed down the stock. First, its gross margin of 66.4% -- which matched its own guidance of 65%-67% and expanded from its gross margin of 59.5% a year earlier -- dipped sequentially from 67.7% in the second quarter.

Story Continues

That sequential contraction wasn't surprising, since TSMC ramped up its 2nm production and expanded its overseas fabs during the quarter. But with its capex already set to hit record levels this year (up 47%-56% from 2025), that dip likely rattled some investors.

Another concern is the AI market's potential slowdown. Even though there is still plenty of pent-up demand for the latest AI chips, rising interest rates and other macro headwinds could throttle the market's near-term growth. If hyperscalers like Amazon and Microsoft rein in their AI spending, TSMC's HPC growth could cool off.

Lastly, TSMC's stock had risen 39% year-to-date before its third-quarter report. Therefore, a lot of optimism was already baked into its stock -- which limited its near-term growth potential.

Should long-term investors be worried?

TSMC will remain a linchpin of the semiconductor market for the foreseeable future, and it's still a balanced way to invest in the AI boom without putting too much faith in a single chipmaker. From 2025 to 2028, analysts expect its revenue and EPS to grow at CAGRs of 36% and 42%, respectively, as the AI chip market expands.

Those are incredible growth rates for a stock that trades at 16 times next year's earnings. So if you plan to hold TSMC for a few years instead of a few quarters, it's still a great time to accumulate this reliable semiconductor stock.

news.Title: The AI Rout: Sorting CAPEX Fact From Fiction
news.Content:
Funding Fears Threaten AI Bull Market

Early in the year, investors rushed into tech stocks as AI innovations, investment, and rapid growth expectations drew attention away from the rest of the market. AI-related leaders like Bloom Energy ( BE ), SanDisk ( SNDK ) and Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) each soared more than 100%. However, over the past few months, Wall Street's price action has completely flipped. Although major market indices are within a hair of all-time highs, leading AI-stocks have been lackluster, with many down 50% or more off their 2026 highs.

What Caused the Destruction in AI Stocks?

Gravity & Profit Taking

First, while the correction in AI-related names is undoubtedly painful for bulls (especially those who bought near the highs), corrections of this magnitude are normal in bull markets. For example, SanDisk exploded by ~2,800% from August 2025 to June 2026. In other words, after such a massive move, profit taking is to be expected. Currently, SanDisk is testing its rising 200-day moving average, the best gauge of the long-term trend, for the first time in its history. Again, even the strongest stocks occasionally succumb to the laws of gravity.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The AI Debt Fear Narrative

More recently, selling in AI stocks has intensified amid a sharp shift in Wall Street sentiment regarding AI spending and the sustainability of debt loads. The tipping point came when neocloud leader CoreWeave ( CRWV ) saw its unsecured bonds dumped, pushing yields to a distressed 15%. In other words, the move in CoreWeave's bonds suggests fixed-income investors have far less confidence in the company's ability to meet its ballooning debt. So far in October, CoreWeave shares have plunged nearly 40%, dragging other neocloud and AI -related stocks like Nebius Group ( NBIS ) along with it.

CoreWeave, which started as a Bitcoin Mining company, pivoted to AI data centers during the 2022 crypto bear market. Today, it is a specialized AI cloud provider that rents out massive clusters of graphics processing units (GPUs) and infrastructure to companies training and running AI models. Building massive AI data centers requires heavy upfront expenses for CoreWeave because its business model demands immediate, large-scale capital spending on infrastructure and hardware before it collects cash from customer contracts.

The Betting Markets Tell a Different Story

I've found that betting markets are far more reliable than traditional surveys or opinions because participants have real money at risk. While many headlines suggest a CoreWeave bankruptcy is imminent, the betting markets suggest otherwise. Polymarket bettors assign only an 11% chance of a CoreWeave bankruptcy filing by the end of next year.

Story Continues

Jensen Huang Weighs in on Neocloud Financing Concerns

Jensen Huang is the iconic CEO of the world's largest company and the most important AI company, NVIDIA ( NVDA ). With that in mind, investors can safely assume Huang has the best sense of what's going on in the AI industry. At the GTC conference in Berlin, Huang weighed in on the neocloud financing concerns, saying:

"Everything else will get solved when demand is high. You can't solve the absence of demand. But when demand is high, everything else will get taken care of. I am quite confident that they will find solutions. Their solution starts with the fact that they have excellent customers. Demand is really high and they just need working capital, and working capital will come."

NVIDIA is a CoreWeave partner and stakeholder.

Will AI CAPEX Continue to Grow?

The current AI buildout already the largest industrial buildout in history. Because of massive amount of capital already invested, bears are betting that AI CAPEX spending is near a peak. However, the most recent data shows that Ai spending isn't slowing; it's actually increasing at a faster rate. SpaceX's ( SPCX ) earnings call provided valuable clues. 52% of SpaceX's revenue are derived from AI.

Meanwhile, during SpaceX's Q3 2026 earnings call, CEO Elon Musk projected that annual recurring revenue (ARR) could reach $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027. Meanwhile, Wells Fargo expects Meta's CAPEX to soar to $249 billion in 2027, up from ~$145 billion in 2026. Goldman Sachs Research now projects that hyperscaler CAPEX will soar from $768 billion in 2026 to $1.182 trillion in 2027.

Image Source: Goldman Sachs Research

Bottom Line

Despite the brutal pullbacks in AI-related stocks, debt fears are far overblown and the bullish fundamental case remains rock-solid for the foreseeable future.

news.Title: As the U.S. Pulls Chip Making Back Home, the Toolmakers Win First
news.Content:
As the U.S. pushes to bring chipmaking home, billions are flowing into new factories, creating massive demand for tools to bring new fabs online. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM), for example, added $100 billion to its Arizona plans in July, bringing its planned U.S. investment to $265 billion. Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) raised its own U.S. spending plan to more than $250 billion through 2035 that same month.

That means tool orders can arrive before a new fab reaches full production. Beyond TSMC and Micron, other companies stand to benefit, including Intel (NASDAQ: INTC), ASML Holding (NASDAQ: ASML), Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT), and Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

For investors, the question now is: Who gets paid first, the companies that build the tools, or the ones that run the factories? Intel is a good place to start.

Intel faces a key turnaround test

With both chip design and manufacturing under one roof, Intel has direct exposure to U.S. efforts to expand local production. Its foundry business could also attract customers seeking alternatives to established manufacturers.

While toolmakers are paid first when fabs are built, Intel sits in the middle of the chain, generating revenue only after it starts shipping chips to device manufacturers. The challenge is execution. Intel must improve manufacturing performance, attract outside customers, and sell enough chips to justify its spending.

That said, another company supplies the tools Intel needs, allowing it to benefit even before production begins.

ASML: the tollbooth for advanced chipmaking

Advanced lithography machines from ASML help chipmakers print complex circuit patterns. As a result, ASML is an early beneficiary when Intel, TSMC, or other manufacturers expand capacity.

However, ASML's growth still depends on customers following through on spending plans. Export restrictions and geopolitical tensions around Taiwan could disrupt sales. With the stock trading at a premium valuation -- a price-to-earnings (P/E) above 40 -- it leaves investors vulnerable if expected growth disappoints.

More ways to capture equipment spending at Applied Materials

Meanwhile, a fellow toolmaker can capture more spending by selling a wider range of equipment. Applied Materials supplies equipment and services used to manufacture chips. Its broad portfolio has exposure to logic chips, memory, and other semiconductor components.

Story Continues

Whether Intel or TSMC expands production, equipment spending creates more business for the company, giving it several ways to benefit. However, delayed projects, export controls, and competition can weaken orders and revenue growth.

TSMC: a proven chipmaker for outsourced production

Once that equipment ships, a contract manufacturer uses it to create advanced chips. As a foundry, TSMC manufactures chips for customers that outsource production, including those that design advanced AI chips. Its established customer relationships and manufacturing capacity position it to benefit from growing AI demand.

Like Intel, TSMC sits in the middle of the supply chain, using the equipment supplied by toolmakers to manufacture chips. Geopolitical tensions around Taiwan create significant operational risk, while U.S. expansion can be more expensive than expansion in Taiwan.

Micron's memory fabs come with high upfront costs

Meanwhile, a memory maker offers exposure to a different part of the AI supply chain. Equipment from the toolmakers helps Micron Technology produce the DRAM and NAND memory used in computers and smartphones. Demand for high bandwidth memory can support added capacity.

The catch is cyclicality. If supply grows faster than demand, memory prices and profits can fall sharply. Micron must also fund costly manufacturing upgrades while competing against other large memory producers.

A fabless model lets Qualcomm skip building its own fabs

Still, one company offers a way to invest in the chip boom without owning the factories. Qualcomm designs processors and connectivity technology for smartphones and connected devices. Its fabless model allows it to outsource manufacturing rather than funding its own factories.

The company sits toward the end of the supply chain, serving as a customer of TSMC. Its growth depends on chip demand and product competitiveness. But smartphone weakness and competition remain key risks.

Who gets paid first when new fabs open?

The six companies sit at different points in the supply chain, and some get paid sooner than others. ASML and Applied Materials sit nearest the top of the supply chain. Their equipment is needed before new fabs can produce chips at scale, allowing them to get paid before everyone else.

Fab operators come next, but with caveats. TSMC faces Taiwan tensions and higher U.S. costs, Intel has to prove it can execute, and Micron's profits can swing with the memory cycle. Qualcomm gets paid last, since it depends on chip demand from smartphone makers. Investors who can accept the caveats might consider the fab operators.

Overall, as the U.S. builds more fabs at home, toolmakers appear to be the early beneficiaries.

news.Title: Prediction: A $10,000 Investment in This Memory Stock Will Double by 2030 (Hint: It’s Not Micron or Sandisk)
news.Content:
The artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure boom has supercharged the memory market, leading to a phenomenal surge in the share prices of Micron Technology and Sandisk .

Lam Research reported fiscal Q1 revenue of $8.22 billion, up nearly 55% from the year-ago period. The guidance implies a 52% year-over-year increase in revenue, and a stronger year-over-year jump of 84% in earnings per share. However, Lam stock fell more than 8% following its quarterly report, as the company's guidance was in line with Wall Street's expectations. Investors were probably expecting Lam's guidance to crush consensus estimates, and that wasn't the case.

I think that the slide is an opportunity for savvy investors to buy a top growth stock, considering that Lam is sitting on a massive growth opportunity that could fuel its growth until the end of the decade. After all, the company sells wafer and fabrication equipment (WFE), and the memory industry accounts for 46% of its revenue.

Story Continues

Industry association SEMI noted in July that global semiconductor manufacturing equipment sales will increase 23% in 2026 to $166 billion. Even better, the market's revenue could hit $201 billion in 2027 and $229.5 billion in 2028. Memory will play a central role in this market's expansion.

SEMI points out that DRAM equipment sales could increase by 39% in 2026, 27% next year, and 15% in 2028. Meanwhile, NAND flash equipment sales are on track to increase by 31% in 2026 and 2027, followed by a 14.5% increase in 2028. So, Lam's addressable market is on track to grow sizably by 2028.

However, I won't be surprised to see strong WFE spending beyond 2028. Bank of America estimates that WFE spending could hit $360 billion in 2030, more than double this year's projected spending. Not surprisingly, analysts have been increasing their revenue expectations for the next couple of fiscal years.

LRCX Revenue Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

Here's why it is a good idea to invest $10,000 in this stock right now

If you have $10,000 in investable cash right now, and you're looking to diversify your portfolio, then buying this AI stock with that money could be a smart move. That's because Lam will not only help investors capitalize on the memory market's growth but also enable them to benefit from the broader semiconductor equipment industry's growth.

Lam's earnings per share could increase by 64% in the current fiscal year to $9.57, according to consensus estimates. The forecast for the next couple of years points to robust double-digit growth.

LRCX EPS Estimates for Next Fiscal Year data by YCharts

However, as the chart below shows, analysts are becoming bullish on the company's long-term earnings growth potential.

LRCX EPS LT Growth Estimates data by YCharts

Assuming Lam's bottom line jumps by even 20% in fiscal 2030, its earnings per share could reach $17.11 after four years (using fiscal 2029's projected EPS of $14.26 as the base). If Lam trades at 30 times earnings at that time, in line with the tech-focused Nasdaq-100 index's earnings multiple, its stock price will reach $513. That implies a potential upside of 116%, meaning a $10,000 investment in this stock could be worth more than $21,600 after four years.

So, buying Lam Research stock following its post-earnings slide could be a profitable move, as the secular growth of the memory and semiconductor equipment markets will be a long-term tailwind for the company.

Key Factors to Note Ahead of KLAC's Q1 Results

KLA's first-quarter fiscal 2027 results are expected to have benefited from accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, particularly advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Increasing demand for AI processors, high-performance computing chips and sophisticated semiconductor designs is driving the adoption of KLA's inspection and metrology solutions. The transition toward 2-nanometer manufacturing and gate-all-around transistor architectures is increasing process control requirements. The company's Semiconductor Process Control business is expected to have benefited from these trends in the to-be-reported quarter.

Increased investments in DRAM manufacturing, particularly high-bandwidth memory (HBM) used in AI accelerators and data centers, are expected to have driven top-line growth in the fiscal first quarter. Growing HBM adoption, increasing extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography applications and rising memory-device complexity are creating additional demand for process control equipment. HBM's larger die sizes, stringent performance specifications and complex stacking architectures require more sophisticated inspection and metrology capabilities. These factors bode well for KLAC.

Moreover, fiscal first-quarter results are expected to have benefited from robust demand for advanced packaging solutions, supported by growing adoption of heterogeneous integration, chiplets and high-performance computing architectures. Increasing packaging complexity is encouraging semiconductor manufacturers to deploy more advanced inspection and metrology tools to improve yields and manufacturing efficiency. Meanwhile, fiscal first-quarter results are also expected to reflect improving component availability and expanding manufacturing capacity. Nevertheless, KLAC management has highlighted that calcium fluoride optical components can have lead times of 18-24 months or longer, potentially limiting production flexibility. KLAC Stock's Valuation

The company expects KLA's share of the advanced packaging market to increase to approximately 7-8% in 2026 from only a few percentage points in 2023. The increasing application of front-end manufacturing processes in advanced packaging is driving demand for more sophisticated inspection and metrology solutions. Growing adoption of hybrid bonding and high-density interconnect technologies should further expand KLA's addressable market.

The company is well-positioned to capitalize on increasing wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending, supported by AI infrastructure investments, semiconductor capacity expansion and technology transitions. The company raised its calendar 2026 WFE market outlook to the low-$150-billion range, representing mid-20% growth from approximately $120 billion in 2025. KLAC management indicated that industry growth in 2027 could match or exceed 2026 levels, with a scenario approaching $190 billion in WFE spending.

KLA's growing installed equipment base is expected to support sustained expansion in its services business. The company has established a long-term annual services revenue growth target of 13-15%, supported by increasing equipment installations, maintenance requirements, upgrades and productivity-enhancing solutions. Approximately 80% of services revenues are contract-based, providing recurring revenue visibility. Strong equipment shipments in calendar 2026 and 2027 should expand the installed base, creating additional opportunities for service contracts and customer support.

Conclusion

KLA's strong positioning in the semiconductor process control market, accelerating AI infrastructure investments and robust demand for advanced packaging solutions bode well for its growth prospects. Increasing process control intensity, rising HBM adoption and expanding WFE spending are expected to sustain revenue momentum. news.Title: AMAT vs. LRCX: Which Stock Has an Edge in the WFE Space?
news.Content:
Applied Materials AMAT and Lam Research LRCX stand out as key suppliers of wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) like Chemical Vapor Deposition, Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD), Physical Vapor Deposition, Chemical Mechanical Planarization Epitaxy and etching tools to serve various stages of chip manufacturing.

With the AI boom continuing to drive growth for the semiconductor industry, the question remains: Which WFE stock is a better investment pick today? Let's break down their fundamentals, growth prospects, market challenges and valuation to determine which offers a more compelling investment case.

The Case for AMAT Stock

Applied Materials is gaining from rising demand for advanced chips used in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, especially in its Semiconductor Systems business. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Semiconductor Systems generated revenues of $7.04 billion, up approximately 27% year over year.

Growing investment in leading-edge foundry-logic, dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and advanced packaging is creating opportunities for the company's wafer fabrication equipment, while rising manufacturing complexity supports demand for differentiated process technologies.

Applied Materials is expanding its technology portfolio to capitalize on these opportunities. Its Centris Spectral SiN ALD system supports advanced logic manufacturing, while enhanced Centura Prime epitaxy and Producer Avila 2 PECVD systems target DRAM performance and higher-layer-count high-bandwidth memory.

Beyond revenue growth, Semiconductor Systems is strengthening Applied Materials' profitability. Its non-GAAP gross margin increased to 55.4% in the third quarter from 53.5% a year earlier. The operating margin expanded to 38% from 33.2%, reflecting the value of its technology portfolio and operating leverage.

AMAT's fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 guidance anticipates Semiconductor Systems revenues of approximately $7.9 billion, representing 62% year-over-year growth. The outlook indicates that demand across leading-edge logic, DRAM and advanced packaging could sustain strong near-term momentum.

Applied Materials expects non-GAAP earnings of $4.02 per share (+/- 20 cents), indicating 85% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. The Zacks Consensus Estimate suggests year-over-year growth of 86.6%. The estimates have been revised upward in the past 30 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Case for LRCX Stock

Lam Research is benefiting from rising demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment as artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure drives investment in memory, leading-edge foundry and advanced packaging. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, systems revenues increased 61.6% year over year to $5.73 billion, reflecting stronger spending across NAND, DRAM and foundry markets.

Story Continues

Growing investments in higher-layer-count NAND, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced chip manufacturing are creating opportunities for Lam Research's etch, deposition and other process technologies. NAND sales increased approximately 40% sequentially, supported by conversions to 256-layer-and-above devices and initial investments in 384-layer technology. Meanwhile, demand for DDR5 and HBM supported DRAM spending, while leading-edge chipmaking and advanced packaging helped drive record foundry revenues.

Lam Research is expanding its technology portfolio to capitalize on these opportunities. Its Akara etch and Aether dry resist products are gaining traction in foundry and DRAM manufacturing. The company has also raised its cumulative Aether revenue outlook to approximately $2.5 billion by the end of the decade, up roughly $1 billion from its previous estimate. Additionally, its panel plating systems have reached more than 20 customers, highlighting opportunities in advanced packaging.

Beyond systems growth, Lam Research's Customer Support Business Group (CSBG) is strengthening its recurring revenue base. Customer support-related revenues and other increased 40% year over year to $2.49 billion, marking a fourth consecutive quarterly record. High equipment utilization, NAND upgrades and demand for spare parts and services supported performance. The company expects CSBG revenue growth of more than 30% in 2026 and over 15% in 2027.

Lam Research's profitability is also improving. Non-GAAP gross margin reached a record 52.4%, up from 50.6% a year earlier, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 40.2% from 35%. A favorable customer and product mix contributed to the improvement, although higher operating expenses and increased investment in product development remain important considerations.

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, LRCX forecasts a non-GAAP gross margin of 52.5%, plus or minus one percentage point, and an operating margin of 40.5% (+/- 1%). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for LRCX's fiscal second-quarter earnings is pegged at $2.26, suggesting year-over-year growth of 78%. Estimates have been revised upward in the past 30 days.

Stock Price Performance and Valuation of AMAT and LRCX

Year to date, shares of Applied Materials and Lam Research have gained 46.1% and 33.4%, respectively.

YTD Performance Chart

From the valuation perspective, AMAT is trading at a discount. AMAT is trading at a price-to-sales (P/S) multiple of 6.57X, below LRCX's P/S multiple of 7.92X.

Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart

Conclusion: LRCX vs. AMAT

Lam Research appears better positioned for growth-oriented investors, driven by rising demand for advanced memory manufacturing, AI infrastructure and innovative process technologies. Its strong customer support business and expanding technology portfolio offer attractive long-term opportunities, although its premium valuation makes Applied Materials a compelling alternative for value-conscious investors. news.Title: Analysts Estimate Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR (APELY) to Report a Decline in Earnings: What to Look Out for
news.Content:
Wall Street expects a year-over-year decline in earnings on lower revenues when Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR (APELY) reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This company is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.81 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of -25.7%.

Revenues are expected to be $1.71 billion, down 5.7% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 39.22% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR?

For Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR, the Most Accurate Estimate is the same as the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that there are no recent analyst views which differ from what have been considered to derive the consensus estimate. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of 0%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #1.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR would post earnings of $0.02 per share when it actually produced a loss of -$0.21, delivering a surprise of -1,150.00%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates three times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

Expected Results of an Industry Player

Another stock from the Zacks Electronics - Miscellaneous Products industry, KLA (KLAC), is soon expected to post earnings of $1.18 per share for the quarter ended September 2026. This estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +34.1%. Revenues for the quarter are expected to be $4.05 billion, up 26.1% from the year-ago quarter.

Over the last 30 days, the consensus EPS estimate for KLA has been revised 0.3% up to the current level. Nevertheless, the company now has an Earnings ESP of -0.03%, reflecting a lower Most Accurate Estimate.

When combined with a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy), this Earnings ESP makes it difficult to conclusively predict that KLA will beat the consensus EPS estimate. The company beat consensus EPS estimates in each of the trailing four quarters.

news.Title: Down 21.0% in 4 Weeks, Here's Why KLA (KLAC) Looks Ripe for a Turnaround
news.Content:
KLA (KLAC) has been beaten down lately with too much selling pressure. While the stock has lost 21% over the past four weeks, there is light at the end of the tunnel as it is now in oversold territory and Wall Street analysts expect the company to report better earnings than they predicted earlier.

We use Relative Strength Index (RSI), one of the most commonly used technical indicators, for spotting whether a stock is oversold. This is a momentum oscillator that measures the speed and change of price movements.

RSI oscillates between zero and 100. Usually, a stock is considered oversold when its RSI reading falls below 30.

Technically, every stock oscillates between being overbought and oversold irrespective of the quality of their fundamentals. And the beauty of RSI is that it helps you quickly and easily check if a stock's price is reaching a point of reversal.

So, by this measure, if a stock has gotten too far below its fair value just because of unwarranted selling pressure, investors may start looking for entry opportunities in the stock for benefiting from the inevitable rebound.

However, like every investing tool, RSI has its limitations, and should not be used alone for making an investment decision.

Here's Why KLAC Could Experience a Turnaround

The RSI reading of 23.92 for KLAC is an indication that the heavy selling could be in the process of exhausting itself, so the stock could bounce back in a quest for reaching the old equilibrium of supply and demand.

This technical indicator is not the only factor that calls for a potential rebound for the stock. There is a fundamental indicator as well. A strong agreement among sell-side analysts covering KLAC in raising earnings estimates for the current year has led to an increase in the consensus EPS estimate by 0.4% over the last 30 days. And an upward trend in earnings estimate revisions usually translates into price appreciation in the near term.

Moreover, KLAC currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on trends in earnings estimate revisions and EPS surprises. news.Title: NVDA vs. LRCX: Which AI Semiconductor Stock Is the Better Buy?
news.Content:
NVIDIA Corporation NVDA and Lam Research Corporation LRCX are two leading semiconductor stocks benefiting from the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.

NVIDIA powers AI workloads through its advanced computing chips and platforms, while Lam Research provides essential manufacturing equipment used to produce advanced chips and memory. Both companies are benefiting from rising AI infrastructure investments, but their growth opportunities, valuations and risks differ.

With NVIDIA trading at a lower price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple and Lam Research delivering stronger year-to-date stock gains, which semiconductor stock offers investors a better buying opportunity today? Let's find out.

NVDA: AI Leadership Supports Strong Growth Prospects

NVIDIA delivered an impressive second-quarter fiscal 2027 performance, with revenues soaring 106% year over year to $96.22 billion. Data Center revenues surged 117% to $89 billion, driven by strong demand for its Blackwell Ultra infrastructure. Non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) increased 120% to $2.22, while gross margin reached 75%.

NVIDIA Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

NVIDIA Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | NVIDIA Corporation Quote

NVIDIA's growth opportunities extend beyond hyperscalers to AI cloud providers, enterprises and sovereign customers. The rollout of its Vera Rubin platform and expanding AI infrastructure investments could support further growth. Its third-quarter revenue guidance of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, and management's preliminary expectation of roughly 70% fiscal 2028 growth signal continued momentum.

However, NVIDIA faces significant challenges. Supply constraints are limiting its ability to meet customer demand, while rising memory costs are expected to pressure gross margins. Management anticipates margins could decline to 71–72% in the fourth quarter before recovering to 72–73% in fiscal 2028.

Geopolitical uncertainty also remains a concern, with the company's forward outlook assuming no Data Center compute revenues from China. Despite these risks, NVIDIA's strong profitability, computing ecosystem and expanding customer base support its long-term investment appeal.

LRCX: AI-Driven Equipment Demand Creates Opportunities

Lam Research is benefiting from growing semiconductor manufacturing requirements as AI chips, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced packaging become increasingly complex. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues increased 54.4% year over year to $8.22 billion. Non-GAAP EPS rose 74.6% to $2.20, while non-GAAP gross and operating margins reached records of 52.4% and 40.2%, respectively.

Story Continues

Lam Research Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Lam Research Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Lam Research Corporation Quote

The company's deposition and etch technologies are essential to manufacturing advanced semiconductors. Its customer support business provides another growth driver, generating nearly $2.5 billion in quarterly revenues. Management expects calendar year 2026 systems revenues to increase well more than 40% and projects wafer fabrication equipment spending to exceed $200 billion in 2027.

Nevertheless, Lam Research remains exposed to semiconductor capital-spending cycles. Clean-room availability and component shortages are restricting industry output, and near-term constraints limited its second-quarter revenue guidance to $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million. The revenue guidance reflects a 4.6% sequential increase, significantly lower than the 22.3% increase in the second quarter.

China supplied 35% of first-quarter revenues, but management expects a meaningfully lower share in the second quarter. These factors could affect near-term growth.

NVIDIA vs. Lam Research: Which Has a Better Growth Profile?

Analysts' projections suggest NVDA has a better growth profile than LRCX. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for NVIDIA's fiscal 2027 revenues and EPS indicates a year-over-year increase of 88.7% and 95%, respectively. For fiscal 2028, the consensus marks for revenue and EPS suggest year-over-year growth of 67.5% and 69.3%, respectively.

Meanwhile, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for Lam Research's fiscal 2027 revenues and EPS indicates a year-over-year jump of 48.5% and 60.9%, respectively. For fiscal 2028, the consensus marks for revenue and EPS suggest year-over-year growth of 17.2% and 22.2%, respectively.

NVDA vs. LRCX: Valuation and Price Performance

NVIDIA has the valuation advantage, trading at a forward 12-month P/E multiple of 15.18 compared with 23.02 for Lam Research. This difference is notable, given NVIDIA's faster recent revenue growth, higher gross margins and strong revenue outlook.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Lam Research has delivered superior stock market momentum, with shares rising 33.4% year to date compared with a 13.8% gain for NVIDIA. However, NVDA's lower valuation and stronger growth profile make it more attractive than LRCX.

Conclusion: NVIDIA Is the Better Investment Bet Today

Lam Research offers compelling exposure to rising semiconductor manufacturing spending, advanced packaging and memory production. Its record profitability and favorable industry outlook make it a strong contender.

However, NVIDIA appears to be the better investment bet today. Its faster growth, 75% gross margin, expanding AI customer base and lower P/E multiple offer a more attractive mix of growth and relative value. Supply constraints, memory costs and geopolitical risks remain important considerations, but NVIDIA's leadership in AI computing gives it the edge.

Currently, NVIDIA sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), making it a must-pick compared with Lam Research, which has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

news.Title: 南韓KOSPI上演V型反轉收高0.3% 半導體雙雄強彈
news.Content:
受隔夜美股科技股重挫、中東局勢升溫及市場對人工智慧支出放緩疑慮的衝擊，南韓綜合股價指數KOSPI周五(23日)早盤面臨沉重賣壓，盤中一度重跌超過 4%，最低下探至 5305.98 點。不過，午後在半導體權值股買盤回流帶動下，大盤演出戲劇性的「V型反彈」，終場逆勢上漲 16.53 點或 0.30%，收在 5550.30 點。

其中，SK海力士因宣布撤回旗下固態硬碟子公司 Solidigm 的赴美掛牌上市(IPO)計畫，消除了長期困擾股價的潛在利空，自早盤下跌 4.3% 逆轉收漲 4.4%；三星電子尾盤也翻紅收漲約 0.46%。

針對周五的逆轉行情，Fibonacci Asset Management Global 執行長 Jung In Yun 指出：「早盤的拋售迅速反映了諸多利空消息，促使投資人逢低承接遭到超賣的股票。」

他進一步表示，美國公債殖利率大幅回落，有助於舒緩科技股的評價壓力；儘管市場對 AI 支出的疑慮猶存，但在企業獲利前景依然具備韌性的情況下，被壓低的股價已難以忽視。不過，他也強調：「當天的反轉雖展現出買盤承接意願，但若要形成可持續的復甦，仍需即將公布的企業財報給予信心。」

相較之下，三星證券股票銷售交易員 Roy Lim 則認為，這波回升「主要是技術性反彈，是機構投資人在 Solidigm 撤回上市案後買進海力士所推動。」

隨著 10 月以來韓股回檔近兩成，KOSPI 的 12 個月預估本益比已下滑至約 4.2 倍，成為 2006 年有紀錄以來首個跌破 5 倍門檻的兆美元級市場。彭博專欄作家 Garfield Reynolds 指出，南韓在經濟強勁成長期間，其市場折價不僅未縮小反而持續擴大，這意味著一旦市場情緒轉向，南韓股市後續極可能展現超越其他市場的強勁走勢。

然而，籌碼結構仍暗藏隱憂。iM Securities 研究員 Lee Sang-heon 分析，9 月外資大舉賣超時，有八成賣壓是由兩大半導體龍頭的買回庫藏股計畫吸收；他表示：「買回庫藏股僅提供了下檔支撐；當前的重挫並非單純因為庫藏股退場，而是因為市場已步入空頭階段。」

展望後市，韓亞證券研究員 Kim Rok-ho 預期，SK海力士財報將展現至少 30 兆韓元的額外股東回饋空間，且買回並註銷庫藏股的可能性高於發放股利。但未來資產證券研究員 Kim Seok-hwan示警，獲利及長期合約題材已充分反映於股價中，推升股價的動能自 8 月起由獲利成長轉向股東回饋，這項轉變本身可能就是景氣循環接近頂部的信號。

news.Title: Better Memory Stock: Micron vs. Sandisk
news.Content:
Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) and Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) are members of an elite club. Only four stocks in the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) have tripled or more so far in 2026. Micron and Sandisk make up half that group.

Sandisk has been the bigger winner by far this year. But that performance is water under the bridge. Which is the better memory stock to buy now?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Two different kinds of memory stocks

Micron and Sandisk are similar in some respects. However, they're two very different kinds of memory stocks.

The most important difference between the two companies is the types of memory they focus on. Micron makes high-bandwidth memory (HBM), dynamic random access memory (DRAM), and NAND memory. Sandisk specializes in NAND flash memory.

HBM is Micron's crown jewel these days. In the company's fiscal 2026 fourth quarter, HBM revenue growth exceeded total revenue growth. Management said that it has completed sales agreements "for the vast majority" of its 2027 calendar-year HBM supply at significantly higher prices than it obtained in 2026.

Sandisk's NAND flash focus has worked to its benefit, though. Surging NAND prices have allowed the company to capture the full upside without any dilution from memory chips that aren't experiencing as strong demand.

But artificial intelligence (AI) serves as a massive tailwind for both companies. Memory is critical to AI applications. In particular, the shift to inference and the rising adoption of agentic AI are driving significant demand for multiple types of memory.

By the numbers: how Micron and Sandisk compare

Micron is much bigger than Sandisk. Its market cap tops $1 trillion, making Micron one of the world's top 10 largest technology companies . Meanwhile, Sandisk's market cap is around $200 billion.

Unsurprisingly, Micron also makes more money than Sandisk. In its latest quarter, Micron reported revenue of $54.2 billion and earnings of $37.7 billion. Sandisk's revenue in its latest quarter was $8.97 billion, with earnings of $6.9 billion.

Both companies boast impressive growth. In its fiscal 2026 Q4, Sandisk's revenue soared 372% year over year and 51% quarter over quarter. Micron's fiscal Q4 revenue jumped 379% year over year and roughly 31% quarter over quarter.

Micron and Sandisk are cyclical stocks, which is reflected in their valuations. Micron's shares trade at only seven times forward earnings, while Sandisk's forward earnings multiple is 8x.

Story Continues

Wall Street likes both memory stocks, although the bullish views seem somewhat stronger for Micron. Of the 29 analysts who rated Micron over the past three months, 27 (93%) recommended buying the stock. The consensus 12-month price target for Micron reflects a potential upside of around 74%. Of the 17 analysts who rated Sandisk over the past three months, 15 (88%) recommended buying the stock. The average price target for Sandisk is roughly 60% above the current share price.

The verdict

Both Micron and Sandisk could (and probably will) continue to deliver exceptional returns over the next few years. But I think that Micron is the better memory stock overall.

While Sandisk's pure-play NAND focus is its greatest strength, it's also the company's most significant risk. If NAND prices fall, Sandisk's revenue and profits will sink. Micron faces risks, too, but its breadth across multiple types of memory should provide some cushion.

I also think that Micron could have a bigger long-term opportunity. In particular, I'm excited about the company's prospects in the humanoid robotics market. Humanoid robots require enormous low-power memory. Micron is investing to meet expected demand and believes it will enjoy "a sustained, substantial multi-decade memory demand cycle" beginning later this decade.

My verdict aligns with Wall Street's take on these two stocks. Micron is the better pick right now.

中國A股三大股指今(23)日開低走高，上證指數( SSEC ) 結束連2日跌勢，盤中一度失守3600點，創業板指亦終止連跌9日頹勢，本周滬指累跌0.69%，深證成指累跌1.09%，創業板指累跌3.18%

滬指今日收漲0.89%至3690.48點，深證成指( SZI ) 收高2.79%，報11673.83點，創業板指收紅4.16%至2684.1點，滬深兩市成交額人民幣1.96兆元，較前一天放量逾4200億元。

盤面上，人形機器人族群大漲，宇樹科技漲停，本週累漲逾46%，大業股連6天漲停，福萊新材出現5個交易來第3根漲停板，華陽智能、正裕工業、襄陽軸承連2日亮燈，宇樹科技，萬向錢潮、山東威達、派斯林、大豐實業漲停；科創次新股表現亮眼，燧原科技、沐曦股份、摩爾線程等多股漲超10%；晶片股回暖，粵芯半導體、利亞德、奧普特等多股漲停；大金融類股拉升，匯金科技、華林證券、大智慧漲停；影視院線族群走高，中廣天擇、慈文傳媒漲停。

下跌族群方面，電力類股走勢較弱，閩東電力、皖能電力、黔源電力紛紛下挫；銀行族群震盪回落，中國銀行跌超4%，工商銀行、建設銀行跌超3%，農業銀行、江蘇銀行、交通銀行亦跟跌。

消息面上，OpenAI切入人形機器人賽道，執行長奧特曼稱該公司正組建名為「OpenAI Robotics」的新團隊，並公開招募全端硬體、營運、系統及機器學習工程師。本周一(19日)，特斯拉向美國證交會(SEC)提交2026年年度股東大會相關文件，特斯拉在同期提交的年度股東報告中明確表示，第三代Optimus人形機器人已為大規模量產做好準備。

此外，國際顧問機構弗若斯特沙利文近日公布《2026年全球人形機器人市場研究報告》，揭露業界最新產銷數據。今年上半年全球人形機器人銷售達3.6萬台，已超越去年全年3.5萬台的規模，同期市場營收為5.4億美元，產業商業化進程明顯加速。

中信證券表示，當下市場風險偏好、情緒接近冰點，三季報在本月中陸續披露，A股市場可望進行主題投資行情風格切換。此外，機器人流動性、估值、政策、技術、鏈主等催化大都符合過去七輪機器人上漲行情特徵，因此，從策略角度來看，中信證券認為機器人主題行情目前已具備啟動條件。

中歐基金出具研報指出，當前市場處於情緒冰點附近的高波動階段，但需區分兩層邏輯：全球長端利率高位、油價與地緣擾動疊加存量資金調倉，屬於估值與流動性層面的衝擊，往往帶來非線性的殺跌；海外AI資本開支仍在上行，記憶體與算力供給偏緊等線索並修緊，等潛在客戶反映動人的威脅性趨勢。

news.Title: 台股逃過一劫？ 日股跌幅收斂、韓翻紅 「這巨頭」大漲逾4%
news.Content:
受到AI巨頭Meta資本支出攀升疑慮加劇，以及年期信用違約交換報價創近一年以來最高，美股費半指數重挫，影響日韓股市今（23）日同步下挫，日經225指數一度大跌逾1400點，創近三個月新低；韓股KOSPI指數也一度下跌逾4%，不過隨著低接買盤進駐，日韓股午後跌幅明顯收斂，終場收跌214點，來到62693點；韓股收盤成功翻紅小漲0.3%，SK海力士也由黑翻紅勁揚4.42%。

日股盤中重挫逾1400點

日股今早延續日前頹勢，日經225指數盤中最低落至6萬1000點區間，一度重挫超過1400點，創7月底以來盤中新低；22日甚至下跌逾1700點，若與21日收盤價相比，兩日累計跌幅一度突破3000點；不過，午後隨著買盤進場，跌幅明顯收斂，終場收跌214點，來到62693點，跌幅0.34%。

日本金融圈分析，包含程式語言PHP安全漏洞問題在內，多項事件推升對AI產業監管加嚴的預期，進而拖慢技術進展，這一疑慮成為投資人拋售AI概念股的重要因素。

韓股同樣受美科技股暴跌拖累，KOSPI一度下跌超過412%，所幸午後指數逐漸回升，終場來到5550點，上漲0.3%，記憶體大廠SK海力士因旗下子公司Solidig取消赴美IPO計畫，激勵股價由黑翻紅，終場勁揚4.42%。。
