news.Title: 【跟著主動式ETF買1】不是台積電！00981A、00403A搶買欣興 一年大漲582%
news.Content:
主動式ETF成分股誰最會漲？《Yahoo股市》交叉比對規模前五大國內股票型主動式ETF的前十大持股，發現除了台積電（2330）、聯發科（2454）等大型權值股外，台光電（2383）、欣興（3037）及奇鋐（3017）也同時獲得四檔ETF青睞。若比較過去一年股價表現，欣興漲幅達582.39%，居共同持股之冠；但若以一年前買進一張、持有至今的價差試算，則由台光電以395萬元領先。

5大主動ETF規模達6298億元 這3檔獲四大ETF青睞

根據最新規模資料顯示，主動統一台股增長（00981A）以2,747億元居冠，其次為主動統一升級50（00403A）、主動中信台灣收益（00406A）、主動復華未來50（00991A）及主動群益台灣強棒（00982A），五檔合計規模達6,298億元。

進一步比對最新前十大股票持股，台積電及聯發科同時入列五檔ETF，台光電、欣興及奇鋐則獲四檔青睞；健策（3653）、旺矽（6223）、台達電（2308）及南電（8046）各進入三檔前十大持股。除了大型權值股，PCB（印刷電路板）、散熱及半導體相關供應鏈，也是這幾檔ETF經理人的主要配置方向。

欣興一年飆582%最會漲！台光電一張賺395萬元最多

若以去年10/22至今年10/22收盤價計算，欣興股價從159元漲至1,085元，一年漲幅達582.39%，為共同持股中漲幅最高的個股；南電以359.17%居次，台光電上漲352.68%，排名第三。

若一年前買進一張，以今年10/22收盤價試算，台光電股價從1,120元漲至5,070元，一張價差獲利達395萬元，居共同持股之冠；健策以383.5萬元排名第二，旺矽以307萬元位居第三。至於漲幅最高的欣興，一張價差獲利則為92.6萬元。

00982A選股最不同！穩懋、亞翔等股入列

值得注意的是，五大主動式ETF的選股方向並非完全一致。00981A、00403A、00406A及00991A，共有台積電、聯發科、台光電、欣興及奇鋐等五檔股票同時進入前十大持股。

相較之下，主動群益台灣強棒（00982A）的前十大持股，除了台積電及聯發科，還包括穩懋（3105）、亞翔（6139）、致茂（2360）、緯穎（6669）及愛普*（6531）等個股，與其他四檔ETF的共同持股組合有所不同，也反映不同經理人的選股策略存在差異。

news.Title: 1分鐘讀財經》台積電ADR狂殺 夜盤又遭血洗！主動式ETF押「這3檔」保命？
news.Content:
小編今天（23）日精選5件國內外重要財經大事。由於市場對科技巨頭砸巨資投入AI的投資報酬率疑慮再起，美股週四（22日）科技與晶片股淪為重災區，費城半導體指數大幅重挫6.72%。其中台積電ADR暴跌4.52%，導致台指期夜盤終場狂跌580點，收在45,654點，失守46,000點大關。不過，台股今（23日）正好碰上颱風假休市，暫時躲過了這波崩盤賣壓。

台股近日跌破重要均線，多空交鋒持續升溫，伴隨盤勢劇烈震盪，各家主動式ETF經理人選股策略原先高度集中在科技股持股的版圖開始洗牌，目前僅剩台積電、台光電、聯發科三檔穩居ETF標配陣容，22日跌破季線，更見經理人狂加金融與傳產股。

【1】台股破季線 主動式ETF趁低掃貨

盤點22日主動式ETF經理人逢低進場掃貨標的，涵蓋台積電、鴻海、日月光投控、聯電等科技權值龍頭，還有台泥、南亞、台化、大成鋼、華航、中華電等低基期傳產股，另有欣銓、聯茂、台燿與力積電等電子零組件個股入列。值得注意的是，欣興、奇鋐、南亞、聯茂、日月光投控及中信金等6檔，更獲得至少2檔主動式台股ETF逢低同步加碼，成為經理人共識的低檔加碼首選。

【2】聯發科法說倒數 雙外資送暖

繼台積電與大立光之後，市場最關注的科技法說會聯發科，將在30日舉行。花旗環球證券指出，市場一直對聯發科TPU開發進度，以及新專案拓展抱持懷疑態度，但聯發科TPU v8專案進展符合預期，今年相關營收可望達到20億美元以上，將成為推動第四季營收強勁成長的重要催化劑（catalyst）；野村證券則提出，市場對聯發科部分擔憂過度，重申「買進」投資評等。

【3】勞保費率明年調升為13％ 雇主年成本增逾百億元

勞動部勞保局22日指出，依《勞工保險條例》規定，勞工保險保險費率自明年1月1日起，由現行12.5％調整為13％，經扣除內含的就業保險費率1％，2027年起，將以12％計收勞工保險保險費。據估算，雇主明年全年可能因此增加逾133.3億元的法定成本。

【4】AI基建燒錢 Meta自由現金流轉負 降至負21.2億美元

Meta公布第三季財報，營收創歷史新高，第四季財測也優於市場預期，但AI軍備競賽的代價浮現。公司調高2026年資本支出預估下限，自由現金流更創上市以來首度轉負，22日早盤股價重挫逾6％。

【5】特斯拉Q3業績報喜 下修全年資本支出

特斯拉第三季業績報喜，營收和獲利雙雙優於市場預期，且資本支出低於華爾街預測，讓上季現金流意外轉正，該公司同時下修全年資本支出。

news.Title: 5 Undervalued AI Stocks According to the Media
news.Content:
The AI trade is getting bumpy as investors question whether the massive spending on data centers and chips will generate sufficient returns. There is only so much capital companies can raise, and cracks are beginning to appear. Yet some prominent investors believe the market is underestimating how much further the AI boom can run.

Speaking to CNBC earlier this week, Altimeter Capital founder and Chief Executive Brad Gerstner said investors have spent the past two years worrying about an eventual glut of AI computing capacity, only to miss substantial gains in semiconductor stocks. He believes the boom still has room to run because physical constraints, including chip production capacity and electricity supply, are limiting how quickly companies can expand AI infrastructure.

Gerstner is one of the loudest AI bulls on Wall Street, and his fund keeps buying AI stocks. Check his top 10 stock picks here . His latest filings show new additions too. Read his two new AI picks here .

"I actually think you have a natural constraint here," Gerstner said on CNBC. "There's only so fast in terms of production of wafers in this country. It's only so fast that we can bring power on."

HSBC's Willem Sels also believes investors are underestimating the AI opportunity. In a September interview with Bloomberg Television, the bank's global chief investment officer said US stock valuations did not fully reflect the potential for AI-driven productivity gains and earnings growth. He particularly highlighted semiconductor companies, whose valuations he believes reflect skepticism about future earnings forecasts despite the possibility of continued strong demand.

"The US is not expensive. The markets are questioning the sustainability of earnings growth, but that's in the price because that gap has closed," Sels told Bloomberg.

So, what are the most undervalued stocks according to the media? We listed the 10 most undervalued AI stock here . You can find the top 5 below.

Photo by AlphaTradeZone

Up 3,700%, Should You Buy Sandisk Right Now?
news.Content:
The appreciation of Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) stock has been nothing short of phenomenal. Since its formal separation from Western Digital in February 2025, the stock has risen 3,700%, a feat unmatched by any large-cap stock over the same period.

Admittedly, no matter what its future holds, it is unlikely to repeat that growth within such a short time frame. However, history suggests that the chip stock is more likely to pull back than rise over time.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The rise (and possible future decline) of Sandisk

Indeed, when Sandisk spun off, it did not appear to be on the verge of massive growth. The company specializes in NAND memory and solid-state storage products. In general, memory and storage are commoditized products, and thus, the companies in that business tend to not attract as much investor interest.

Nonetheless, the boom in AI centers led to unprecedented demand for flash storage solutions. The stock price surged as AI stock investors and institutional investors took notice. Soon after, Sandisk joined the Nasdaq-100 and the S&P 500 , leading to additional buying.

The company's financials also played a major role in its gains. Its net income was over $11 billion in fiscal 2026, far better than the $1.6 billion loss in the previous fiscal year.

That profit left it with an attractive valuation despite its massive stock gains. Currently, its P/E ratio is 19, and the immediate future appears bright as its forward P/E stands at just 6.3.

Ironically, seasoned investors' long-term memory may explain the low valuations. These shareholders know that memory companies tend to experience more volatile industry cycles than tech stocks in general. This is because memory and storage command tremendous pricing power in boom times. However, when the down cycle begins, lower demand and price cuts can reduce or even wipe out company profits.

Sandisk has signed customers into long-term contracts, which could mitigate a down cycle. Still, slumps can be exceptionally painful for memory stocks. In the nearly nine years Western Digital owned Sandisk, its stock gained over 75%. Still, since it earned all of those gains in the first year of ownership, it is easy to see why Western Digital later doubted the wisdom of the merger and decided to spin off Sandisk.

Story Continues

The performance of both Sandisk and Western Digital stocks since the separation indicates the AI boom would have ended the slump with or without the separation. Still, performance in previous years suggests storage stocks have not performed well historically, possibly pointing to pain for Sandisk in the foreseeable future.

Should you buy Sandisk stock right now?

The history of Sandisk and its industry in general suggests one should approach its stock with caution.

With Sandisk dominating the S&P 500 in 2026, it implies that it is the stock to own. Still, the stocks in that industry have faced huge sell-offs once the boom ends. That history may also explain why investors have not bid the stock higher despite its 19 P/E ratio.

Indeed, if revenue forecasts prove accurate, Sandisk stock could continue rising. Nonetheless, given Sandisk's history and the history of the memory and storage industries in general, investors should probably assume they missed out on this boom.

news.Title: Fortinet (FTNT) vs. CSCO and PANW: Can Its Hardware-Software Advantage Support Long-Term Growth?
news.Content:
Is FTNT a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Fortinet, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on FTNT. Fortinet, Inc.'s share was trading at $170.93as of October 20th 2026. FTNT's trailing and forward P/E were 61.58 and 45.05 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a cybersecurity company pitched as a great investment. FTNT shares gained 101.90% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like CrowdStrike and Cisco Systems gained 81.86% and 51.02%, respectively, during the same period. Protecting businesses from cyber threats can create lasting demand, but a stock that has more than doubled also raises expectations. Does FTNT still offer an attractive buying opportunity, or has too much optimism already been priced in?

GlebStock/Shutterstock.com

In June, we published an article about the 12 Best Growth Stocks Trading in Oversold Territory and FTNT ranked #12 in that article. FTNT returned 14.34% since then. So, hedge funds were right about FTNT. This article explains why Jim Cramer favors Fortinet alongside CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Fortinet, Inc. (NASDAQ:FTNT) provides cybersecurity solutions that combine hardware, software, and security services. Its fastest-growing opportunity right now is enterprise cybersecurity demand, and that is central to understanding the stock. As companies expand into the cloud, adopt AI, and face more sophisticated cyberattacks, they need stronger network security — an area where Fortinet specializes.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

Revenue over the past year came in at $7.5 billion, up nearly 19%, with gross margin at 80.2% and operating margin at 32.4%. Despite this strength, the stock isn't cheap: it trades at about 54 times trailing earnings and 45 times forward earnings, well above the peer median of roughly 33 times, suggesting investors are betting on several more years of growth rather than paying only for today's numbers.

The bullish case is that Fortinet can keep growing alongside the expanding cybersecurity market while converting that growth into strong cash flow. Unlike many competitors, it builds its own hardware and software together — including its FortiASIC security chips — which helps it stand out in firewall and network security markets. Results back this up: the company generated $2.2 billion in free cash flow last fiscal year, holds a net cash position of $3.6 billion, and posted a very high return on equity of about 150%.

Story Continues

Management keeps expanding the platform, including its August 2026 purchase of Virtue AI, a company focused on AI-related cybersecurity, aimed at strengthening its position in that growing niche. If businesses keep raising security spending, bulls see years of growth ahead rather than a short-lived cycle. Still, the company needs to prove it can sustain its growth rate and protect its high margins without losing ground to competitors.

Recent results support the bullish story. Second-quarter revenue grew 26% year over year to $2.05 billion, and product revenue jumped 52% to $773 million — both signs that demand is accelerating. Billings, a signal of future revenue, rose 33% to $2.37 billion, while free cash flow reached $966 million for the quarter. Following these results, management raised full-year guidance, now expecting revenue between $8.02 billion and $8.18 billion and adjusted earnings per share between $3.41 and $3.47. The stronger outlook backs the case that growth is broad-based, though investors will want to see whether this pace holds up.

Investors are also watching how durable this growth is, not just how large it is. Fortinet's high margins reflect real pricing power and scale, but holding them steady could get harder as competition rises and enterprise customers grow more selective about spending.

Valuation remains the central debate around Fortinet's stock. Bulls argue that if growth and margins keep improving, the stock could reach $220, while a base case of around $165 assumes steady execution and a stable valuation. The bear case, on the other hand, sees the stock falling toward $102 if growth slows, margins shrink, or investors decide the current multiple is too rich. That range reflects real disagreement about how much more Fortinet can grow into its premium price tag. With the stock trading at about 54 times trailing earnings and 45 times forward earnings, continued strong execution is essential to justify that premium.

AI security is a promising growth avenue, but cybersecurity spending still tends to concentrate among a relatively small group of large enterprise customers, adding some unpredictability. The Virtue AI acquisition gives Fortinet a foothold in AI security, but it still needs to show these new products can translate into meaningful revenue. Investors should also watch ongoing shareholder lawsuits and the company's reliance on specialized chip suppliers, both of which could pressure sentiment if conditions worsen.

Another risk for the stock is the potential loss of customer trust if Fortinet's security products fail to protect against cyberattacks. Customers rely on its firewalls and software to protect critical systems, so an exploited vulnerability could damage trust in the wider platform. Fortinet warns that product defects and unsuccessful security updates could expose customers to attacks or disrupt operations. Its integrated approach makes reliability across those products especially important. A serious incident could slow new sales and weaken subscription renewals. Remediation and customer support costs could also weigh on margins. In our opinion, this could pressure Fortinet's price multiples if customers question its ability to provide the protection underpinning its growth story.

Hedge fund positioning shows a strong signal for Fortinet (see why Emerald Wealth Partners is bullish on FTNT ). As per our database, 62 hedge funds held the stock at the end of the second quarter, up from 52 in the previous quarter. This notable jump suggests institutional investors are growing more confident in the company's growth prospects, profitability, and balance sheet strength, even with its rich valuation. By comparison, Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW) was held by 89 hedge funds, up from 87, Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) was held by 101 hedge funds, up from 97, and CrowdStrike (NASDAQ:CRWD) was held by 89 hedge funds, up from 79. The increase in hedge fund ownership across Fortinet, Palo Alto Networks, Cisco Systems, and CrowdStrike points to continued institutional interest in cybersecurity. CrowdStrike saw the strongest increase in conviction, while Fortinet's larger jump compared with Palo Alto Networks and Cisco Systems highlights improving sentiment despite the company's premium valuation.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture for the group. Just 2.06% of Fortinet, Inc.'s float is sold short, compared with 2.66% for Palo Alto Networks, Inc., 2.60% for CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc., and 1.30% for Cisco Systems, Inc. Bearish bets remain low across all four stocks, suggesting limited outright bearish conviction. Fortinet, Inc.'s short interest sits above Cisco Systems, Inc.'s but below Palo Alto Networks, Inc.'s and CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc.'s, indicating somewhat more skepticism than Cisco Systems, Inc. faces, but less than its other two peers.

Valuation Analysis

FTNT's forward P/E is 45.05x. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc., Cisco Systems, Inc., and Palo Alto Networks, Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 208.33x, 19.80x, and 94.34x, respectively. FTNT's own forward P/E was 27.17x on December 31, 2025, meaning its current valuation is approximately 66% higher. We believe the current valuation reflects significant investor confidence in accelerating cybersecurity demand, Fortinet's integrated platform, and its strong profitability. However, its discount to CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks does not establish a bargain, since differences in growth prospects and earnings adjustments limit direct comparisons. Fortinet, Inc.'s second-quarter adjusted earnings per share increased from $0.64 to $0.90, representing approximately 41% growth, alongside revenue growth of approximately 26%. We believe this performance supports a premium, but investors should not assume that one quarter's earnings growth will continue long enough to justify 45.05 times forward earnings, particularly after the substantial increase in its multiple. If Fortinet sustains strong earnings growth and protects its margins, profits could support further upside, but we would prefer a lower entry valuation to reduce the risk that a falling P/E offsets those gains.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Fortinet, Inc. (FTNT) by Dan in January 2025, which highlighted Fortinet's AI-powered cybersecurity expansion, acquisitions, product innovation, and Secure Networking growth. FTNT's stock price has appreciated by approximately 79.94% since our coverage. We believe FTNT could be a good long-term investment at a lower price, as its premium valuation could limit returns even if earnings continue growing strongly.

Fortinet, Inc. is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds . While FTNT could benefit from growing cybersecurity demand and expansion into AI security, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential at more attractive valuations, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. news.Title: Chip stocks break a bear trap after a $3 trillion rout — here are the levels bulls need to hold
news.Content: Chip bulls sprang a bear trap on Tuesday. Two sessions later, the floor under it has cracked. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) fell more than 6% Thursday, closing below 11,000 — the support that rescued the group twice since September. A bear trap is a breakdown that quickly reverses, catching traders who bet on further losses. This one only worked as long as that floor held. It was the index's worst day since June and its lowest close since July 29. The damage is piling up. All 60 stocks in a Yahoo Finance chip basket are down since Oct. 6, erasing more than $3 trillion in market value, more than $900 billion of it Thursday alone. Lam Research ( LRCX ) and Applied Materials ( AMAT ) have each lost about 30% in that span, and AMD ( AMD ) more than 20%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) has fallen less, but on its size that's more than $600 billion. Lam led Thursday's slide after reporting record revenue Wednesday night. The company said supply limits capped its outlook and that China sales will be "meaningfully down" in December. The selling isn't sparing the giants. Meta ( META ) shed more than $120 billion in market value after its earnings, and SpaceX ( SPCX ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) slid too. Still, the Nasdaq 100 ( ^NDX ) is down about 7% since Oct. 6. Chips are down more than twice as much. The 11,000 floor cracked The index closed near 11,130 on Sept. 14 and again on Oct. 16. Tuesday's dip into that zone reversed sharply, springing the trap. Thursday's break puts the 10,450-10,550 zone in focus. That's where the summer rally started on July 29. The 200-day moving average sits just above it, and Thursday's low stopped a few points short of that line. On the upside, bulls first need to win back 11,000, then 12,600-12,700. That area capped rallies in August and September. Dip buyers haven't given up Semiconductor ETFs saw record flows over the past week, Bloomberg senior ETF analyst Eric Balchunas posted Thursday. "Buying the dip here has [a] pretty good record of working," he wrote. There's little room to hide from the AI trade. "Every index on the planet is basically an AI index," Matt Miskin, co-chief investment strategist at Manulife John Hancock Investments, said on Yahoo Finance's live show Thursday. The close below 11,000 puts the 10,500 area in play if the 200-day gives way. Bulls need a close back above 11,000 in the next couple of days to revive the trap. news.Title: Taiwan Semiconductor and ASML Are Incredible, but 1 of These Monopoly Chip Stocks Is Far Safer.
news.Content:
There are few companies on the market more impressive than Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) and ASML Holding (NASDAQ: ASML). Both are essentially monopolies for different reasons, but each is an incredible business and has rewarded shareholders with strong stock performance.

However, these two aren't the same from an investment standpoint. One is far safer, and it all boils down to how much success is priced into the stock. I think Taiwan Semiconductor is the far safer bet for multiple reasons, making it the better investment right now. Here's why.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

How are these two monopolies?

There are different types of monopolies, and not all of them are viewed the same way. When it comes to monopolies, ASML is about as good as it gets. It is the only company in the world with the technology to make extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. These machines are about as big as a school bus and cost hundreds of millions of dollars.

EUV machines are used by chip fabricators, such as Taiwan Semiconductor, to lay down tiny electrical traces on chips. These traces are microscopic and have spacing as little as 2 nanometers (nm) apart. For reference, a human hair is 80,000 to 100,000 nanometers across. With ASML being the sole supplier of a critical machine in the chip manufacturing world, it has a very solid technological monopoly that will be nearly impossible to break.

Taiwan Semiconductor's monopoly status is a bit more shaky but still impressive. There are several other chip foundries out there, and many have the same advanced technology available to make the highest-performance chips possible. However, nobody has the scale that TSMC does.

During Q2, Taiwan Semiconductor accounted for about 72.5% of revenue in the chip fabrication industry . That's a major size advantage that holds its clients captive, because they couldn't move all of their work to another foundry if they tried, since its competitors wouldn't have the necessary scale.

While this advantage could be challenged over time by a rising competitor, there's nobody even close right now. TSMC has great relationships with its clientele, so I doubt its grip on this industry will be broken anytime over the next decade.

While I would say ASML's monopoly status is stronger than TSMC's, I can't say the same about their businesses or stocks.

Story Continues

ASML is on shakier ground than TSMC

ASML's business model requires its clients to expand production capacity to sell more machines. While it makes revenue servicing these machines every year, it's not nearly as much as outright selling them.

Business is good for ASML right now because every chip manufacturer (including TSMC) is racing to expand production capacity to meet demand from the AI build-out . However, once the AI build-out is complete, there may not be a need to expand chip production capacity for some time, which could harm ASML's business.

At the same time, while TSMC may not be growing, there could be other technologies that require a substantial number of chips, such as humanoid robots, physical AI, or self-driving cars. That would allow Taiwan Semiconductor to maintain the business size it has achieved, making it a better long-term investment. However, none of this is reflected in the stock's valuation.

TSM PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

ASML trades at a sizable premium to Taiwan Semiconductor when using 2026 earnings estimates. That same trend persists when 2027 earnings are used.

TSM PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts

So, ASML is a more expensive stock but with a less certain long-term demand outlook. While monopoly stocks may be safer, I'm more concerned about how they will fare when the current demand wave wraps up. As a result, I think Taiwan Semiconductor is a far safer investment option.

news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Susquehanna is reshuffling price targets across the semiconductor sector ahead of earnings, raising its outlook for AMD ( NASDAQ:AMD ), Qualcomm ( NASDAQ:QCOM ) and Skyworks Solutions while cutting targets for Intel ( NASDAQ:INTC ), Onsemi, Cirrus Logic and Wolfspeed.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with AMD.

The firm raised AMD's target to $620 from $550 , Qualcomm's to $185 from $160 , and Skyworks' to $90 from $65 .

Intel's target was cut to $105 from $115 , while Onsemi was reduced to $120 from $150. Cirrus Logic and Wolfspeed were also lowered.

Susquehanna analyst Christopher Rolland said AI remains the biggest source of upside, but the broader semiconductor cycle is also improving.

The firm's SemiSIGnals data showed lead times expanding by roughly two weeks for a second consecutive quarter , while pricing actions are becoming more aggressive.

Susquehanna also expects additional price increases in the fourth quarter and into 2027.

The problem is that not every end market is participating equally.

PC demand is tracking below expectations, which could leave second-half client results for both AMD and Intel below normal seasonal patterns.

In response, both companies are shifting wafer capacity away from PCs and toward servers, where demand tied to agentic AI remains much stronger.

Susquehanna also expects ARM-based hyperscale CPUs to keep gaining share as they increasingly serve as host processors for custom AI accelerators.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most important part of Susquehanna's note is the widening split between AI-driven data center demand and weaker consumer electronics .

For AMD, that is relatively favorable because server demand gives the company another avenue to offset softness in PCs.

For Intel, the same shift helps, but weaker client demand still creates more pressure on the near-term setup.

Qualcomm benefits from the high end of the handset market holding up better, although Susquehanna remains cautious on smartphones overall because of memory constraints and deteriorating demand in China.

For investors, the key things to watch are server revenue, wafer reallocation, semiconductor pricing, hyperscaler capex and whether PC and handset weakness becomes more severe .

The chip cycle still appears to be improving.

But increasingly, the strongest part of that recovery is concentrated around AI infrastructure rather than broad-based consumer demand.

news.Title: Prediction: Sandisk Stock Will Soar After Oct. 29. Here Are 379 Billion Reasons Why
news.Content:
Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock has fallen from grace in recent months after delivering a stunning performance in the first half of 2026.

Shares of the flash storage specialist have pulled back 32% since the beginning of July. For comparison, Sandisk stock rose by a stunning 858% in the first half of 2026. The recent slide in Sandisk stock has nothing to do with the company's financial performance. Investors have pressed the panic button and are booking profits in Sandisk amid concerns about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure build-out .

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

However, a closer look at the developments in the NAND flash industry suggests that the fears about a slowdown in Sandisk's growth are overblown. In fact, I won't be surprised to see the company deliver stronger-than-expected fiscal 2027 first-quarter results on Oct. 29.

Let's check the reasons why Sandisk stock could take off following its upcoming quarterly report.

Image source: Getty Images.

Sandisk's growth and potential don't justify its slide

The incredible demand for NAND flash storage in AI data centers has been Sandisk's biggest growth driver. The resulting supply shortage has led to a massive increase in NAND flash prices, which explains the red-hot growth in Sandisk's revenue and earnings.

The company expects fiscal Q1 revenue of $10.3-$10.8 billion, along with non-GAAP earnings of $45.00 per share. The guidance implies a year-over-year increase of 357% in revenue at the midpoint, along with a 37x jump in non-GAAP earnings per share. Market research firm TrendForce expects NAND flash prices to surge by 235% in 2026, which explains why Sandisk is anticipating such phenomenal growth in fiscal Q1.

Even better, analysts expect Sandisk to sustain its red-hot growth in the current quarter as well. Consensus estimates on Yahoo! Finance predict a 4x year-over-year increase in Sandisk's revenue in the current quarter to $12.2 billion. Meanwhile, earnings per share could increase by 8x to $52.94. So, the recent slide in Sandisk's stock price isn't justified when we consider that the strong NAND flash demand and price environment will continue to remain a tailwind for the company.

Moreover, the NAND flash market is poised for further growth in 2027. TrendForce expects NAND flash industry revenue to reach $379 billion in 2027, up 40% from this year. Of course, the market's growth rate is expected to slow substantially next year compared with 2026's estimated 280%, but that's still a healthy number.

Story Continues

Importantly, Sandisk can make the most of this huge opportunity given that it controls 11% of the NAND flash market, according to Counterpoint Research. A similar share of this market at the end of 2027 could send Sandisk's revenue in calendar 2027 to almost $42 billion, double the revenue it has generated over the past twelve months.

So, Sandisk seems poised to grow at a robust pace over the next year and a half, given the incredible $379 billion addressable opportunity it is sitting on. Throw in the fact that the NAND flash industry will remain undersupplied in 2027 and 2028, according to Citi , and Sandisk should also be able to clock healthy earnings growth.

This probably explains why there has been a slight uptick in Sandisk's earnings per share expectations for the current and the next fiscal year.

SNDK EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

A stronger-than-expected outlook can supercharge the stock

One of the reasons why this AI stock has been under pressure lately is because of concerns that NAND flash supply growth will overtake demand next year. This could erase the pricing advantage that Sandisk has been enjoying.

However, the points discussed above suggest otherwise. Additionally, robust NAND flash demand from AI servers could lead to a sequential increase of 15%-20% in NAND flash contract prices in the current quarter, according to TrendForce. This is why I think Sandisk's guidance for the ongoing quarter may exceed expectations, giving the stock a much-needed boost.

Another reason why Sandisk seems like a no-brainer buy right now is that it trades at an extremely cheap 8 times forward earnings. The S&P 500 index, for comparison, has a forward earnings multiple of 19. Sandisk should ideally trade at a significant premium given its exponential growth rate. So, it makes sense for savvy investors to buy this growth stock before Oct. 29 as strong results and a sunny guidance could set it up for a strong finish to the year.

news.Title: Vicor Corporation Shares Gain 4.5% on Strong Q3 Earnings Growth
news.Content:
Vicor Corporation VICR shares have gained 4.5% since it reported third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 20. The uptick can be attributed to strong AI-driven demand and rising recurring royalty revenues, which lifted sales, margins and profitability.

The company reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $1.33 per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.32%. The figure increased 111.1% year over year.

Revenues surged 78.5% year over year to $197.11 million and surpassed the consensus estimate by 5.4%. Strong Advanced Products sales and higher royalty income supported growth. The company's order backlog increased 166% year over year to $406 million, reflecting robust demand.

VICR's Advanced Products Revenues Accelerate

Advanced Products revenues, including royalties, increased 47.5% sequentially to $138.9 million. The business accounted for 70.4% of total revenues, up from 65.7% in the preceding quarter.

Vicor Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Vicor Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Vicor Corporation Quote

Brick Products revenues increased 18.4% sequentially to $58.3 million and represented 29.6% of total revenues.

Shipments to stocking distributors increased 24.8% sequentially and 16.2% year over year. Exports accounted for approximately 36.1% of revenues, down from 46% in the second quarter of 2026.

Vicor Benefits From Expanding Royalty Income

Product revenues totaled $130.5 million, up 47.1% year over year. Royalty revenues surged 206.6% year over year to $66.6 million from $21.7 million. Sequentially, royalty revenues increased 119.1%, supported by licensing agreements.

The company granted its first vertical power delivery (VPD) license to a leading artificial intelligence (AI) original equipment manufacturer at Stage 2-unit royalty rates. Management noted that part of the quarterly royalty contribution reflected initial payments, while the underlying licensing arrangements provide recurring income.

Vicor also received inquiries from hyperscalers regarding broader licensing agreements. Management expects royalty income to grow as additional customers adopt its intellectual property, although the timing of payments and new agreements could create quarterly fluctuations.

VICR's Backlog Reflects Strong Market Demand

The book-to-bill ratio remained above 1, while backlog increased 7% sequentially to $380 million. Management highlighted approximately $100 million in bookings during the first two weeks of the fourth quarter, including a substantial order for second-generation VPD modules.

Demand remained strong across AI computing, automatic test equipment (ATE), industrial, aerospace and defense markets. The company's ATE business, which serves semiconductor and memory testing applications, now generates more than $100 million in annual revenues.

Management highlighted growing customer interest in second-generation VPD technology following demonstrations at Open Compute. The technology aims to address increasing power density and efficiency requirements for advanced AI processors.

Story Continues

Vicor's Margins Expand Despite Rising Expenses

Gross profit increased sequentially to $134.7 million from $83.1 million. Gross margin expanded 1,030 basis points to 68.3%, benefiting from higher royalty revenues, improved product mix, manufacturing efficiencies and increased volumes.

Operating expenses increased 29.6% sequentially to $62.5 million. Legal expenses, a substantial portion of which are linked to royalty revenues, increased approximately $11.1 million to $16.1 million. Management expects legal expenses to average approximately 20% of royalty revenues in the near term.

Operating income surged 245.1% year over year to $72.1 million from $20.9 million in the year-ago quarter.

VICR Strengthens Cash Position and Expands Capacity

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $513.1 million compared with $453.6 million in the previous quarter.

Operating activities generated $69.7 million in cash compared with $34 million in the second quarter.

Vicor acquired two additional manufacturing sites within 30 miles of its existing Andover facility. The planned Fab-2 and Fab-3 facilities could increase manufacturing capacity nearly fivefold relative to Fab-1.

Management expects initial equipment deployment at Fab-2 in the second quarter of 2027. The expansion will initially target capacity-constrained manufacturing processes. The company expects to fund its expansion plans without raising additional capital.

Vicor Expects Further Product Revenue Growth

Vicor expects fourth-quarter 2026 product revenues to increase approximately 10% sequentially. The outlook assumes another double-digit sequential increase in Advanced Products hardware revenues.

Management also expects at least $43 million in fourth-quarter royalty revenues, assuming no additional licensing agreements. Existing arrangements could generate incremental royalties beyond this baseline.

The company anticipates further margin expansion as revenues increase and manufacturing utilization improves. However, near-term capacity constraints at Fab-1 remain a consideration as Vicor works to expand production capabilities and meet growing customer demand.

Zacks Rank & Upcoming Earnings to Watch

Vicor currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

news.Title: Can Semiconductor Systems Drive AMAT's Next Growth Phase?
news.Content:
Applied Materials AMAT is gaining from rising demand for advanced chips used in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, especially in its Semiconductor Systems business. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Semiconductor Systems generated revenues of $7.04 billion, up approximately 27% year over year.

Growing investment in leading-edge foundry-logic, dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and advanced packaging is creating opportunities for the company's wafer fabrication equipment, while rising manufacturing complexity supports demand for differentiated process technologies.

Applied Materials is expanding its technology portfolio to capitalize on these opportunities. Its Centris Spectral SiN ALD system supports advanced logic manufacturing, while enhanced Centura Prime epitaxy and Producer Avila 2 PECVD systems target DRAM performance and higher-layer-count high-bandwidth memory.

Beyond revenue growth, Semiconductor Systems is strengthening Applied Materials' profitability. Its non-GAAP gross margin increased to 55.4% in the third quarter from 53.5% a year earlier. The operating margin expanded to 38% from 33.2%, reflecting the value of its technology portfolio and operating leverage.

AMAT anticipates fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 Semiconductor Systems revenues to be approximately $7.9 billion, suggesting 62% year-over-year growth. The outlook indicates that demand across leading-edge logic, DRAM and advanced packaging could sustain strong near-term momentum.

How Competitors Fare Against AMAT

Applied Materials faces competition from Lam Research (LRCX), KLA Corporation (KLAC) and other semiconductor equipment suppliers, although their primary areas of specialization differ. Lam Research secured multiple critical etch wins at a major DRAM manufacturer with its new Akara etch system, which supports 3D DRAM architectures. This was supported by LRCX's customer investments in DDR5, LPDDR5 and high-bandwidth memory.

Lam Research's Aether dry-resist technology was recently selected as the production tool of record for a leading DRAM customer, securing a foothold in this high-growth segment. Although KLA does not compete directly with AMAT across its entire Semiconductor Systems portfolio, both companies can benefit from rising investment in advanced logic, high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging.

Applied Materials shares have climbed 59.1% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's appreciation of 15.9% and 18%, respectively.

news.Title: MRVL Taps Into AI Infrastructure Growth: What's Next for Investors?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology MRVL is benefiting from rising demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, with its custom silicon, optical interconnect and switching solutions driving strong data center growth. The company's expanding partnerships and broader product portfolio are strengthening its position in next-generation AI systems. However, margin pressures, customer concentration and a premium valuation remain key considerations for investors.

Marvell's second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues increased 36.5% year over year to $2.74 billion, driven by hyperscalers, as they continued investing in AI infrastructure. Demand for 800G optical digital signal processors (DSPs) remained strong, while next-generation 1.6T products ramped up rapidly. Meanwhile, scale-out switching revenues are expected to more than double in fiscal 2027, supported by growing adoption of its 51.2T switching products.

Marvell expects its custom silicon business to accelerate in the second half of fiscal 2027, with revenues projected to more than double year over year in fiscal 2028. Demand for custom accelerators and related connectivity solutions is creating opportunities as hyperscalers develop increasingly sophisticated AI systems.

The company is also expanding its networking capabilities across scale-up, scale-out and scale-across architectures. Its strategic partnership with NVIDIA strengthens its participation in next-generation AI infrastructure through NVLink Fusion integration, optics and related connectivity technologies. Recent acquisitions of Celestial AI and XConn Technologies further broaden its technology portfolio.

How Competitors Fare Against MRVL

In the data center market, MRVL faces stiff competition from Broadcom AVGO and Advanced Micro Devices AMD.

Broadcom is a leader in the domain of custom silicon solutions for data centers. Broadcom's advanced 3.5D XDSiP packaging platform is critical to ensure the performance and efficiency of custom AI XPUs. Broadcom's relationships with leading hyperscale and frontier AI customers give it direct insight into workload requirements and help shape differentiated accelerators. The company continues to work with six core XPU customers across multiyear programs.

Advanced Micro Devices is another established player in the custom silicon solutions and AI accelerator market. Advanced Micro Devices offers semi-custom SoCs and Instinct Accelerators to power data centers. AMD is broadening its data center AI opportunity from Instinct accelerators to the Helios rack-scale platform. In the second quarter of 2026, Data Center revenues rose 107% year over year to $6.7 billion, while Instinct sales more than doubled.

Story Continues

MRVL's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Marvell Technology shares have rallied 188.1% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry and Zacks Computer and Technology sector's appreciation of 16% and 18%, respectively.

news.Title: Buy, Sell or Hold AMKR Stock? Key Tips Ahead of Q3 Earnings
news.Content:
Amkor Technology AMKR is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 26.

For the quarter, the company expects revenues between $1.95 billion and $2.05 billion. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for revenues is pegged at $2.02 billion, indicating year-over-year growth of 1.54%.

Amkor Technology projects earnings between 72 cents and 82 cents per share. The consensus mark for earnings stands at 79 cents per share, reflecting growth of 54.9% from the year-ago quarter. The consensus EPS estimate has remained unchanged over the past 30 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AMKR's Earnings Surprise History

Amkor Technology has an impressive earnings surprise history, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the trailing four quarters and delivering an average earnings surprise of 43.58%. In the second quarter of 2026, the company reported earnings of 70 cents per share, beating the consensus estimate of 47 cents by 43.58%.

Amkor Technology, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Amkor Technology, Inc. price-eps-surprise | Amkor Technology, Inc. Quote

Q3 Earnings Whispers for AMKR Stock

Our proven model does not conclusively predict an earnings beat for Amkor Technology this time around. According to the Zacks model, a positive Earnings ESP combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold) increases the odds of an earnings beat.

AMKR has an Earnings ESP of 0.00% and currently carries a Zacks Rank #3. You can uncover potential earnings-beat candidates with the Zacks Earnings ESP Filter.

Key Factors Expected to Shape AMKR's Q3 2026 Results

Amkor Technology is expected to have benefited from accelerating demand for AI data center and high-performance computing applications in the third quarter of 2026. The Computing end market achieved record revenues in the second quarter, increasing 20% sequentially. Management expects Computing revenues to grow nearly 30% sequentially in the third quarter, supported by robust AI infrastructure demand and the continued ramp-up of its high-density fan-out (HDFO) data center CPU program. Growing adoption of advanced packaging technologies is likely to have strengthened the company's revenue growth in the quarter under review.

Amkor Technology is expected to have gained from strong demand across its Automotive and Industrial end market, driven by increasing semiconductor content in vehicles and growing adoption of advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). The segment achieved record revenues in the preceding quarter, growing 17% sequentially. Management expects mid-single-digit sequential growth in the third quarter. Additionally, the Consumer end market is expected to have benefited from broad-based Internet of Things (IoT) demand, with revenues projected to increase in the mid-teens percentage range sequentially. These trends are likely to have supported overall revenue growth.

The company is anticipated to have benefited from an improving product mix and higher utilization of advanced packaging capacity. Its advanced products generated $1.56 billion in second-quarter revenues, accounting for approximately 82% of total sales. Accelerating HDFO production and growing demand for higher-value Computing applications are expected to have supported profitability in the third quarter. Management projects gross margin between 18.5% and 19.5%, compared with 16.8% in the preceding quarter. Strategic collaborations with TSMC and NVIDIA further strengthen Amkor Technology's long-term competitive position in advanced packaging.

However, Amkor Technology is expected to have faced headwinds in its Communications end market during the third quarter of 2026. Management anticipates a high-single-digit sequential revenue decline, departing from typical seasonal demand patterns. Ongoing memory supply constraints, changes in smartphone production schedules and softer Android demand are likely to have weighed on performance. Android revenues declined 20% sequentially in the preceding quarter due to memory supply dynamics. Given that Communications contributed 42% of second-quarter revenues, these challenges are expected to have partially offset growth in Computing and other end markets.

Amkor Technology's ongoing transition of system-in-package (SiP) manufacturing from Korea to Vietnam is also expected to have affected third-quarter revenues. The strategic relocation involves equipment transfers, customer qualifications and production ramp-ups, potentially creating temporary shipment disruptions. Management indicated that certain applications could experience headwinds extending into the fourth quarter and the first half of 2027. Although the transition is intended to improve manufacturing efficiency and release capacity in Korea for advanced Computing programs, near-term execution challenges are likely to have constrained Communications revenues in the quarter under review.

Story Continues

AMKR's Stock Price Performance & Valuation

Amkor Technology's shares have risen 36.7% in the past year, substantially outperforming both the Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, which gained 18.4% and 13.7%, respectively. AMKR's strong performance also stands out against its peers, including Ambarella AMBA, Broadcom AVGO and GlobalFoundries GFS. Over the past year, Ambarella and Broadcom's shares have declined 20.9% and 1.9%, respectively, while GlobalFoundries has appreciated 35.6%. This relative strength highlights the market's favorable view of Amkor Technology's AI and advanced-packaging opportunity compared with several semiconductor peers.

One-Year AMKR Stock Price Performance

From a valuation standpoint, AMKR appears attractively priced, trading at a trailing 12-month price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 1.47X, significantly below the industry average of 13.6X. AMKR has a Zacks Value Score of A, compared with F for Ambarella and Broadcom and C for GlobalFoundries, indicating a more favorable valuation profile.

AMKR's Valuation (P/S TTM)

Investment Thesis: Balancing Growth and Risks

Amkor Technology's strong position in outsourced semiconductor packaging and testing, supported by strategic partnerships with TSMC and NVIDIA, strengthens its long-term prospects. Accelerating AI computing demand, automotive semiconductor growth and improving product mix support its earnings outlook. Liquidity of $3.6 billion provides financial flexibility. However, Communications weakness, memory supply constraints and manufacturing transitions present near-term challenges. Substantial capital expenditures and debt obligations could pressure cash flows, while competition from established packaging providers and semiconductor manufacturers remains intense. Despite attractive valuation and expanding advanced-packaging opportunities, sustained profitability will depend on successful capacity ramp-ups, cost management and customer demand.

Conclusion: Hold AMKR Stock Ahead of Q3 Earnings

Amkor Technology offers promising growth opportunities from AI infrastructure, advanced packaging and automotive semiconductor demand, supported by improving margins and strategic partnerships. Its attractive valuation strengthens the investment case.

Nevertheless, Communications weakness, manufacturing transition risks and elevated capital spending warrant caution.

Given these competing factors, holding AMKR stock appears prudent ahead of third-quarter earnings. Existing investors may retain their positions, while prospective investors could await greater clarity on operating performance, cash generation and management's outlook before initiating new positions.

news.Title: Can Strong Momentum in LoRa Boost Semtech's Long-Term Growth?
news.Content:
Semtech Corporation SMTC is seeing strong growth in its LoRa business as demand increases across industrial, commercial and consumer applications. LoRa-enabled net sales reached a record $58 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 31% sequentially and 58% year over year. Growth reflects wider adoption of LoRa across different applications, including smart homes, security systems and industrial monitoring. Management expects the business to maintain its momentum, with LoRa revenues projected to grow about 15% sequentially and 65% year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

Semtech is expanding its LoRa portfolio to address more applications. Its LoRa Gen 4 platform supports higher data speeds while maintaining low power consumption and long-range connectivity. These features can support new uses in smart homes, security and industrial applications. For example, LoRa-enabled sensors can help monitor industrial equipment and support predictive maintenance. In public safety, the technology can also enable sensors to transmit audio for AI-based verification instead of sending simple alerts.

Amazon Sidewalk is another potential growth driver for Semtech's LoRa business. Following Ring's launch of a new range of LoRa-based sensors in the United States, Amazon Sidewalk is expanding internationally, starting with Canada and Mexico, while Europe, Australia and Japan are expected to follow. This expansion could help increase the use of LoRa-based devices in consumer applications through Amazon's network. Meanwhile, LoRa Plus is gaining traction in smart home and security markets, broadening the company's opportunities beyond traditional industrial and commercial use cases.

Strong momentum in LoRaWAN, LoRa Plus and Amazon Sidewalk can also support SMTC's future growth. Management expects LoRa revenues to grow at a rate above its previous 20% benchmark, supported by demand across these applications. With record revenues, new use cases and expanding distribution through Amazon Sidewalk, LoRa could become an increasingly important contributor to Semtech's overall growth.

How Competitors Fare Against SMTC

Semtech faces competition from Texas Instruments TXN and NXP Semiconductors NXPI across the broader industrial and Internet of Things (IoT) markets.

Texas Instruments offers Sub-1 GHz wireless microcontrollers and transceivers designed for applications such as smart meters, building automation and industrial sensors. These products provide long-range connectivity while using little power, making them an alternative for certain applications served by Semtech's LoRa technology. In the third quarter of 2026, TXN's revenues rose 28% year over year to $6.1 billion, while industrial revenues grew more than 40%. The company is expanding manufacturing capacity to support rising customer demand. These investments and its broad wireless product portfolio strengthen TXN's position in industrial and connected-device markets.

Story Continues

NXPI also offers low-power Sub-GHz wireless products for smart metering, home and building automation, asset tracking and industrial monitoring. Its OL2385 transceiver family supports multiple wireless protocols, including Sigfox and Wireless M-Bus, giving customers options for connected-device applications. NXPI's industrial and IoT business reported revenues of $755 million in the second quarter of 2026, up 38% year over year. Its newer processing products, including the i.MX, RT and MCX families, grew 40% year over year, reflecting strong demand for its industrial and IoT portfolio.

news.Title: TXN Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Analog, Data Center Demand
news.Content:
Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $2.62 per share, which increased 77% year over year. The bottom line beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 9.2%.

TXN posted revenues of $6.06 billion, which rose 28% from the year-ago quarter. The top line surpassed the consensus mark by 2.2%, driven by broad-based growth across industrial, automotive and data center markets. Data center revenues surged approximately 95% year over year.

TXN's Segment Mix Reflects Broad-Based Growth

Texas Instruments' third-quarter results reflected strong growth across its Analog and Embedded Processing segments, supported by improving demand conditions across key end markets.

Analog revenues came in at $4.91 billion (81.1% of total revenues), which grew 32% from the year-ago quarter. The figure came above our model estimate of $4.79 billion. The segment's operating profit increased 69% year over year to $2.51 billion, benefiting from stronger demand and improving manufacturing utilization.

Texas Instruments Incorporated Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Texas Instruments Incorporated price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Texas Instruments Incorporated Quote

Embedded Processing revenues totaled $858 million (14.2% of total revenues), reflecting 21% year-over-year growth. The figure surpassed our model estimate of $823.1 million. The segment's operating profit surged 110% to $227 million, supported by improving profitability as the business continued its cyclical recovery.

The Other segment generated $286 million in revenues (4.7% of total revenues), declining 6% from the prior-year quarter. The figure missed our model estimate of $293.9 million. The segment's operating profit increased 106% to $142 million.

Texas Instruments Benefits From End-Market Momentum

Industrial revenues increased more than 40% year over year and approximately 10% sequentially, supported by demand across aerospace and defense, energy infrastructure, test and measurement, and robotics.

Automotive revenues grew at a mid-teens percentage rate year over year and approximately 10% sequentially. Management highlighted improving customer demand, particularly in China and the United States, alongside increasing semiconductor content in hybrid electric and powertrain systems.

Data center revenues increased approximately 20% sequentially, reflecting sustained investments in computing infrastructure. Personal electronics revenues remained approximately flat year over year but increased at an upper-single-digit rate sequentially. Communications equipment revenues grew both year over year and sequentially.

Story Continues

TXN's Margins Expand on Higher Revenues

Texas Instruments' gross profit increased 42.7% year over year to $3.89 billion. Gross margin expanded approximately 680 basis points (bps) year over year to 64.2%, benefiting primarily from higher revenues, alongside favorable pricing, manufacturing loadings and product mix.

Selling, general and administrative expenses increased 4.2% year over year to $476 million. As a percentage of revenues, SG&A expenses contracted approximately 180 bps to 7.9%.

Research and development expenses increased 2.3% year over year to $530 million. As a percentage of revenues, R&D expenses declined approximately 220 bps to 8.8%.

Operating profit surged 72.8% year over year to $2.87 billion. Operating margin expanded approximately 1,240 bps to 47.5%.

Texas Instruments Strengthens Its Manufacturing Position

Texas Instruments continued expanding manufacturing capacity to support rising semiconductor demand. Management highlighted its investments in 300mm wafer manufacturing and assembly and test operations as key competitive advantages.

The company is ramping manufacturing operations in Malaysia while expanding capacity at its Lehi facilities. Management also highlighted improving Analog pricing during the second half of 2026, supported by stronger demand and tighter industry supply conditions.

Capital expenditure plans for 2026 remain between $2 billion and $3 billion, with spending potentially approaching the higher end depending on equipment delivery schedules.

TXN's Cash Generation Supports Shareholder Returns

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash and short-term investments totaled $8.14 billion. Long-term debt stood at $12.91 billion, while the current portion of long-term debt was $650 million.

Texas Instruments generated operating cash flow of $3.42 billion during the quarter, while capital expenditures totaled $463 million. Quarterly free cash flow reached $2.96 billion.

During the quarter, TXN repurchased shares worth $48 million and paid $1.30 billion in dividends. The company also repaid $500 million in debt.

Trailing 12-month free cash flow increased 249% year over year to $8.42 billion. Management announced a 7% dividend increase to $1.52 per share, marking its 23rd consecutive annual dividend increase.

Texas Instruments Provides Q4 2026 Guidance

Management expects fourth-quarter 2026 revenues between $5.80 billion and $6.30 billion, with a midpoint of $6.05 billion.

Texas Instruments anticipates earnings per share between $2.45 and $2.79. The company expects an effective tax rate of approximately 13% for the fourth quarter and 13-14% for 2027.

Management expects industrial, automotive and data center demand to support fourth-quarter performance. Continued strength in data center infrastructure investments and industrial recovery underpins the company's outlook, while manufacturing capacity expansion remains a key operational priority.

Zacks Rank and Other Stocks to Consider

Currently, TXN carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

Some other top-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector are Analog Devices ADI , Applied Materials AMAT and Cisco Systems CSCO , each carrying a Zacks Rank #2 at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Shares of Analog Devices have rallied 49.7% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ADI's fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $13 per share, up by 4 cents over the past seven days, indicating an increase of 66.9% year over year.

Shares of Applied Materials have jumped 59.1% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AMAT's fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $12.79 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating a rise of 35.8% year over year.

Cisco Systems shares have surged 39.2% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CSCO's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $5.11 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating an increase of 18% year over year.

China's technology footprint in the United States enters the final quarter of 2026 on steadier, if still choppy, footing. GCT, Taiwan Semiconductor TSM and KE Holdings BEKE for impressive returns heading into 2027.

Sector-by-Sector Progress

In semiconductors, October data from IDC showed Nvidia's share of China's data-center AI-chip market slipping to 34% in the first half of 2026, while Huawei climbed to 28% after shipping 572,000 accelerators, per Reuters. Even so, ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent reportedly ordered more than three million Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 cards worth about $35 billion, per an Oct. 20 report, though supply limits may cap fulfillment. Expect licensed access and domestic substitution to advance together into 2027.

In electric vehicles, BYD sold 463,561 vehicles in September, its best month of 2026, as overseas shipments jumped about 154% to nearly 180,000 units, offsetting a 13% domestic decline. With overseas sales targeted above 2.5 million units in 2027 and a Hungary plant due online this quarter, exports should remain the primary growth engine.

In artificial intelligence (AI), DeepSeek launched V4.1-Flash and a faster update on Oct. 17, while Beijing proposed export curbs on 23 AI technologies, exempting open-source releases. The new bilateral AI-safety channel should temper friction into 2027.

In humanoid robots, Unitree unveiled its H2-X as MIIT projected full-year output topping 100,000 units, while UBTech opened a Liuzhou plant with capacity exceeding 10,000 robots annually, supporting volume growth into 2027.

In aerospace, COMAC delivered a C919 to China Southern, yet only 11 were delivered this year through September. With U.S. jet-engine licenses and a Boeing order now bargaining chips ahead of APEC, deliveries should keep climbing gradually.

In computerized machines and defense, CNC machine tool output rose 13.5% and industrial robots 29.1% in the first three quarters. Beijing widened export controls on drones, critical components, dredger parts and tunnel boring machines, effective Nov. 18, signaling that dual-use curbs will persist into 2027.

In medical devices, Chinese imports still face the 12.5% Section 301 forced-labor duty, while Washington's Section 232 device probe remained undecided in September, keeping import substitution in focus into 2027.

In maritime and rail equipment, more than 200 trade groups urged USTR on Sept. 23 to extend the Section 301 vessel-fee suspension expiring Nov. 9, while the CR450 train, designed for 400 km/h service, nears commercial rollout.

In new synthetic materials and advanced electrical equipment, energy-storage battery sales surged 104.4% to 73.5 GWh in September, and new storage installations rose 42%, while draft curbs on perovskite and tandem solar technology underscore continued localization into early 2027.

Taken together, September and October developments reinforce a China technology landscape marked by managed stability, selective friction and steady momentum across strategic sectors, keeping Chinese tech stocks well positioned into 2027.

news.Title: Monolithic Power (MPWR) Reports Next Week: Wall Street Expects Earnings Growth
news.Content:
Monolithic Power (MPWR) is expected to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price.

The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 29. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This chipmaker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $7.80 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +64.9%.

Revenues are expected to be $1.16 billion, up 57.5% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 4.33% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Monolithic?

For Monolithic, the Most Accurate Estimate is higher than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of +1.35%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.

So, this combination indicates that Monolithic will most likely beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Monolithic would post earnings of $5.88 per share when it actually produced earnings of $6.50, delivering a surprise of +10.54%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Monolithic appears a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

Expected Results of an Industry Player

Another stock from the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry, NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), is soon expected to post earnings of $4.14 per share for the quarter ended September 2026. This estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +33.1%. Revenues for the quarter are expected to be $3.77 billion, up 18.8% from the year-ago quarter.

The consensus EPS estimate for NXP has been revised 0.5% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. However, a lower Most Accurate Estimate has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.27%.

When combined with a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy), this Earnings ESP makes it difficult to conclusively predict that NXP will beat the consensus EPS estimate. Over the last four quarters, the company surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times.
